Of this Jeremias spoke: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus]], [[Lam 4:20|to whom we said: Under thy shadow we shall live among the Gentiles|cui diximus, In umbra tua vivemus inter gentes]]. Without this shadow we cannot live in grace. This shadow, then, the Church desires; nay, still more she desires the bridegroom himself, and the clear, face-to-face sight of him: and since for the meantime she is far from him and set apart by unlikeness, she longs to contemplate him in faith through the gift of wisdom, and to be defended by his loving-kindness from the assaults of all enemies, visible and invisible, to be guarded by the help of the angels, and to be aided by the sacraments of the Church and the watchful care of prelates. Nor is she cheated of her hope, as is added next.

paras.t: Et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo : id est, refectio sua, qua modo me alit per divinorum infusionem charismatum, per spem et contemplationem futurorum bonorum, per sacra eloquia, per sacramentorum edulia, per quotidianum profectum ac aliis modis, est mihi valde suavis : ita quod æquanimiter dilationem gloriosæ præsentiæ suæ sustineo : sicut testatur Propheta, Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua ! Et iterum, Dulciora (inquit) super mel et favum. Hinc alibi sponsus loquitur : Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum ; sed fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Et rursus : Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos. Hinc quoque in Actibus Apostolorum narratur de primitiva Ecclesia : Sumebant cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis. Præterea, quam copiose et delicate reficiatur a sponso, subinfert :
paras.en: [[2:3|and his fruit was sweet to my palate|Et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo]]: that is, his refreshment, by which he now feeds me through the pouring in of divine gifts, through hope and the contemplation of the good things to come, through the sacred words, through the food of the sacraments, through daily progress and in other ways, is very sweet to me: so that I bear with an even mind the delay of his glorious presence; as the Prophet witnesses, [[Ps 118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua]]! And again, [[Ps 18:11|sweeter|Dulciora]] (he says) [[Ps 18:11|than honey and the honeycomb|super mel et favum]]. Hence elsewhere the bridegroom says: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum]]; but it [[John 4:14|shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]. And again: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you.|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]] Hence too in the Acts of the Apostles it is told of the primitive Church: [[Acts 2:46|they took their meat with gladness and simplicity of heart|Sumebant cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis]]. Further, how abundantly and delicately she is refreshed by the bridegroom, she adds next:

paras.t: Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam, id est in spiritualium alimentorum exuberantiam, in sacram Scripturam, et in veram ac spiritualem ejus intelligentiam, quæ sobrie inebriat mentem, in sacram communionem, qua sub speciebus panis et vini ipsemet sponsus vere incomprehensibiliterque accipitur. Introduxit me quoque in cœlestis patriæ deliciosissimam mansionem, dando mihi aliquantulam tantæ gloriæ prælibationem, et certam ipsius spem atque notitiam amorosam ac refectivam. Specialissime vero introducta fuit primitiva Ecclesia in cellam vinariam, quando in die sacro Pentecostes in cœnaculo illo, in quo Christus Cœnam suam celebravit novissimam, Spiritum Sanctum accepit in igneis linguis : et tanta illius plenitudine fuit potata, quod sponsum suum cum omni fiducia evangelizare incepit, in tanto fervore, quod increduli irridendo dixerunt : Musto pleni sunt isti.
paras.en: The king [[2:4|brought me into the cellar of wine|Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam]] [Denis's text adds "the king", as at 1:3, "The king hath brought me into his storerooms"; the Vulgate here has only "He brought me"], that is, into an abundance of spiritual nourishment: into sacred Scripture and its true and spiritual understanding, which soberly inebriates the mind; into holy communion, in which, under the species of bread and wine, the bridegroom himself is truly and incomprehensibly received. [[2:4|He brought me|Introduxit me]] also into the most delightful mansion of the heavenly country, giving me some small foretaste of so great a glory, and a sure hope of it, and a loving and refreshing knowledge of it. But most especially was the primitive Church brought [[2:4|into the cellar of wine|in cellam vinariam]] when, on the holy day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:1||]], in that upper room in which Christ celebrated his Last Supper[[Luke 22:12||]], she received the Holy Ghost in fiery tongues[[Acts 2:4||]]: and she was given to drink of such fullness of him that she began to preach her bridegroom with all confidence, in such fervour that the unbelievers said in mockery: [[Acts 2:13|These men are full of new wine|Musto pleni sunt isti]].

paras.t: Ordinavit in me caritatem, id est, præordinavit ab æterno diligere me per eximios ac præcipuos caritatis effectus, sicut jam mihi multipliciter demonstravit, personaliterque testatus est : Majorem, inquiens, caritatem nemo habet, ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis ; et denuo, Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos. Imo et ipse prior dilexit me. Ordinavit quoque in me caritatem, id est, præcepit mihi ut quidquid ego fecero, toleravero, habuero, ponam sub ordine divini amoris, id est, ad caritatem Dei tanquam ad summam virtutem ordinem semper ac referam ; nec aliquid agam, nisi sit ordinabile ad Deitatis amorem, id est, nisi sit tale, quod per ipsum queam in caritate proficere. Iterum, Ordinavit in me caritatem, id est, non solum præstitit mihi ipsum habitum caritatis, sed et per gratiam specialem mihi donavit ordinatum usum seu actum caritatis : ut scilicet id prius ac maxime diligam, quod primo et maxime est amandum, videlicet ipsum Deum, deinde creata sub ipso ordine congruente : quia et ordo caritatis cadit sub præcepto, ut homo in primis summe et incomparabiliter toto corde diligat Deum, deinde se ipsum, tertio loco parentes, deinceps propriam sobolem, quinto domesticos et propinquos ac benefactores : qui omnes nomine proximi designantur, sub quo etiam nomine, Beati in patria intelliguntur, imo et in purgatorio existentes.
paras.en: [[2:4|he set in order charity in me|Ordinavit in me caritatem]]: that is, he foreordained from eternity to love me with excellent and special effects of charity, as he has already shown me in many ways, and has witnessed in his own person: [[John 15:13|Greater|Majorem]], he says, [[John 15:13|love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends|caritatem nemo habet, ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis]]; and again, [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]. Nay, he himself [[1 John 4:10|hath first loved|prior dilexit]] me. [[2:4|he set in order|Ordinavit]] also [[2:4|charity in me|in me caritatem]]: that is, he commanded me that whatever I shall do, suffer or have, I should put under the order of divine love; that is, that I should always order and refer it to the charity of God as to the highest virtue, and do nothing unless it can be ordered to the love of the Godhead, that is, unless it is such that by it I may advance in charity. Again, [[2:4|he set in order charity in me|Ordinavit in me caritatem]]: that is, he not only bestowed on me the very habit of charity [habitus: the abiding disposition of the virtue, as distinct from its acts], but by a special grace also gave me the ordered use or act of charity: namely, that I should love first and most that which is first and most to be loved, God himself, and then created things beneath him in fitting order. For the order of charity too falls under precept: that a man should first love God supremely and beyond compare with his whole heart, then himself, in the third place his parents, next his own offspring, fifth his household, his kinsfolk and his benefactors; all of whom are signified by the name of neighbour, under which name are understood also the Blessed in the fatherland, and indeed those who are in purgatory.

paras.t: Circa hoc loquitur Origenes : Omnes homines amant aliquid, et nullus est qui ad id ætatis venerit ut possit amare, et non aliquid amet : sed hic amor seu caritas, in aliquibus suo ordine congruenter procedit ; in plurimis vero contra ordinem, dum scilicet aliquid diligit, quod non debet, aut quod debet diligit, sed plus aut minus justo. In illis vero, quos valde paucos arbitror esse, qui scilicet per viam vitæ incedunt, et non declinant ad dexteram aut sinistram, in ipsis solis ordinata est caritas. Est autem mensura et ordo caritatis, ut in dilectione Dei nullus modus, nulla mensura sit, nisi hæc sola, ut totum exhibeas quantum habes. In dilectione autem proximi, aliqua est mensura. Diliges, inquit, proximum tuum sicut te ipsum. Si ergo in dilectione Dei minus aliquid feceris quam potes, aut certe inter te et proximum non servaveris æquitatem ; non est in te caritas ordinata, nec ordinem suum tenens. Nam si, ut ait Apostolus, sumus alterutrum membra, hunc affectum erga proximum habere debemus, ut eos non quasi aliena corpora, sed ut membra nostra diligamus. Secundum hoc ergo, quod membra invicem sumus, æqualem erga omnes dilectionem habere debemus ; secundum hoc vero, quod sunt in corpore aliqua membra honorabiliora et honestiora, alia vero inhonestiora et inferiora, pro membrorum meritis et honore librari debet modus dilectionis. Unde magis est diligendus, qui in via salutis nos instruit, et a peccati præcipitio ad lucem revocat veritatis, sicut ait Apostolus : Abundantius habeatis in caritate eos qui in Dei verbo laborant. Similiter qui gratiam instruendi non habet, sed tamen innocentis et justæ est conversationis, magis amandus est eo qui impie conversatur. Et hanc materiam prolixe et pulchre declarat atque prosequitur Origenes.
paras.en: On this Origen says: All men love something, and there is no one who has come to an age at which he can love, and does not love something. But this love or charity proceeds in some fittingly, in its due order; but in most against order, that is, when one loves something he ought not, or loves what he ought, but more or less than is just. But in those, whom I judge to be very few, who walk the way of life and turn not aside to the right hand or to the left, in them alone is charity set in order. Now the measure and order of charity is this: that in the love of God there be no limit and no measure save this alone, that thou give the whole of what thou hast. But in the love of the neighbour there is some measure: [[Matt 22:39|Thou shalt love|Diliges]], he says, [[Matt 22:39|thy neighbour as thyself|proximum tuum sicut te ipsum]]. If then in the love of God thou dost something less than thou canst, or at least dost not keep equity between thyself and thy neighbour, charity in thee is not set in order, nor does it keep its due order. For if, as the Apostle says, we are [[Rom 12:5|members one of another|alterutrum membra]], we ought to have this affection towards our neighbours, to love them not as other men's bodies but as our own members. According to this, then, that we are members one of another, we ought to have equal love towards all; but according to this, that in the body some members are more honourable and comely, and others less comely and lower, the measure of love ought to be weighed by the merits and honour of the members. Hence he is more to be loved who instructs us in the way of salvation, and calls us back from the precipice of sin to the light of truth; as the Apostle says: [[1 Thess 5:13|That you esteem them more abundantly in charity|Abundantius habeatis in caritate eos]] who labour in the word of God [Denis's wording is freer than the Vulgate's, and joins 1 Thess 5:12–13]. Likewise, he who has not the grace of teaching, but yet is of innocent and just conversation, is more to be loved than he who lives impiously. And Origen sets out and pursues this matter at length and beautifully.

paras.t: Insuper Antisiodorensis in tertia parte suæ Summæ inquirit : Quis ordo observandus est in dilectione? Ad quod respondet : Ambrosius dicit : Primo debemus diligere Deum ; secundo, nos ipsos ; tertio, parentes ; quarto, filios ; quinto, domesticos ; sexto, extraneos, qui si boni sunt, præponendi sunt filiis atque domesticis malis ; septimo et ultimo, inimicos. Et dicimus, quod nullus est diligendus, nisi quia bonus, vel ut sit bonus ; et qui magis est bonus, magis est diligendus, ceteris circumstantiis paribus. Etenim quem scimus meliorem, debemus magis diligere, id est majus bonum ei velle ; non tamen oportet ut diligamus eum magis, id est majori affectu. Nam tribus modis dicitur aliquid plus amari : primo, ad majus præmium sive ad gratiam ampliorem ; secundo, majori affectu ; tertio, quoad majorem exhibitionem exteriorem. Hæc Antisiodorensis : qui loco præallegato alia multa de hac materia scribit. De qua etiam Thomas in secunda secundæ per plures quæstiones scribit plenissime.
paras.en: Further, William of Auxerre [Denis calls him Antisiodorensis, "the man of Auxerre"; his Summa is the Summa aurea], in the third part of his Summa, asks: What order is to be kept in love? To which he answers: Ambrose says: First we ought to love God; second, ourselves; third, our parents; fourth, our children; fifth, our household; sixth, strangers, who, if they are good, are to be preferred to children and household who are wicked; seventh and last, our enemies. And we say that no one is to be loved except because he is good, or that he may be good; and he who is more good is more to be loved, other circumstances being equal. For him whom we know to be better we ought to love more, that is, to will him a greater good; yet it is not needful that we love him more, that is, with greater affection. For a thing is said to be loved more in three ways: first, with regard to a greater reward or a more ample grace; second, with greater affection; third, with regard to a greater outward showing. So far William of Auxerre, who in the place cited writes many other things on this matter. Of it Thomas too writes most fully, over several questions, in the Secunda Secundæ [the second part of the second part of his Summa theologiae; the order of charity is its q. 26].

paras.t: Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo. Universalis Ecclesia ex persona perfectorum, qui ex caritatis vehementia languent, hæc ait ad sponsi sodales, paranymphos, amicos, videlicet angelos sanctos, sive prælatos, et contemplativos ac prædicatores. Quemadmodum autem sponsa carnalis præ desiderio sponsi languescens et afflicta de illius absentia, floribus recreatur et pomis, suavi odore ac dulci sapore; ita Ecclesia perfectorum ex ferventissimæ dilectionis impetu sauciata, eo quod cupitis ac incessabilibus sui superpulcherrimi ac supernobilissimi sponsi amplexibus nequeat in vita hac frui, profert hæc verba. Quamvis enim amor faciat in dilecto lætari; tamen ob dilecti absentiam, facit tristari atque affligi : et cruciatus hujusmodi nominatur hic languor. Denique, sicut carnalis amor prædominans, qui amor ἔρως appellatur, corpori infirmitatem inducit (quia ad amorem talem consequitur transmutatio corporalis excessiva discrucians, et inquietudo imaginationis, ex quibus fit homo ad refectionem somnumque impotens); sic spiritualis amor perfectus ecstaticus parit redundantiam grandem in corpus partemque sensitivam, quia appetitus superior movet, immutat, et post se trahit appetitum inferiorem, quemadmodum sphæra cœlestis superior inferiorem : ex qua redundantia, sicut ex prænominata, fit indispositio corporalis naturæ, et alteratio harmoniæ immoderata ac innaturalis, ut præcipue patet in raptu, ad quem gravis concomitatur afflictio, præcipue in reditu ad se. Unde in Daniele legitur : Langui (inquit) post visionem. Ezechiel quoque ait : Vidi; et cecidi in faciem meam. Et Isaias : Corrui, quum audirem ; conturbatus sum, quum viderem ; emarcuit cor meum.
paras.en: [[2:5|Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love.|Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo]] The universal Church, in the person of the perfect, who languish from the vehemence of charity, says this to the bridegroom's companions, his paranymphs [the bridegroom's friends, who led the bride to him], his friends: that is, to the holy angels, or to prelates, contemplatives and preachers. For as a bride according to the flesh, languishing with desire for her bridegroom and afflicted by his absence, is revived with flowers and apples, with their sweet odour and sweet taste; so the Church of the perfect, wounded by the onset of most fervent love, because she cannot in this life enjoy the longed-for and unceasing embraces of her bridegroom, surpassingly fair and surpassingly noble, utters these words. For though love makes one rejoice in the beloved, yet because of the beloved's absence it makes one sad and afflicted; and torment of this kind is here called languor. Lastly, as carnal love, when it prevails (the love that is called ἔρως [eros]), brings infirmity upon the body (for upon such love there follows an excessive and tormenting change in the body, and a restlessness of the imagination, from which a man becomes unable to take food and sleep); so perfect, ecstatic spiritual love produces a great overflow into the body and the sensitive part, because the higher appetite moves, changes and draws after it the lower appetite, as the higher heavenly sphere draws the lower. And from this overflow, as from the one named before, there arises an indisposition of the bodily nature, and an immoderate and unnatural alteration of its harmony; as appears especially in rapture, which is accompanied by grievous affliction, especially on returning to oneself. Hence in Daniel we read: I [[Dan 8:27|languished|Langui]] (he says) after the vision. Ezechiel too says: [[Ezech 44:4|I saw|Vidi]]; [[Ezech 44:4|and I fell on my face|et cecidi in faciem meam]]. And Isaias: [[Is 21:3|I fell down at the hearing of it, I was troubled at the seeing of it|Corrui, quum audirem ; conturbatus sum, quum viderem]]; [[Is 21:4|My heart failed|emarcuit cor meum]].

paras.t: Taliter ergo spirituali ac sincerissimo languens amore Ecclesia, dicit ac deprecatur : Fulcite me floribus, id est, replete et expolite me contemplationibus sponsi mei consolatoriis, claris ac dulcibus; stipate me malis, id est, circumdate et valate me internis refectionibus ex prælibatione futuræ salutis : quatenus totaliter recreata, vires resumam, et gloriæ dilatationem, beatificique adspectus sponsi absentiam æquanimius feram. Insuper, Fulcite me floribus, id est reformationibus membrorum ac filiorum meorum, ut videam eos per gratiam reflorere, quos vidi in peccatis marcescere; stipate me malis, id est quotidianis profectibus, quibus tanquam odoriferis saporosisque pomis reficiar (malum quippe nunc pro pomo accipitur arboris mali) : sicque ex intuitu profectus mei et conversionis ac reformationis filiorum meorum, hujus incolatum exsilii sustineam patienter. Nam et Apostolus dixit : Permanere autem in carne, necessarium propter vos.
paras.en: Languishing, then, with such spiritual and most pure love, the Church speaks and prays: [[2:5|Stay me up with flowers|Fulcite me floribus]], that is, fill and adorn me with the consoling, clear and sweet contemplations of my bridegroom; [[2:5|compass me about with apples|stipate me malis]], that is, surround and fence me about with inward refreshments from the foretaste of the salvation to come: so that, wholly restored, I may take up my strength again, and bear with a more even mind the delay of glory and the absence of the beatific sight of my bridegroom. Further, [[2:5|Stay me up with flowers|Fulcite me floribus]], that is, with the reforming of my members and children, that I may see them flower again by grace whom I saw withering in sins; [[2:5|compass me about with apples|stipate me malis]], that is, with daily progress, by which I may be refreshed as with fragrant and savoury fruits (for malum is here taken for the fruit of the apple tree): and so, from the sight of my own progress and of the conversion and reformation of my children, I may patiently bear my sojourn in this exile. For the Apostle too said: [[Phil 1:24|But to abide still in the flesh is needful for you|Permanere autem in carne, necessarium propter vos]].

paras.t: Denique audiens sponsus piam hanc Ecclesiæ querimoniam atque petitionem, misertus ejusdem, statim subvenit, et consolatus est eam, prout ipsa fatetur, subdendo : Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me. Per lævam seu sinistram sponsi, significatur gratiosa consolatio, ac præsentia ejus per fidem et dona spiritualia in hac vita, per virtutes infusas, per sacramenta et prægustationem futuræ beatitudinis : per quæ omnia sponsus consolatur, sustentat, confortat Ecclesiam, sicut oravit Apostolus : Deus spei vos repleat omni gaudio in credendo, ut abundetis in virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti. Hanc lævam tenet sponsus sub capite sponsæ, id est sub ratione et mente ipsius, illuminando, exhilarando, roborando eam per ista. Juxta hunc modum Psalmista loquitur de electo : Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam. Porro per dexteram sponsi insinuatur gloriosa manifestatio ejus per speciem, qua Ecclesiam militantem finito vitæ hujus curriculo totaliter rapit in se, jucundissime amplexatur, et triumphantis Ecclesiæ societati eam innectit : sicut sponsus promisit Ecclesiæ, Ego, inquiens, dispono vobis regnum : et rursus : Pater, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem quam dedisti mihi. Itemque : Vado vobis parare locum : et iterum veniam, et assumam vos ad me ipsum : et gaudebit cor vestrum, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis.
paras.en: Then the bridegroom, hearing this devout complaint and petition of the Church, has pity on her, comes at once to her help, and consoles her, as she herself confesses, adding: [[2:6|His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.|Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me]] By the left hand of the bridegroom is signified his gracious consolation, and his presence through faith and spiritual gifts in this life, through the infused virtues, through the sacraments and the foretaste of the beatitude to come: by all of which the bridegroom consoles, sustains and strengthens the Church; as the Apostle prayed: [[Rom 15:13|the God of hope fill you with all joy|Deus spei vos repleat omni gaudio]] [[Rom 15:13|in believing: that you may abound|in credendo, ut abundetis]] in the power and grace of the Holy Ghost [Denis's text differs here from the Vulgate, which has "with all joy and peace in believing: that you may abound in hope and in the power of the Holy Ghost"]. This left hand the bridegroom holds under the head of the bride, that is, under her reason and mind, enlightening, gladdening and strengthening her by these things. In this way the Psalmist speaks of the elect: [[Ps 36:24|When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, for the Lord putteth his hand under him.|Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam]] But by the right hand of the bridegroom is meant his glorious manifestation by sight, by which, when the course of this life is ended, he catches up the Church militant wholly into himself, embraces her most joyfully, and joins her to the fellowship of the Church triumphant: as the bridegroom promised the Church: [[Luke 22:29|I|Ego]], he says, [[Luke 22:29|dispose to you|dispono vobis]] [[Luke 22:29|a kingdom|regnum]]; and again: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also|Pater, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi]] [[John 17:24|may be with me: that they may see my glory which thou hast given me|sint mecum, ut videant claritatem quam dedisti mihi]]. And again: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado vobis parare locum]]: [[John 14:3|I will come again and will take you to myself|et iterum veniam, et assumam vos ad me ipsum]]: [[John 16:22|and your heart shall rejoice. And your joy no man shall take from you|et gaudebit cor vestrum, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis]].

paras.t: Præterea pius amorosusque sponsus conspiciens Ecclesiam caritate tam languidam, atque ex sua consolatione paululum repausantem, pro ea non inquietanda sollicitus est, sicut subjungitur in ejus persona : Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, id est, o ecclesiasticæ personæ seu animæ adhuc fragiles et proclives ad culpas, per capreas cervosque camporum, id est per vestros primos prælatos, sanctos Apostolos et apostolicos viros, seu per Prophetas et Patriarchas : qui omnes per capreas designantur ac cervos, quoniam interioris visus acumine vigent, et virtutum montana contemplationisque alta conscendunt, in quibus pascua animarum suarum requirunt, quemadmodum capreæ cernunt valde acute, et pascendo scandunt ad montes; ac instar cervorum agiles sunt ad actus virtutum, et juvant se invicem; et sicut desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum, ita ad fontem adspirant ac sitiunt vitæ æternæ.
paras.en: Furthermore, the loving and tender Bridegroom, seeing the Church so languishing with charity and resting a little in her consolation, is anxious that she be not disturbed, as is added in his person: [[2:7|I adjure you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, O persons of the Church, or souls still frail and prone to faults, [[2:7|by the roes, and the harts of the field|per capreas cervosque camporum]], that is, by your first prelates, the holy Apostles and apostolic men, or by the Prophets and Patriarchs: all of whom are signified by roes and harts, because they are strong in the keenness of inward sight, and climb the mountains of the virtues and the heights of contemplation, in which they seek the pastures of their souls, just as roes see very keenly and climb up to the mountains as they graze; and like harts they are nimble in acts of virtue, and help one another; and [[Ps 41:2|As the hart panteth after the fountains of water|sicut desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum]], so they aspire to and thirst for the fountain of eternal life.

paras.t: Quemadmodum autem jurare Deo non competit, proprie loquendo, nisi per semetipsum, sicut ad Hebræos docet Apostolus, ita non competit ei proprie adjurare, nisi per se. Idcirco per cervos capreasque adjurat, in quantum aliquid divinæ perfectionis et auctoritatis in ipsis relucet. Amplius, propter proprietates quasdam irrationabilium animalium, solent homines per talia designari, prout in libro Geneseos Jacob sanctus dixisse narratur : Catulus leonis, Juda; Nephthali, cervus emissus; Issachar, asinus fortis; fiat Dan coluber in via, cerastes in semita; Benjamin, lupus rapax. Sicque Isaias, de Achaz et Ezechia loquens : De radice, inquit, colubri egredietur regulus, et semen ejus absorbens volucrem.
paras.en: Now just as it does not befit God, properly speaking, to swear except by himself, as the Apostle teaches in the Epistle to the Hebrews[[Heb 6:13||]], so it does not properly befit him to adjure except by himself. He adjures by harts and roes, therefore, inasmuch as something of the divine perfection and authority shines forth in them. Moreover, because of certain properties of the irrational animals, men are commonly signified by such creatures, as holy Jacob is related in the book of Genesis to have said: [[Gen 49:9|Juda is a lion's whelp|Catulus leonis, Juda]]; [[Gen 49:21|Nephthali, a hart let loose|Nephthali, cervus emissus]]; [[Gen 49:14|Issachar shall be a strong ass|Issachar, asinus fortis]]; [[Gen 49:17|Let Dan be a snake in the way, a serpent in the path|fiat Dan coluber in via, cerastes in semita]]; [[Gen 49:27|Benjamin a ravenous wolf|Benjamin, lupus rapax]]. And so Isaias, speaking of Achaz and Ezechias: [[Is 14:29|Out of the root|De radice]], he says, [[Is 14:29|of the serpent shall come forth a basilisk, and his seed shall swallow the bird|colubri egredietur regulus, et semen ejus absorbens volucrem]].

paras.t: Itaque, Adjuro vos, id est, per jurationem prohibeo, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, id est, ne sponsam meam Ecclesiam, utpote perfectiores et superiores in ea, inquietetis, perturbetis, seu a tranquillitate suæ contemplationis et recollectionis in Deo impediatis aut abstrahatis, implicando eam exterioribus curis, mundanis negotiis, activæ occupationibus vitæ; et ne inter vos sitis contentiosi, aut alio modo graviter offendatis, propter quod ipsa cogatur interrumpere suæ contemplationis quietem, et circa vestram pacificationem, correctionem, refrenationem sollicitari ac distrahi; quoadusque ipsa velit, id est, quousque ipsa rationabiliter et sponte consentiat suscitari ac taliter occupari, videlicet tempore opportuno : quia interdum vult ipsa propter commune bonum forinsecus evocari, et opera pastoralis exercere officii, dum præcepto aut legitima electione, seu rationabili ad hoc compellitur causa. Nam et Apostolus scripsit : Judicia si habetis inter vos, contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, illos constituite ad judicandum; et rursus, Non quæro quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis.
paras.en: So then, [[2:7|I adjure you|Adjuro vos]], that is, I forbid you under oath, [[2:7|that you stir not up, nor make the beloved to awake|ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam]]: that is, that you do not disquiet or disturb my bride the Church (namely those in her who are more perfect and set over others), nor hinder her or draw her away from the tranquillity of her contemplation and recollection in God by entangling her in outward cares, worldly business and the occupations of the active life; and that you be not contentious among yourselves, or give grave offence in some other way, so that she is forced to break off the quiet of her contemplation and be troubled and distracted with making peace among you, correcting you and restraining you; [[2:7|till she please|quoadusque ipsa velit]], that is, until she reasonably and freely consents to be roused and occupied in this way, namely at a fitting time: for at times she is willing to be called out of doors for the common good, and to perform the works of the pastoral office, when she is compelled to it by a command or a lawful election, or by some reasonable cause. For the Apostle too wrote: If [[1 Cor 6:4|you have judgments|Judicia si habetis]] among you, [[1 Cor 6:4|set them to judge who are the most despised in the church|contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, illos constituite ad judicandum]]; and again, [[1 Cor 10:33|not seeking that which is profitable to myself but to many|Non quæro quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis]].

paras.t: Circa hæc scribit Anselmus : Virtutes quas inhianter desiderare debetis, sine quibus nemo potest ad vitam pervenire æternam, in capreis ac cervis naturaliter considerantur. Caprea namque acumine oculorum suorum herbas sibi utiles a nocivis discernit, eligit, comedit, et in suum trajicit ventrem. Pascendo quoque tendit ad montium altiora. Quod si fuerit sauciata, herbam quamdam dictamnum nomine quærit, et ejus tactu ferro expulso cum ipsa putredine, recuperat sanitatem. Sic sancti viri acumine sui ingenii, ope Spiritus Sancti salubres sententias a falsis discernunt et amplectuntur; atque se ipsos ac alios spiritualiter nutriendo, ad sublimitatem virtutum altitudinemque regni cœlestis toto conatu festinant. Si autem sagitta diaboli fuerint vulnerati, Christum tanquam dictamnum requirunt, et per pœnitentiam curari nituntur. Porro cervi has virtutes naturaliter habere dicuntur, quod tempore sui amoris optima pascua inquirentes, regionem suam relinquunt, alienam introeunt : et hoc, noctu, quia in die videri et capi verentur. Quod si magna aqua eis occurrerit transvadanda, sese vicarie devehunt : ita ut primus ac fortior, super clunes suas portet caput sequentis, secundus itidem caput tertii, et ita usque ad ultimum; ultimus autem qui portatur nec portat, succedit in locum prioris, qui portat et non portatur : sicque dictante naturali amore, alter juvatur ab altero, quousque, quo pergunt, perveniant. Similiter sancti viri amore Christi ferventes, dum vitæ pascua quærunt, et per mare sæculi hujus transire habent, caritative juvant se mutuo, quousque ad concupitam cœlestis patriæ deveniant mansionem. Insuper fertur, quod si cervi obstacula quædam in via reperiant, quando a canibus insectantur, transiliunt ea, aut reflexis cornibus frangunt; sicque a canum morsibus se tuentur. Sic sancti viri per fidem et operationem, seu per duo caritatis præcepta, a dæmonum insectatione se muniunt. Legitur etiam, quod cervus caligantibus sibi præ senio oculis, manducat serpentem : quo æstuans, currit ad fontem; et eo potatus, vomit venenum, recuperat visum, ac superflua quæque deponens, quodammodo reviviscit. Sic electi, si forte ex tentatione diaboli, per consensum aut effectum illicitum in se serpentem receperint infernalem, ad fontem pietatis divinæ per pœnitentiam currunt, in quo, a suis loti inquinamentis, illustrantur ac reviviscunt.
paras.en: On this Anselm writes: The virtues which you ought to desire eagerly, without which no one can come to eternal life, are seen by nature in roes and harts. For the roe, by the keenness of its eyes, tells the grasses that are good for it from the harmful ones, chooses them, eats them and takes them down into its belly. As it grazes, too, it makes for the heights of the mountains. And if it has been wounded, it seeks a certain herb called dittany, and at its touch the iron is driven out together with the festering, and it recovers its health. So holy men, by the keenness of their minds, with the help of the Holy Ghost, tell wholesome teachings from false ones and embrace them; and nourishing themselves and others spiritually, they hasten with all their strength to the sublimity of the virtues and the height of the heavenly kingdom. And if they have been wounded by the devil's arrow, they seek Christ as their dittany, and strive to be healed by penance. Harts, again, are said to have these virtues by nature, in that at the time of their mating, seeking the best pastures, they leave their own country and go into another; and this by night, because they fear to be seen and caught by day. And if they meet a great water that has to be forded, they carry one another in turn: the first and strongest bears on his haunches the head of the one following, the second likewise the head of the third, and so on to the last; and the last, who is carried and does not carry, takes the place of the first, who carries and is not carried; and so, at the prompting of natural love, one is helped by another until they reach the place they are making for. In the same way holy men, burning with the love of Christ, while they seek the pastures of life and have to cross the sea of this world, help one another in charity until they arrive at the longed-for dwelling of the heavenly fatherland. It is said besides that if harts, when they are chased by hounds, find obstacles in the way, they leap over them or break them with their horns thrown back, and so protect themselves from the hounds' teeth. So holy men, by faith and works, or by the two precepts of charity, defend themselves against the pursuit of the demons. We read also that the hart, when its eyes grow dim with age, eats a serpent; burning with it, it runs to a spring, and when it has drunk from it, it vomits the poison, recovers its sight, and, putting off everything superfluous, in a manner comes to life again. So the elect, if perhaps through the devil's temptation, by consent or by unlawful deed, they have taken the serpent of hell into themselves, run by penance to the spring of the divine mercy, in which, washed from their defilements, they are enlightened and come to life again.

paras.t: Præterea dicuntur capreæ et cervi camporum, quoniam sancti Apostoli et apostolici viri, per spatia orbis terrarum ad evangelizandum undique cucurrerunt, et in locis diversis quasi in campis magna habuerunt certamina, omnique virtute ac meritis tanquam camporum floribus se ornarunt; atque ab hominibus aliquando secedentes, in secretis et solitariis locis quasi in campis Deo vacantes, ibi meditabantur et hauriebant a Domino, quod postea sermocinati sunt populo.
paras.en: Further, they are called [[2:7|the roes, and the harts of the field|capreæ et cervi camporum]] because the holy Apostles and apostolic men ran everywhere through the expanses of the world to preach the Gospel, and in diverse places, as in fields, had great contests, and adorned themselves with every virtue and merit as with the flowers of the fields; and at times withdrawing from men, giving themselves to God in secret and solitary places as in fields, they meditated there and drew from the Lord what they afterwards preached to the people.

paras.t: Præterea præinductam sponsi adjurationem zelo sponsæ ad subditos inferioresque factam, sponsa cognovit et valde gratanter accepit. Unde subjungitur : Vox dilecti mei. Quasi dicat Ecclesia : Adjuratio illa a sponso processit, qui in tantum me diligit, tamque libenter in meis amplexibus, in contemplationis lectulo requiescit, quod prohibuit me suscitari quousque egomet vellem.
paras.en: Furthermore, the bride recognized the Bridegroom's adjuration given above, made out of zeal for the bride to her subjects and those beneath her, and received it very gratefully. Hence it is added: [[2:8|The voice of my beloved|Vox dilecti mei]]. As if the Church were saying: That adjuration came from the Bridegroom, who loves me so much, and rests so gladly in my embraces, on the little bed of contemplation, that he forbade me to be roused until I myself should wish it.

paras.t: Et quasi quæreretur a sponsa, Ubi est dilectus tuus? qualiter venit ad te? et ubi eum poterimus reperire? respondet : Ecce iste venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles : id est, per Incarnationis mysterium venit in mundum a summo cœlo egrediens, de cœlis descendens, in ordinibus angelorum velocissime operans, per carnis propagationem a Patriarchis prosiliens. Venit quoque in montibus saliens, id est perfectissimas virtutum actiones exercens, præclarissima miracula copiosissime faciens, incomprehensibilia mysteria implens : quia divinam naturam cum humana in unitate personæ conjunxit, de Virgine natus est, inter homines vixit, qui Deus est et conditor angelorum : sicque transiliit colles, quia a Prophetarum oraculis usque ad Apostolos se deduxit, omniumque virtutes atque prodigia sua omnipotentia ac perfectione transcendit : sed et superbos Judæorum pontifices, Scribas ac Pharisæos ac seniores in suis dignitatibus, scientiis et officiis gloriantes relinquendo transiliit, et ad Ecclesiam ex gentilitate electam descendit. Denique saliens venit, quia de sinu Patris venit in uterum Virginis, de utero Virginis in præsepe, de præsepio in templum; deinde vectus est in Ægyptum, ac inde relatus, inter homines est conversatus; post hæc ascendit in crucem, inde descendit in monumentum atque in limbum, inde resurgens apparuit suis discipulis; tandem coram ipsis scandit in cœlum, rediitque ad Patrem, a cujus sinu, corde et intellectu invariabilis ac immensus nunquam recessit.
paras.en: And as though the bride were asked, Where is thy beloved? how does he come to thee? and where shall we be able to find him? she answers: [[2:8|behold he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills|Ecce iste venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles]]: that is, through the mystery of the Incarnation he came into the world, going forth from the highest heaven[[Ps 18:7||]], coming down from the heavens, working most swiftly among the orders of the angels, springing from the Patriarchs through the propagation of the flesh. [[2:8|He cometh|Venit]] also [[2:8|leaping upon the mountains|in montibus saliens]], that is, performing the most perfect acts of the virtues, working most glorious miracles in great abundance, accomplishing incomprehensible mysteries: for he joined the divine nature with the human in unity of person, was born of a Virgin, and lived among men, he who is God and the maker of the angels. And so he skipped over the hills, because he brought himself down from the oracles of the Prophets to the Apostles, and surpassed the virtues and wonders of them all by his omnipotence and perfection; and he also skipped over the proud high priests of the Jews, the Scribes and Pharisees and elders, who gloried in their dignities, learning and offices, by leaving them behind, and came down to the Church chosen from the Gentiles. Lastly, he [[2:8|cometh leaping|saliens venit]], because from the bosom of the Father he came into the womb of the Virgin, from the womb of the Virgin into the manger, from the manger into the temple; then he was carried into Egypt, and brought back from there, and lived among men; after this he went up on the cross, from there went down into the tomb and into limbo, and from there, rising again, appeared to his disciples; at last, before their eyes, he went up into heaven and returned to the Father, from whose bosom, heart and understanding he, unchangeable and immense, never departed.

paras.t: Consequenter sponsa exponit, qualiter suo dilecto conveniat salire in montibus, collesque transilire. Similis est dilectus meus caprea hinnuloque cervorum. Hinnulus est filius cervi ac cervæ. De proprietatibus autem capreæ ac cervi, jam dictum est. Christus itaque capreæ comparatur, quia et ipse præ cunctis acutissimo viget intuitu oculi intellectualis; et sicut caprea visu suo clarissimo herbam sibi utilem a nociva discernit, sic Christus justos discernit et separat ab iniquis. Et sicut caprea in locis montanis magnos saltus exercet atque celeriter currit; sic juxta expositionem jam introductam, Christus venit saliens in montibus, et transiliens colles. Unde assimilatur et hinnulo velocissime cursitanti ac salienti, et montium juga petenti, ac commoranti in arduis : qui et secundum carnem ex Patriarchis est natus. Patriarchæ autem et sancti viri, sicut jam patuit, cervi vocantur. Velocitas demum capreæ, secundo volumine Regum insinuatur, quo legitur : Asael frater Joab velocissimus cursor fuit, quasi unus ex capreis. Sed et propter teneritudinem suæ complexionis, Christus hinnulus nuncupatur.
paras.en: Next the bride explains how it befits her beloved to leap upon the mountains and skip over the hills. [[2:9|My beloved is like a roe, or a young hart|Similis est dilectus meus caprea hinnuloque cervorum]]. A *hinnulus* [the word rendered 'young hart'] is the young of a hart and a hind. Of the properties of the roe and the hart we have already spoken. Christ, then, is compared to a roe because he too, above all others, is strong in the keenest gaze of the eye of the understanding; and as the roe by its very clear sight tells the grass that is good for it from the harmful, so Christ discerns the just and separates them from the wicked. And as the roe makes great leaps in mountainous places and runs swiftly, so, according to the explanation already given, Christ [[2:8|cometh leaping upon the mountains|venit saliens in montibus]], and [[2:8|skipping over the hills|transiliens colles]]. Hence he is likened also to a young hart, which runs about and leaps very swiftly, seeks the ridges of the mountains and lingers on the heights; and he was also born, according to the flesh, of the Patriarchs. And the Patriarchs and holy men, as has already been shown, are called harts. Lastly, the swiftness of the roe is shown in the second book of Kings, where we read: Asael, the brother of Joab, [[2 Kings 2:18|was a most swift runner, like one of the roes|velocissimus cursor fuit, quasi unus ex capreis]]. And Christ is also called a young hart because of the tenderness of his constitution.

paras.t: En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, id est, multum approximavit nobis, ita quod inter ipsum et nos non videtur mediare nisi paries noster, id est nostræ mortalitatis conditio, qua ab ejus claro impedimur intuitu, et a beatifico visu : quia dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino, et corpus hoc corruptibile aggravat animam. Stat quoque post parietem nostrum, id est caliginosum interstitium, quod inter statum viatorum Beatorumque mediat : quoniam ignorantia atque obscuritas nostræ cognitionis dividit inter ipsum et nos. Item stat post parietem nostrum, quoniam concupiscentiæ et opera carnis passionesque sensitivæ partis impediunt nos ab ipso : quibus sublatis seu reformatis, mox ad nos plene ac splendide introibit. Stat demum post parietem nostrum, id est, in nostra humanitate, quam assumpsit, nobis apparet, et tamen in ea nobis suam deitatem celavit. Respiciens per fenestras, id est per assumpti corporis sensus, et per documenta atque miracula, per quæ tanquam per fenestras nos illustrare dignatus est; vel, Per fenestras, id est per sanctos Apostolos, et alios prædicatores pastoresque sanctos, per quos discutit, investigat ac edocet subditos ; prospiciens per cancellos, id est per secretas inspirationes, per arduas vias internæ exercitationis, allocutionesque abditas, juxta illud Job : Quasi furtive suscepit auris mea venas susurrii ejus. Prospicit quoque per fenestras, id est per directiones præceptorum, et per cancellos, id est per suggestiones evangelicorum consiliorum. Postremo fenestræ et cancelli, per quos inspicit sponsam, sunt præparationes ac desideria cordis, quibus se ad sponsi susceptionem disponit, et ingressui ejus se aperit.
paras.en: [[2:9|Behold he standeth behind our wall|En ipse stat post parietem nostrum]]: that is, he has come very near to us, so that between him and us nothing seems to stand but [[2:9|our wall|paries noster]], that is, the condition of our mortality, by which we are kept from the clear sight of him and from the beatific vision: for [[2 Cor 5:6|while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord|dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino]], and [[Wis 9:15|the corruptible body is a load upon the soul|corpus hoc corruptibile aggravat animam]]. [[2:9|He standeth|Stat]] also [[2:9|behind our wall|post parietem nostrum]], that is, the dark partition that stands between the state of wayfarers and that of the Blessed: since the ignorance and obscurity of our knowledge divide him from us. Again, [[2:9|he standeth behind our wall|stat post parietem nostrum]], since the concupiscences and works of the flesh and the passions of the sensitive part keep us from him: and when these are taken away or reformed, he will soon come in to us fully and in splendour. [[2:9|He standeth|Stat]], lastly, [[2:9|behind our wall|post parietem nostrum]], that is, he appears to us in our humanity, which he assumed, and yet in it he hid his Godhead from us. [[2:9|Looking through the windows|Respiciens per fenestras]], that is, through the senses of the body he assumed, and through the teachings and miracles by which, as through windows, he deigned to enlighten us; or, [[2:9|through the windows|Per fenestras]], that is, through the holy Apostles and the other holy preachers and pastors, through whom he examines, searches out and instructs his subjects; [[2:9|looking through the lattices|prospiciens per cancellos]], that is, through secret inspirations, through the steep ways of inward exercise, and hidden addresses, according to that saying of Job: [[Job 4:12|my ears by stealth, as it were, received the veins of its whisper|Quasi furtive suscepit auris mea venas susurrii ejus]]. He looks also [[2:9|through the windows|per fenestras]], that is, through the directions of the precepts, and [[2:9|through the lattices|per cancellos]], that is, through the promptings of the evangelical counsels. Finally, the windows and lattices through which he looks in upon the bride are the preparations and desires of the heart, by which she disposes herself to receive the Bridegroom and opens herself to his coming in.

paras.t: En dilectus meus loquitur mihi : Surge, id est, de quiete et actu contemplationis ad exercitia vitæ activæ procede, et de secreto ad publicum, propera per caritatis fervorem et obedientiæ promptitudinem, hoc ipsum festinanter implendo, o amica mea per mutuam caritatis affectionem, columba mea, quæ ornaris virtutibus, per proprietates columbæ significatis, utpote verecunda, simplex, mansueta, non fellea nec invidiosa, formosa mea, id est, plena decore virtutum, donorum ac meritorum ; et veni, jam repetitis vicibus invitata, et tam multis amorosis expressa nominibus, ex quibus merito caritas tua ad me magis accenditur.
paras.en: [[2:10|Behold my beloved speaketh to me|En dilectus meus loquitur mihi]]: [[2:10|Arise|Surge]], that is, go forth from the quiet and the act of contemplation to the exercises of the active life, and from privacy into public; [[2:10|make haste|propera]] by the fervour of charity and the readiness of obedience, carrying this out speedily, O [[2:10|my love|amica mea]] [*amica*, 'friend'], by the mutual affection of charity, [[2:10|my dove|columba mea]], who art adorned with the virtues signified by the properties of the dove, being modest, simple, gentle, without gall or envy; [[2:10|my beautiful one|formosa mea]], that is, full of the beauty of virtues, gifts and merits; [[2:10|and come|et veni]], invited now again and again, and addressed by so many loving names, by which thy charity towards me is rightly kindled the more.

paras.t: Jam enim hiems transiit : id est, tempus infidelitatis, seu rigidæ observationis legis, finem accepit; imber, id est abundantia tribulationis, abiit et recessit. De quo imbre in Evangelio legitur : Descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam ; et cecidit, et fuit ruina ejus magna.
paras.en: [[2:11|For winter is now past|Jam enim hiems transiit]]: that is, the time of unbelief, or of the rigid observance of the Law, has come to an end; [[2:11|the rain|imber]], that is, the abundance of tribulation, [[2:11|is over and gone|abiit et recessit]]. Of this rain we read in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:27|the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the fall thereof|Descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam ; et cecidit, et fuit ruina ejus magna]].

paras.t: Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra : id est, bonæ dispositiones et inchoationes ad actus virtutum in hominibus inveniuntur : sicut Salvator dixit Apostolis, Videte regiones, quia jam albæ sunt ad messem. In flore enim spes atque initium fructus inveniuntur. Tempus putationis advenit : id est, inchoatum nunc est tempus ab æterno præordinatum conversioni gentilium, in quo ipsæ gentes incredulæ et iniquæ sunt spiritualiter circumcidendæ, amputando ab eis passiones et vitia, omnemque perfidiam, sicut a vinea abscinduntur sarmenta sterilia. Vox turturis audita est in terra nostra : id est, electa pars plebis gentilis, desiderium veræ salutis ac conversionis cœpit habere, cœpitque se ad gratiam præparare, præventa pie a Domino, vel ex angelica inspiratione, aut ex fama et aliqua auditione legis Mosaicæ. Nam et ipso Christo in terris evangelizante, multi gentilium confluxerunt ad eum ex Decapoli et Syria, Tyro, Sidone, et aliis locis : ut ex Evangelio probatur. Atque ex Actibus patet Apostolorum, quod eunuchus potens Candacis reginæ, venit in Jerusalem adorare, legitque Isaiam prophetam.
paras.en: [[2:12|The flowers have appeared in our land|Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra]]: that is, good dispositions and beginnings of acts of virtue are found in men; as the Saviour said to the Apostles: [[John 4:35|see the countries. For they are white already to harvest|Videte regiones, quia jam albæ sunt ad messem]]. For in the flower are found the hope and the beginning of the fruit. [[2:12|The time of pruning is come|Tempus putationis advenit]]: that is, the time foreordained from eternity for the conversion of the Gentiles has now begun, in which the unbelieving and wicked nations themselves are to be spiritually circumcised, by cutting away from them their passions and vices and all faithlessness, as barren shoots are cut from a vine. [[2:12|The voice of the turtle is heard in our land|Vox turturis audita est in terra nostra]] [the turtle is the turtledove]: that is, a chosen part of the Gentile people began to have the desire of true salvation and conversion, and began to prepare itself for grace, being lovingly forestalled by the Lord, whether through an angel's inspiration, or through report and some hearing of the Law of Moses. For even while Christ himself was preaching the Gospel on earth, many of the Gentiles flocked to him from Decapolis and Syria, Tyre, Sidon and other places[[Matt 4:25||]][[Mark 3:8||]], as is shown from the Gospel. And it is clear from the Acts of the Apostles that the eunuch of great authority under Candace the queen came to Jerusalem to adore[[Acts 8:27||]], and was reading Isaias the prophet[[Acts 8:28||]].

paras.t: Ficus protulit grossos suos : id est, Synagoga (quæ fuit aliquando arbor fici fecunda) jam protulit sensus suos carnales, quibus litteram sequitur occidentem, observantiamque legalem in cæremonialibus : in quibus ponit spem suam, magis quam in fide et gratia Salvatoris; et putat per talia mihi placere sine interiori sinceritate ac devotione, quum talia nunquam placuerint mihi ex parte operis operati, sed operis operantis. Ficus ergo accipitur hic pro arbore fici; et grossi fici, proprie nuncupantur fructus immaturi, ineptique esui. Vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum: id est, electæ congregationes ex Judaismo, conversæ seu convertendæ, et credituræ aut credentes in me, per virtuosæ suæ conversationis dulcedinem me attraxerunt ad exaudiendum preces earum, ut per earum ministerium ac doctrinam incipiam gentiles convertere.
paras.en: [[2:13|The fig tree hath put forth her green figs|Ficus protulit grossos suos]]: that is, the Synagogue (which was once a fruitful fig tree) has now put forth her carnal senses, by which she follows the letter that killeth[[2 Cor 3:6||]], and the legal observance in ceremonial things, in which she places her hope rather than in faith and the grace of the Saviour; and she thinks to please me by such things without inward sincerity and devotion, though such things never pleased me by the work done [*opus operatum*: the rite as performed], but by the work of the one doing it [*opus operantis*: the faith and devotion of the one who performs it]. *Ficus*, then, is taken here for the fig tree; and *grossi* of the fig are properly the name for fruit that is unripe and unfit to eat [the Douay-Rheims renders them 'green figs']. [[2:13|The vines in flower yield their sweet smell|Vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum]]: that is, the chosen congregations from Judaism, converted or to be converted, believing or about to believe in me, have drawn me by the sweetness of their virtuous life to hear their prayers, so that through their ministry and teaching I may begin to convert the Gentiles.

paras.t: Hoc totum est, quod in Actibus Apostolorum asserit Paulus: Tempora prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat omnibus hominibus, ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant. Juxta quem modum ait Psalmista ad Dominum: Tu exsurgens misereberis Sion, quia tempus miserendi ejus, quia venit tempus. Unde rursus testatur Apostolus: Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum: itemque, Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. Hinc in Actibus princeps apostolici chori fatetur: Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps annuntiaverunt dies istos.
paras.en: All this is what Paul asserts in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 17:30|God indeed having winked at the times of this ignorance, now declareth unto men that all should every where do penance|Tempora prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat omnibus hominibus, ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant]]. In the same way the Psalmist says to the Lord: [[Ps 101:14|Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come|Tu exsurgens misereberis Sion, quia tempus miserendi ejus, quia venit tempus]]. Hence again the Apostle testifies: [[Gal 4:4|when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son|Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum]]; and likewise, [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]]. Hence in the Acts the prince of the apostolic choir declares: [[Acts 3:24|all the prophets, from Samuel and afterwards|Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps]] [[Acts 3:24|have told of these days|annuntiaverunt dies istos]].

paras.t: Itaque per prædicta videtur Christus primitivam Ecclesiam ad convertendum gentilitatem, atque ad laborandum pro proximorum salute per vitiorum amputationem et virtutum insertionem. Unde adhuc admonetur: Surge, amica mea, sponsa mea, et veni ad exsequendum actus præfatos: et per hanc tam frequentem ejusdem exhortationis reiterationem insinuare videtur, quod primitiva Ecclesia ex Judæis collecta, erat multum difficilis ad relinquendum Synagogam, ut gentilibus prædicaret. Nam multis annis post Christi ascensionem manserunt Apostoli in Judæa; et quum princeps Apostolorum convertit Cornelium centurionem ac suos, disceptabant adversus eum quidam ex Judæis conversi, dicentes : Quare introisti ad viros præputium habentes? Paulus quoque et Barnabas, ut constat in Actibus, diu hinc inde pergebant, prædicantes solis Judæis. Hinc sponsus tam amorose, blande, dulciter et frequenter primitivam Ecclesiam ad gentium conversionem exhortans, ait:
paras.en: So by all this Christ is seen [the Latin has no verb here; something like 'to call' is understood] to call the primitive Church to convert the Gentiles, and to labour for the salvation of her neighbours by cutting away vices and planting virtues. Hence she is admonished yet again: [[2:13|Arise, my love|Surge, amica mea]], my spouse [Denis reads *sponsa mea*, 'my spouse', where the Vulgate has *speciosa mea*, 'my beautiful one'], [[2:13|and come|et veni]], to carry out the acts already mentioned. And by this so frequent repetition of the same exhortation he seems to hint that the primitive Church, gathered from the Jews, was very hard to move to leave the Synagogue in order to preach to the Gentiles. For the Apostles remained in Judea for many years after Christ's ascension; and when the prince of the Apostles converted Cornelius the centurion and his household, some of the converted Jews disputed against him, saying: [[Acts 11:3|Why didst thou go in to men uncircumcised|Quare introisti ad viros præputium habentes]]? Paul and Barnabas too, as is plain in the Acts, went to and fro for a long time preaching to the Jews alone[[Acts 13:5||]][[Acts 13:14||]][[Acts 14:1||]] [the margin gives Acts xiii, 5, 14 and following; xiv, 1 and following, etc.]. Hence the Bridegroom, exhorting the primitive Church so lovingly, tenderly, sweetly and often to the conversion of the Gentiles, says:

paras.t: Columba mea per puram et simplicem intentionem, in foraminibus petræ, id est habitans in firmissimis munimentis fidei et virtutum, et in profundo humilitatis, in caverna maceriæ, id est in abscondito protectionis divinæ, quæ est ipsis credentibus murus ac paries contra adversarios suæ salutis. Denique per foramina petræ, valde convenienter intelliguntur vulnera Salvatoris, de quo sanctus ait Apostolus: Petra autem erat Christus. Et ipsemet Dominus: Super hanc petram, id est super me ipsum, quem tu, o Petre, confessus es, ædificabo Ecclesiam meam. Per cavernam demum maceriæ, aptissime designatur vulnus dominici lateris. In quibus vulneribus ac caverna sponsa moratur, dum dominicam passionem devote, compassive, ac sapientialiter meditatur, ejusque meritis ac virtuti innitur, ac fructum vulnerum horum sacratissimorum perpendens, in eis suam figit fiduciam, in eis omnem suam adversitatem dulcorat, in contemplatione eorum patientiam discit, et universam sponsi passionem cordi suo inscribit: quod assidue faciendo fit sponso carissima.
paras.en: [[2:14|My dove|Columba mea]], through pure and simple intention, [[2:14|in the clefts of the rock|in foraminibus petræ]], that is, dwelling in the strongest defences of faith and the virtues, and in the depth of humility, [[2:14|in the hollow places of the wall|in caverna maceriæ]], that is, in the hiding place of the divine protection, which is to believers a wall and rampart against the enemies of their salvation. Again, by [[2:14|the clefts of the rock|foramina petræ]] are very fittingly understood the wounds of the Saviour, of whom the holy Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:4|the rock was Christ|Petra autem erat Christus]]. And the Lord himself: [[Matt 16:18|upon this rock|Super hanc petram]], that is, upon myself, whom thou, O Peter, hast confessed, [[Matt 16:18|I will build my church|ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]. By [[2:14|the hollow places of the wall|cavernam demum maceriæ]], lastly, is most aptly signified the wound of the Lord's side. In these wounds and in this hollow the bride dwells while she meditates on the Lord's passion devoutly, with compassion and with wisdom, and leans on its merits and power; and weighing the fruit of these most sacred wounds, she fixes her trust in them, sweetens all her adversity in them, learns patience in contemplating them, and writes the whole passion of the Bridegroom upon her heart: and by doing this continually she becomes most dear to the Bridegroom.

paras.t: Ostende mihi faciem tuam: id est, stude ac satage te ipsam mihi puram et irreprehensibilem exhibere, et coram me effunde cor tuum sincere, nec in confessione sacramentali quidquam culpæ occultes. Ostende mihi faciem tuam, id est, mentem tuam converte ad me, et pura intentione coram me ambula, sicut dixi ad Abraham, Ambula coram me, et esto perfectus; et imple quod scriptum est: Tibi dixit cor meum, Exquisivit te facies mea; faciem tuam, Domine, requiram. Per promptam quoque obedientiam ostende mihi faciem tuam ; et quia te diligo, faciem tuam speciosam intueri delector. Sonet vox tua in auribus meis: id est, verba mihi placentia loquere, tamque sonore, sapienter, ac dulciter evangelicam legem sermocinare, et infideles converte, ut acceptum sit mihi ; subditis quoque credentibus efficaciter prædica, imo et orationibus, psalmis, hymnis, et canticis spiritualibus tam ferventer, pure, stabiliterque insiste, ut mihi sit gratum. Vox enim tua dulcis: id est, prædicatio, oratio, psalmodia, locutio tua est virtuosa, delectabilis, et accepta. Nam et ea, quæ dicis, agis ; quæ doces, adimples ; et quidquid prædicas, ad meum spectat honorem hominumque salutem. Et facies tua decora: id est, mens tua, quæ est interior facies, per dona gratiæ, per sapientiam et virtutes est reformata ac decorata, et ad intuendum jucunda : ideo noli hanc per aliquam inobedientiam inquinare.
paras.en: [[2:14|Shew me thy face|Ostende mihi faciem tuam]]: that is, strive and take pains to present thyself to me pure and blameless, and pour out thy heart before me sincerely[[Ps 61:9||]], and hide no fault in sacramental confession. [[2:14|Shew me thy face|Ostende mihi faciem tuam]], that is, turn thy mind to me, and walk before me with a pure intention, as I said to Abraham: [[Gen 17:1|walk before me, and be perfect|Ambula coram me, et esto perfectus]]; and fulfil what is written: [[Ps 26:8|My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek|Tibi dixit cor meum, Exquisivit te facies mea; faciem tuam, Domine, requiram]]. By ready obedience also [[2:14|shew me thy face|ostende mihi faciem tuam]]; and because I love thee, I delight to look upon thy beautiful face. [[2:14|Let thy voice sound in my ears|Sonet vox tua in auribus meis]]: that is, speak words pleasing to me, and preach the law of the Gospel so resoundingly, wisely and sweetly, and convert unbelievers, that it may be acceptable to me; preach effectively also to the believers in thy charge, and indeed apply thyself to prayers, psalms, hymns and spiritual canticles so fervently, purely and steadfastly that it may be pleasing to me. [[2:14|For thy voice is sweet|Vox enim tua dulcis]]: that is, thy preaching, prayer, psalmody and speech is full of virtue, delightful and acceptable. For what thou sayest, thou doest; what thou teachest, thou fulfillest; and whatever thou preachest looks to my honour and the salvation of men. [[2:14|And thy face comely|Et facies tua decora]]: that is, thy mind, which is the inward face, has been reformed and adorned by the gifts of grace, by wisdom and the virtues, and is pleasant to behold: therefore do not defile it by any disobedience.

paras.t: Consequenter Christus committit prælatis et prædicatoribus sanctis: Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas: id est, ad meum honorem ac vestram salutem, apprehendite, convincite, reprobate, auferte hæreticos, schismaticos, falsosque fratres, et omnes animarum deceptores, simulatores ac callidos : qui particulares Ecclesias et congregationes devotas nituntur subvertere, plurimosque decipiunt, fingendo se mortuos huic mundo, et rigorosam vitam forinsecus prætendendo : quemadmodum vulpes famelica fingit se mortuam, et tanquam cadaver neglectum projicit se seorsum, eversis oculis, decidentibus pilis, extensisque pedibus, quatenus ignorantes et supersedentes sibi aves deglutiat. Hoc est quod in Evangelio loquor : Attendite vobis a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces. Nam vinea nostra floruit: id est, tota Ecclesia, quæ est una vinea generalis, totalis ac integra, omnes particulares Ecclesias seu vineas in se complectens ac continens : quæ vinea est mea, tanquam domini principalis ac redemptoris et summi pastoris ac fundatoris : et vestra, tanquam agricolarum et vicarialium prælatorum atque custodum ipsius, sicut Ezechieli locutus sum : Speculatorem te dedi domui Israel. Et Isaias fatetur : Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem. Qui rursus ait ad Synagogam, tanquam sibi suo modo commissam : Tritura mea et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino, annuntiavi vobis. Hæc, inquam, vinea crescit quotidie numero ac merito, et floret in gratia omnique decore virtutum : quod tempore Apostolorum et postea sæpius ita fuit. Ideo præcavendum, ne a vulpibus illis, quæ fingunt se humiles, et revera vilissimæ sunt, lædatur.
paras.en: Next Christ gives this charge to the prelates and holy preachers: [[2:15|Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vines|Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas]]: that is, for my honour and your salvation, seize, convict, condemn and remove heretics, schismatics and false brethren, and all deceivers of souls, pretenders and cunning men, who strive to overthrow particular churches and devout congregations, and deceive very many by feigning themselves dead to this world and making an outward show of a rigorous life; just as a hungry fox feigns itself dead and, like a neglected carcass, throws itself down apart, with eyes rolled back, hair falling out and feet stretched out, so that it may swallow the birds that, unawares, settle on it. This is what I say in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves|Attendite vobis a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]]. [[2:15|For our vineyard hath flourished|Nam vinea nostra floruit]]: that is, the whole Church, which is one vineyard, general, entire and whole, embracing and containing in itself all the particular churches or vineyards: which vineyard is mine, as its principal lord and redeemer and chief shepherd and founder; and yours, as its husbandmen and the prelates and keepers who stand in my place, as I said to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 3:17|I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel|Speculatorem te dedi domui Israel]] [the same words stand at Ezech 33:7]. And Isaias declares: [[Is 21:8|I am upon the watchtower of the Lord, standing continually by day|Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem]]. And he says again to the Synagogue, as committed in his own way to him: [[Is 21:10|O my thrashing, and the children of my floor, that which I have heard of the Lord|Tritura mea et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino]] [Denis reads *filia*, 'daughter', where the Vulgate has *filii*, 'children'], [[Is 21:10|I have declared unto you|annuntiavi vobis]]. This vineyard, I say, grows daily in number and merit, and flowers in grace and in every beauty of the virtues, as was often the case in the time of the Apostles and afterwards. Therefore care must be taken that it be not harmed by those foxes that feign themselves humble and are in truth most vile.

paras.t: Ad hanc jussionem respondet Ecclesia, videns se a sponso tam vehementer amari, ac incessanter curari ac protegi : Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi. Amorosæ locutiones solent esse truncatæ, quoniam magnitudo affectionis verba abrumpit : ut quum in Evangelio ait Salvator, videns ac defiens Jerusalem : Quia si cognovisses et tu, et quidem in hac die tua, quæ ad pacem tibi, nunc autem abscondita sunt ab oculis tuis. Quemadmodum igitur eloquens Aaron fuit os Moysis, ita in talibus ratio prudens debet supplere ac interpretari verba ferventis affectionis, et excessivi amoris. Sic ergo et nunc quum loquitur sponsa, Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi, supplendum est : Dilectus meus intentus, familiaris, fidelis, amorosus atque dulcissimus mihi est ; ego quoque pro viribus meis intenta, fidelis, affectuosa, familiaris sum illi. Ideo per prælatos et filios meos non omittam capere vulpes demolientes.
paras.en: To this command the Church replies, seeing herself so ardently loved by the Bridegroom, and unceasingly cared for and protected: [[2:16|My beloved to me, and I to him|Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi]]. Loving speech is wont to be broken off, because the greatness of the affection cuts the words short: as when in the Gospel the Saviour, seeing Jerusalem and weeping over it, says: [[Luke 19:42|If thou also hadst known, and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace: but now they are hidden from thy eyes|Quia si cognovisses et tu, et quidem in hac die tua, quæ ad pacem tibi, nunc autem abscondita sunt ab oculis tuis]]. Just as the eloquent Aaron was the mouth of Moses, then, so in such cases prudent reason must supply and interpret the words of fervent affection and excessive love. So now too, when the bride says, [[2:16|My beloved to me, and I to him|Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi]], we must supply: My beloved is attentive, intimate, faithful, loving and most sweet to me; and I too, as far as my strength allows, am attentive, faithful, affectionate and intimate to him. Therefore through my prelates and sons I will not fail to catch the foxes that destroy.

paras.t: Qui pascitur inter lilia, id est, in cordibus continentium ac pure viventium et in splendore virtutum delectatur, quiescit, et quasi nutriri se protestatur. Justus enim Dominus et justitias dilexit ; et recti habitabunt cum vultu ipsius. Qui ait per Jeremiam prophetam : Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris. Unde in Apocalypsi de talibus fertur : Hi sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit.
paras.en: [[2:16|Who feedeth among the lilies|Qui pascitur inter lilia]], that is, he delights and rests in the hearts of the continent and of those who live purely, and in the splendour of the virtues, and declares that he is, as it were, fed there. For [[Ps 10:8|the Lord is just, and hath loved justice|Justus enim Dominus et justitias dilexit]]; and [[Ps 139:14|the upright shall dwell with thy countenance|recti habitabunt cum vultu ipsius]] [Denis has 'his countenance']. It is he who says through Jeremias the prophet: If [[Jer 15:19|thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]]. Hence it is said of such in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 14:4|These follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth|Hi sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit]].

paras.t: Donec adspiret dies : id est, usque ad diem judicii, et quousque dies gloriæ æternalis adveniat, sic pascitur sponsus inter candidos viatores : quos tunc transferet ad plenissimam beatificæ fruitionis refectionem qua pascet eos ; et inclinentur umbræ : quia tunc cessabit imperfectio nostræ cognitionis, et mortale hoc induet immortalitatem, nec diutius erunt electi sedentes in tenebris et umbra mortis. Omnis autem contemplatio vitæ præsentis, respectu beatificæ visionis, umbra est, et velut caligo ac somnus.
paras.en: [[2:17|Till the day break|Donec adspiret dies]]: that is, until the day of judgment, and until the day of eternal glory comes, the Bridegroom feeds thus among the shining wayfarers, whom he will then bring over to the fullest refreshment of the beatific enjoyment, with which he will feed them; [[2:17|and the shadows retire|et inclinentur umbræ]]: for then the imperfection of our knowledge will cease, and [[1 Cor 15:54|this mortal hath put on immortality|mortale hoc induet immortalitatem]], and the elect shall no longer [[Luke 1:79|sit in darkness and in the shadow of death|sedentes in tenebris et umbra mortis]]. For all the contemplation of the present life, compared with the beatific vision, is a shadow, and as it were a darkness and a sleep.

paras.t: Revertere : similis esto, dilecte mi, etc. Hæc verba sunt sponsæ, tanquam Ecclesia in persona prælatorum ac prædicantium dicat : Tu mihi, o sponse, officium prædicationis et pastoralium exsecutionem actuum commisisti : in quibus quia parata sum tuo obedire imperio, precor ut cito digneris reverti ad me, applicando me tibi in exercitiis vitæ contemplativæ, atque in florido lectulo nostro præfato me dignanter ac dulciter amplexando. Revertaris quoque assidue ad me, per quotidianam tuæ gratiæ confortationem, ac tui gratiosi subsidii exhibitionem : ut quod mihi jussisti, digne adimpleam, quæ sine te nil agere queo. Insuper, revertere ad me, quatenus de hujus incolatu exsilii, et de tenebris umbraque mortis vitæ istius, ad diem æternitatis et splendoris, ad lumen gloriæ me transferre digneris; et in hoc, esto similis caprææ hinnuloque cervorum, implendo celeriter desiderium meum, sicut animalia ista (de quorum proprietatibus dictum est) velocissimi motus sunt, quoniam te clare ac fruitive intueri summe desidero : sicut dixit Apostolus : Infelix ego homo! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Sic quoque similis esto caprææ ac hinnulo super montes Bethel, id est in personis militantis Ecclesiæ jam perfectis : quæ cupiunt dissolvi, et aptæ sunt te protinus frui ; et recte montes dicuntur, propter eminentiam gratiæ ac virtutum suarum, et propter altitudinem dignitatis eis concessæ; quæ etiam montes Bethel vocantur, id est montes Ecclesiæ, quæ est domus Dei. Bethel equidem, domus Dei interpretatur. Vel : o dilecte, similis esto, etc., id est, tu exsistens ac habitans super montes Bethel, id est super omnes choros angelorum, qui sunt montes Bethel, id est triumphantis Ecclesiæ, quæ est summa, pulcherrima, ac perfectissima domus Dei : tu, inquam, similis esto capreæ, etc., sicut jam expositum est.
paras.en: [[2:17|Return|Revertere]]: [[2:17|be like, my beloved|similis esto, dilecte mi]], etc. These are the words of the bride, as though the Church, in the person of her prelates and preachers, were saying: Thou, O Bridegroom, hast entrusted to me the office of preaching and the carrying out of the pastoral duties; and since I am ready to obey thy command in these, I pray thee to deign to return to me soon, joining me to thyself in the exercises of the contemplative life, and graciously and sweetly embracing me on our flowery little bed of which we spoke before. Return to me also continually, by the daily strengthening of thy grace and the showing of thy gracious help, that I may worthily fulfil what thou hast bidden me, I who without thee can do nothing[[John 15:5||]]. Moreover, [[2:17|return|revertere]] to me, so as to deign to bring me over from the sojourning of this exile, and from the darkness and shadow of death of this life, to the day of eternity and splendour, to the light of glory; and in this [[2:17|be like|esto similis]] [[2:17|to a roe, or to a young hart|caprææ hinnuloque cervorum]], fulfilling my desire swiftly, as these animals (of whose properties we have spoken) are very swift of movement; for I desire above all to behold thee clearly and with enjoyment, as the Apostle said: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus?]] So too, [[2:17|be like|similis esto]] [[2:17|to a roe, or to a young hart|caprææ ac hinnulo]] [[2:17|upon the mountains of Bether|super montes Bethel]] [the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have *Bether*; Denis reads *Bethel*, which he goes on to interpret], that is, in the persons of the Church militant who are already perfect, who [[Phil 1:23|desire to be dissolved|cupiunt dissolvi]], and are fit to enjoy thee forthwith. And they are rightly called mountains, because of the eminence of their grace and virtues, and because of the height of the dignity granted them; and they are also called the mountains of Bethel, that is, the mountains of the Church, which is the house of God: for *Bethel* is interpreted 'house of God'. Or: O [[2:17|beloved|dilecte]], [[2:17|be like|similis esto]], etc., that is, thou who art and dwellest [[2:17|upon the mountains of Bether|super montes Bethel]], that is, above all the choirs of angels, who are the mountains of Bethel, that is, of the Church triumphant, which is the highest, most beautiful and most perfect house of God: thou, I say, [[2:17|be like|similis esto]] [[2:17|to a roe|capreæ]], etc., as has already been explained.

2.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM CAPITULI SECUNDI, […]
2.title_en: Exposition of the same second chapter, […]

paras.t: Loquitur sponsus cælestis ad animam amorosam: Ego flos campi. Tanquam dicat: Recte dixisti, Lectulus noster floridus, quoniam ego ipse sum flos campi, id est omnis intellectus creati devoti ac fervidi, quia in ipso tanquam in campo pulchro ac plano sto, moror, quiesco ac floreo, et ipsum adorno ac florentem efficio: et ita tu ipsa, o anima fervida, sponsa mea, es campus floridus et decorus. Et sicut campus exterior floribus, virgultis, seminibus, fructibusque ornatur; sic tu decorata es gratia virtutibusque infusis, donis, fructibus, meritis ac beatitudinibus viæ. Et quia sincera et simplex es, tortuositatibus injustitiæ, spinis ac tribulis passionum vitiorumque carens, atque per caritatis latitudinem ad omnes etiam inimicos te extendens, instar campi plana ac lata es; ideo in te tanquam in campo amœno ac grandi libenter deambulo. Iterum, sicut campus aratur, seminatur, et colitur a domino suo; sic tu præpararis ad gratiam, seminaris ac fecundaris a Spiritu Sancto. Si itaque vis ut sim flos tui ipsius, nequaquam permittas in agro cordis tui vitia pullulare, cogitationes inutiles passionumque motus manere; sed mihi reserva hunc campum, ut excolam, impinguem ac fecundificem eum, et in eo tanquam in paradiso deambulem.
