Unde dixi Judæis : Faciem cœli dijudicare nostis, signa autem temporum non potestis? Jam quoque sceptrum a Juda ablatum est, et dux de femore ejus defecit. Tempus putationis advenit, id est tempus liberationis populi Israel a suis peccatis, ut vitiorum superfluitates nunc amputentur : juxta id quod scribitur in Daniele : Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum, ut consummetur prævaricatio, et finem accipiat peccatum, et deleatur iniquitas, et adducatur justitia sempiterna, et impleatur visio et prophetia, et ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum. Unde his consonanter loquitur Paulus : Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum natum ex muliere, factum sub lege, ut eos qui sub lege erant, redimeret.
paras.en: [[2:12|The flowers have appeared in our land|Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra]]: that is, the bright and flowering signs of my coming have begun to be fulfilled, and will be fulfilled more abundantly from now on, for the time of the weeks foretold by Daniel has now come[[Dan 9:24||]]. Hence I said to the Jews: [[Matt 16:3|You know then how to discern the face of the sky|Faciem cœli dijudicare nostis]], [[Matt 16:3|and can you not know the signs of the times|signa autem temporum non potestis]]? [The margin gives Matt. xvi, 4; in the Douay-Rheims these words stand at the end of v. 3.] Now too the sceptre has been taken away from Juda, and the ruler from his thigh has failed[[Gen 49:10||]]. [[2:12|the time of pruning is come|Tempus putationis advenit]], that is, the time of the deliverance of the people of Israel from their sins, so that the overgrowth of the vices may now be cut away [*putatio*, pruning; *amputentur*, be cut away]; according to what is written in Daniel: [[Dan 9:24|Seventy weeks are shortened upon thy people|Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum]], [[Dan 9:24|that transgression may be finished, and sin may have an end, and iniquity may be abolished; and everlasting justice may be brought; and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled; and the Saint of saints may be anointed|ut consummetur prævaricatio, et finem accipiat peccatum, et deleatur iniquitas, et adducatur justitia sempiterna, et impleatur visio et prophetia, et ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum]]. In keeping with this Paul says: [[Gal 4:4|when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law|Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum natum ex muliere, factum sub lege]], [[Gal 4:5|That he might redeem them who were under the law|ut eos qui sub lege erant, redimeret]].

paras.t: Vox turturis audita est in terra nostra: id est, in Synagoga insonuit sermo legis, vaticinium Prophetarum, annuntiatio de proximo regis Messiæ adventu : instante etenim Salvatoris adventu, Omnipotens revelavit aliquibus patribus Synagogæ, tempus adventus Christi adesse. Unde Simeon justus et timoratus responsum acceperat a Spiritu Sancto, non visurum se mortem nisi videret Christum Domini. Similiter Zachariæ justo Gabriel nuntiavit de filio suo Joanne : Ipse præcedet ante illum in spiritu et virtute Eliæ.
paras.en: [[2:12|the voice of the turtle is heard in our land|Vox turturis audita est in terra nostra]]: that is, in the Synagogue there sounded the word of the law, the prophecy of the Prophets, the announcement of the near coming of the King Messias: for as the Saviour's coming drew near, the Almighty revealed to some of the fathers of the Synagogue that the time of Christ's coming was at hand. Hence Simeon, [[Luke 2:25|just and devout|justus et timoratus]], [[Luke 2:26|had received an answer from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord|responsum acceperat a Spiritu Sancto, non visurum se mortem nisi videret Christum Domini]]. In the same way Gabriel announced to the just Zachary of his son John: [[Luke 1:17|he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias|Ipse præcedet ante illum in spiritu et virtute Eliæ]].

paras.t: Ficus protulit grossos suos : id est, Synagoga fructifera et electa, quæ creditura fuit in Christum, primo observavit diligenter ea quæ legis erant. Propter quod princeps dixit Apostolorum : Nunquam comedi aliquid commune et immundum. Paulus quoque fatetur se sine querela conversatum in lege. Sed postea abjecerunt hæc tanquam fructus ineptos, cognita gratia Christi et Spiritu Sancto accepto, sicut in Actibus Archiapostolus loquitur : Per gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi credimus salvari. Vas quoque electionis disserit : Quæ mihi lucra fuerunt, hæc arbitratus sum detrimenta esse. Vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum : id est, virtuosæ personæ ipsius Synagogæ, dulciflua desideria sua de meo adventu coram me effuderunt, rogantes assidue pro adventu regis Messiæ : quarum me trahit pia affectio, et allicit devotio sancta.
paras.en: [[2:13|The fig tree hath put forth her green figs|Ficus protulit grossos suos]] [*grossi*, figs not yet ripe]: that is, the fruitful and chosen Synagogue, which was to believe in Christ, at first carefully observed the things of the law. For which reason the prince of the Apostles said: [[Acts 10:14|I never did eat any thing that is common and unclean|Nunquam comedi aliquid commune et immundum]]. Paul too confesses that he lived without blame in the law[[Phil 3:6||]]. But afterwards, once the grace of Christ was known and the Holy Ghost received, they cast these things away as unfit fruit, as the chief Apostle says in the Acts: [[Acts 15:11|by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, we believe to be saved|Per gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi credimus salvari]]. The vessel of election [that is, Paul] too declares: [[Phil 3:7|the things that were gain to me, the same I have counted loss|Quæ mihi lucra fuerunt, hæc arbitratus sum detrimenta esse]]. [[2:13|the vines in flower yield their sweet smell|Vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum]]: that is, the virtuous persons of that Synagogue poured out before me their sweetly flowing longings for my coming, praying constantly for the coming of the King Messias; their loving affection draws me, and their holy devotion entices me.

paras.t: Itaque propter hæc omnia, jam Surge, amica mea, sponsa mea singularis et optima, et veni, per mentis consensum, ut me concipias tuum creatorem et omnium salvatorem; columba mea pudicissima, summe faceta, in foraminibus petræ, id est in viribus seu potentiis animæ tuæ, in omni gratia solidatæ, constantissimæ et firmatæ, puta in intellectu ac voluntate, quæ sunt spiritualia foramina per quæ anima intellectualiter cernit me et cupit. Unde in Ezechiele Dominus ait ad Cherub qui cecidit : Foramina tua in die conditionis tuæ parata sunt. Fuit itaque sacratissima Virgo, amica, sponsa et columba Verbi æterni in foraminibus petræ, id est in intellectu ac voluntate, quia per fidem et sapientiam sui intellectus, atque per spem et caritatem suæ voluntatis, placuit sponso cœlesti potissime. Et in caverna maceriæ, id est in intellectuali memoria, per quam jugiter meditabatur divina. Nam et (teste Evangelista) Maria conservabat omnia verba hæc, conferens in corde suo. Memoria autem est receptaculum locusque specierum, et quasi venter similitudinum rerum : et ita recte vocatur caverna, imo et caverna maceriæ, id est muri sive parietis, videlicet animæ virtuosæ, quæ, juxta Ezechielem, interponit se murum inter Deum sponsum ac judicem, et inter animas peccatrices, pro quibus laborat, ut eas reconciliet Deo, et protegat a maligno. Dicitur quoque caverna maceriæ, quia latet in corpore, quod inter Deum et animam quasi medius murus est, in quantum frequenter impedit a divinis, quemadmodum S. Andreas cruci appensus, dixit : Tu, Domine, nosti, quoties a tui contemplatione me impedivit.
paras.en: Therefore, because of all these things, now [[2:13|Arise, my love|Surge, amica mea]], my singular and best bride, [[2:13|and come|et veni]], by the consent of thy mind, that thou mayest conceive me, thy creator and the saviour of all; [[2:14|My dove|columba mea]], most chaste, supremely gracious, [[2:14|in the clefts of the rock|in foraminibus petræ]], that is, in the powers or faculties of thy soul, made solid, most constant and firm in every grace, namely in the intellect and the will, which are the spiritual openings through which the soul sees me with the understanding and desires me. Hence in Ezechiel the Lord says to the Cherub who fell: [[Ezech 28:13|thy pipes were prepared in the day that thou wast created|Foramina tua in die conditionis tuæ parata sunt]] [*foramina*, the word the Douay-Rheims renders *clefts* in this verse, means "holes" or "openings"]. So the most sacred Virgin, the love, bride and dove of the eternal Word, was [[2:14|in the clefts of the rock|in foraminibus petræ]], that is, in the intellect and the will, for by the faith and wisdom of her intellect, and by the hope and charity of her will, she pleased the heavenly Bridegroom above all. And [[2:14|in the hollow places of the wall|in caverna maceriæ]], that is, in the intellectual memory, by which she meditated on divine things without ceasing. For (as the Evangelist bears witness) [[Luke 2:19|Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart|Maria conservabat omnia verba hæc, conferens in corde suo]]. Now the memory is the receptacle and place of the species [that is, the images by which things are known], and as it were the belly of the likenesses of things; and so it is rightly called a hollow, indeed a hollow of the wall, that is, of the wall or partition, namely of the virtuous soul, which, according to Ezechiel, sets itself as a wall between God, the bridegroom and judge, and sinful souls [see Ezech 13:5 and 22:30], for whom it labours to reconcile them to God and to protect them from the evil one. It is also called the hollow of the wall because it lies hidden in the body, which is as a wall in the middle between God and the soul, in so far as it often hinders it from divine things; as St Andrew said, hanging on the cross: Thou knowest, Lord, how often it [that is, the body] has hindered me from the contemplation of thee.

paras.t: Ostende mihi faciem tuam, id est obedientialem promptitudinem tuæ mentis, et cor tuum converte ad meum amplexum, ut per incarnationis mysterium celebrentur in utero tuo nuptiæ personales, id est unio naturæ humanæ cum divina in unitate personæ; et tu ipsa in nuptiis illis sponsa mea singularis efficiaris. Sonet vox tua in auribus meis, ita ut dicas, Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum; ac deinceps completo incarnationis sacro secreto, pro beneficiis tibi impensis gratias mihi referens, dicas : Magnificat anima mea Dominum, etc. Vox enim tua dulcis, quum ex plenitudine virtutum, summa caritate, ferventissima devotione, sincerissima intentione emanet : ideo tuis laudibus, tuis orationibus, tuis irreprehensibilibus verbis delector. Et facies tua decora, id est, mens tua pulcherrima est. Magnum est valde, creaturam sic commendari a superaltissimo suo opifice et infallibili creatore. Si quis ab imperitis et pueris vilibusque personis laudetur, parum appretiat; si autem a justis ac sapientibus, forsitan magni pendit : quanto magis a Creatore, qui est ipsa sanctitas ac sapientia infinita, incomparabiliter majus est commendari?
paras.en: [[2:14|shew me thy face|Ostende mihi faciem tuam]], that is, the obedient readiness of thy mind, and turn thy heart to my embrace, so that through the mystery of the incarnation a personal marriage may be celebrated in thy womb, that is, the union of the human nature with the divine in the unity of a person; and that thou thyself mayest be made my singular bride in that marriage. [[2:14|let thy voice sound in my ears|Sonet vox tua in auribus meis]], so that thou sayest, [[Luke 1:38|Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it done to me according to thy word|Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum]]; and afterwards, when the holy secret of the incarnation has been accomplished, giving me thanks for the benefits bestowed on thee, thou sayest: [[Luke 1:46|My soul doth magnify the Lord|Magnificat anima mea Dominum]], etc. [[2:14|for thy voice is sweet|Vox enim tua dulcis]], since it flows from the fulness of the virtues, from the highest charity, the most fervent devotion and the most sincere intention: therefore I delight in thy praises, thy prayers, thy blameless words. [[2:14|and thy face comely|Et facies tua decora]], that is, thy mind is most beautiful. It is a very great thing for a creature to be so commended by its most high maker and unerring creator. If someone is praised by the unskilled, by children and by low persons, he thinks little of it; but if by the just and wise, perhaps he values it greatly: how much greater beyond compare, then, is it to be commended by the Creator, who is holiness itself and infinite wisdom?

paras.t: Denique omnia ista ab illo loco, Surge, amica mea, sponsa mea, et veni, possunt exponi de Christo, qui in suæ benedictæ Matris gloriosa ascensione, ista et consimilia ad eam locutus est, ejusque faciem glorificatam voluit sibi ostendi in throno gloriæ, quo eam juxta se collocavit; ibi quoque voluit eam affari et vocem ejus audire. De talibus amorosis, ardentissimis, suavissimis, laudisonis vocibus, quibus Christus et Mater virginea se mutuo alloquuntur ac laudant cum maxima delectatione in cœlo, multa in revelationibus sanctæ Brigittæ continentur : in quibus sponsus ille cœlestis in supernorum præsentia civium fatetur et asserit, allocutiones ac laudes suæ Matris sibi acceptissimas ineffabiliterque suaves existere. Sed brevitas, cui studeo, prohibet me illa diffusius allegare.
paras.en: Lastly, all these words from the place [[2:13|Arise, my love|Surge, amica mea]], my bride, [[2:13|and come|et veni]], can be explained of Christ, who at the glorious ascension of his blessed Mother [that is, her Assumption] spoke these and like words to her, and willed that her glorified face be shown to him on the throne of glory where he set her beside himself; there too he willed to speak to her and to hear her voice. Of such loving, most ardent, most sweet words, sounding with praise, with which Christ and his virgin Mother speak to and praise each other with the greatest delight in heaven, much is contained in the revelations of St Bridget: in which that heavenly Bridegroom, in the presence of the citizens on high, confesses and declares that the words and praises of his Mother are most acceptable to him and unspeakably sweet. But the brevity I aim at forbids me to cite them at greater length.

paras.t: Capite nobis, tu, sponsa, cum tuis, vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas. Hoc Regina cœlorum, universarum electissima creaturarum, excellentissime adimplevit : quæ sola omnem hæreticam dicitur pravitatem interemisse; cujus meritis et precibus sancti viri convicerunt hæresiarchas. Parvulæ quoque vulpes sunt dæmones vitiosi ac viles, qui parvuli sunt valore, non malignitate, et tanquam parvuli invisibiliter circumquaque discurrunt; atque ob maximam suam invidiam rite parvuli nuncupantur, juxta quod scriptum est : Parvulum occidit invidia. Hinc frequenter in forma parvulorum Æthiopum, sanctis sunt viris ostensi. Et nisi sacratissima advocata ac sponsa ista auxilietur, vineas (id est Ecclesias ac animas pias) demoliuntur. Nam vinea nostra floruit, id est universalis Ecclesia, quæ communis est Christo sponso ac Matri ejus dignissimæ. Christus enim est Deus, Dominus, salvator et judex, legiferque Ecclesiæ : Virgo autem Christifera, regina, mater, et advocata Ecclesiæ prædicatur.
paras.en: [[2:15|Catch us|Capite nobis]], thou, O bride, with thine, [[2:15|the little foxes that destroy the vines|vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas]]. This the Queen of the heavens, the most chosen of all creatures, fulfilled most excellently: she who alone is said to have slain all heretical wickedness [as the Church sings of her: *cunctas hæreses sola interemisti*, "thou alone hast slain all heresies"]; by whose merits and prayers holy men have refuted the heresiarchs. The little foxes are also the demons, vicious and vile, who are little in worth, not in malice, and who run about everywhere unseen like little ones; and they are rightly called little because of their very great envy, according to what is written: [[Job 5:2|envy slayeth the little one|Parvulum occidit invidia]]. Hence they have often been shown to holy men in the form of little Ethiopians. And unless this most sacred advocate and bride gives help, they destroy the vines (that is, the churches and devout souls). [[2:15|for our vineyard hath flourished|Nam vinea nostra floruit]], that is, the universal Church, which is common to Christ the Bridegroom and to his most worthy Mother. For Christ is the God, the Lord, the saviour and judge and the lawgiver of the Church; and the Virgin is proclaimed the Christ-bearer, queen, mother and advocate of the Church.

paras.t: Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi : id est, sponsus iste omnibus Sanctis dilectus ; sed tanto specialius mihi carus, quanto præ ceteris me in matrem et sponsam singularem elegit : hic, inquam, dilectus mihi familiarissime est intentus, cohærens, innixus ; et ego similiter illi. Qui pascitur inter lilia, id est in mentibus castis ac puris.
paras.en: [[2:16|My beloved to me, and I to him|Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi]]: that is, this Bridegroom, beloved by all the Saints, but the more especially dear to me as he chose me before the rest to be his mother and singular bride: this beloved, I say, is most intimately intent upon me, clinging to me, leaning on me; and I likewise upon him. [[2:16|who feedeth among the lilies|Qui pascitur inter lilia]], that is, in chaste and pure minds.

paras.t: Revertere; similis esto, dilecte mi, capreæ hinnuloque cervorum. Hoc tenerrima et affectuosissima Virgo ac Domina dixit, Unigenito suo sibi per passionem et mortem corporaliter ad modicum tempus ablato : propter quod desolata ac prorsus mœstissima facta, atque de proxima ejus resurrectione certissima, desideravit ut post resurrectionem suam appareret mox sibi, et reverteretur ad eam : quod clementissimus Filius utique fecit; et quo suavissima Mater fuerat ei magis compassa, atque amarius desolata, eo in ista apparitione copiosius ac dulcius consolatus est eam Filius ejus. Tunc quoque et ipsa Filium exoravit, ut rediret ad suos discipulos atque discipulas, præsertim ad Magdalenam, et sua gloriosissima apparitione consolaretur gregem suum pusillum amarissime desolatum : quod et Filius adorandus tam celerrime egit, ut in hoc capreæ sit assimilatus et hinnulo.
paras.en: [[2:17|Return: be like, my beloved, to a roe, or to a young hart|Revertere; similis esto, dilecte mi, capreæ hinnuloque cervorum]]. This the most tender and most loving Virgin and Lady said when her Only-begotten had been bodily taken from her for a little time by his passion and death: for which reason, left desolate and altogether most sorrowful, yet most certain of his resurrection soon to come, she longed that after his resurrection he should appear to her at once and return to her. This the most merciful Son indeed did; and the more the most sweet Mother had suffered with him and the more bitterly she had been left desolate, the more abundantly and sweetly her Son consoled her in that appearing. Then too she besought her Son to return to his disciples, men and women, above all to Magdalen, and by his most glorious appearing to console his little flock, most bitterly desolate: which the adorable Son did so very swiftly that in this he was likened to a roe and a young hart.

3.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI TERTII : IN LECTULO MEO, ETC. ; DE SPONSO ET SPONSA GENERALI.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: In my bed, etc.; of the Bridegroom and the bride in general

paras.t: Ecclesia in fine præcedentis capituli dixit, Revertere, cupiens gratiosum ac dulcem reditum sponsi: quo tardante, ipsa fecit quod in exordio hujus capituli loquitur: In lectulo meo per noctes quæsivi quem diligit anima mea. In lectulo namque magis sentitur atque molestius toleratur sponsi absentia.
paras.en: The Church, at the end of the preceding chapter, said: [[Cant 2:17|Return|Revertere]], longing for the gracious and sweet return of the Bridegroom; and as he delayed, she did what she tells of at the opening of this chapter: [[3:1|In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth|In lectulo meo per noctes quæsivi quem diligit anima mea]]. For it is in bed that the Bridegroom's absence is more keenly felt and more grievously borne.

paras.t: In toto autem hoc libro tractatur de spirituali connubio ac divino amore, quasi sub similitudinibus carnalis conjugii ac sensualis dilectionis. Unde quidam obtenebrati, putarunt Salomonem loqui ad litteram de se ipso et conjuge ejus filia Pharaonis: quod nequaquam putandum, nec littera consonat, imo in multis inde discordat.
paras.en: Now throughout this whole book the subject is spiritual wedlock and divine love, set forth as it were under the likenesses of carnal marriage and sensual love. Hence some, whose minds were darkened, have thought that Solomon speaks literally of himself and of his wife, the daughter of Pharao: which is by no means to be thought; nor does the letter agree with it, but in many places is at odds with it.

paras.t: Itaque Ecclesia universalis in tribulationibus et persecutionibus constituta, aut solitis gratiarum affluentiis destituta, atque in pluribus deformata, testatur: In lectulo meo, id est in quiete meditationum et orationum mearum, et in exercitatione interna conscientiæ meæ, per noctes, id est, temporibus adversitatum atque in regione ac umbra mortis, et in obscuritate præsentis notitiæ, quæ est per speculum et ænigma, quæsivi sponsum quem diligit anima mea. Quamvis enim sponsus iste nunquam relinquat Ecclesiam suam in toto, nec quantum ad ea quæ sunt de necessitate salutis; aliquando tamen deseruit eam in parte, et quantum ad dulcedinis suæ experimentalem saporem, et quoad hoc, quod eam persecutionibus afflictionibusque exponit. Quæsivi illum, id est, dulcem ejus præsentiam, celerem subventionem, optavi et postulavi: et non inveni tam cito ut concupivi. Interdum namque, ut tactum est præcedenti capitulo, subtrahit se ad tempus propter causas ibi prætactas, et ut sponsæ suæ fidelitatem experiatur, et ipsa per tribulationes coronari gloriosius mereatur, suoque tempore exaudiatur perfectius: quia, ut sponsus in Evangelio loquitur, Oportet semper orare, et non deficere. Et rursus affirmat: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cælorum.
paras.en: Therefore the universal Church, set amid tribulations and persecutions, or bereft of her wonted abundance of graces, and in many respects disfigured, testifies: [[3:1|In my bed|In lectulo meo]], that is, in the quiet of my meditations and prayers and in the inward exercise of my conscience, [[3:1|by night|per noctes]], that is, in times of adversity, and in the region and shadow of death [the edition notes a variant reading here, *hac umbra*, "this shadow"], and in the obscurity of our present knowledge, which is [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum et ænigma]], [[3:1|I sought him whom my soul loveth|quæsivi sponsum quem diligit anima mea]] [Denis has "the Bridegroom" for "him"]. For although this Bridegroom never forsakes his Church wholly, nor as regards the things necessary to salvation, yet at times he has forsaken her in part: both as regards the savour of his sweetness known by experience, and in this, that he exposes her to persecutions and afflictions. [[3:1|I sought him|Quæsivi illum]], that is, I desired and begged for his sweet presence, his speedy help, [[3:1|and found him not|et non inveni]] as quickly as I longed. For at times, as was touched on in the preceding chapter, he withdraws himself for a while, for the causes mentioned there: both to try the faithfulness of his bride, and that she may merit to be crowned more gloriously through tribulations, and in his own time be heard more perfectly; for, as the Bridegroom says in the Gospel, [[Luke 18:1|we ought always to pray and not to faint|Oportet semper orare, et non deficere]]. And again he affirms: [[Matt 5:10|Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.|Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cælorum]]

paras.t: Surgam, id est, ab ista orationum et meditationum mearum quiete ad tempus cessabo, et in operibus exterioribus bonis me occupabo, et per jejunia, abstinentias, disciplinas et consimilia pœnitentiæ opera quæram dilectum: et circuibo civitatem, id est, congregationem totam fidelium undique diligenter considerabo: quod est spiritualiter circuire, et a Deo incipere, atque ad ipsum redire, sicut in motu circulari ad punctum egressionis redditur. Nempe Ecclesia tanquam pia ac sollicita mater, statum suorum considerat filiorum. Per vicos et plateas quæram quem diligit anima mea. Per vicos qui strictiores sunt, possunt religiosi intelligi, qui ultra mandata profitentur consilia, et strictiorem ambulant viam; per plateas vero, quæ latiores sunt, sæculares, qui viam mandatorum incedunt. Quæsivi illum, et non inveni eum in vicis his et plateis, quia tam in religiosis quam in sæcularibus temporis hujus, magnam deformationem et scandala, magis quam ædificationem et opem, inveni.
paras.en: [[3:2|I will rise|Surgam]], that is, I will cease for a while from this quiet of my prayers and meditations and busy myself with good outward works, and by fasts, abstinences, disciplines [that is, scourgings taken as penance] and like works of penance I will seek my beloved; [[3:2|and will go about the city|et circuibo civitatem]], that is, I will look carefully on every side at the whole congregation of the faithful: which is to go about spiritually, to begin from God and return to him, as in circular motion one comes back to the point of setting out. For the Church, as a loving and careful mother, considers the state of her children. [[3:2|in the streets and the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth|Per vicos et plateas quæram quem diligit anima mea]]. By the streets, which are narrower [Latin *vici*, lanes, against *plateæ*, wide streets], may be understood religious, who profess the counsels beyond the commandments and walk the narrower way; and by the broad ways, which are wider, seculars, who go by the way of the commandments. [[3:2|I sought him, and I found him not|Quæsivi illum, et non inveni]] in these streets and broad ways; for in the religious and the seculars alike of this time I found great disfigurement and scandals rather than edification and help.

paras.t: Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem, id est, prælati ac doctores fidelium, quorum est cum vigilantia cordis custodire ipsos fideles ab infernalibus lupis, a tentationum periculis, a laqueis vitiorum. Unde per Isaiam loquitur Dominus: Super muros tuos, Jerusalem, constitui custodes. Et Paulus hortatur: Qui præest, in sollicitudine, supple, præsit. Interdum quoque per vigiles in Scripturis intelliguntur angeli sancti, juxta illud, In sententia vigilum decretum est; itemque, Descendit sanctus vigil. Pastores igitur fidelium jugiter vigilent super creditum sibi gregem, quemadmodum uni eorum, et sub persona illius omnibus eis præcipitur: Esto vigilans, et confirma cetera quæ moritura erant. His itaque vigilibus mihi occurrentibus interrogatorie dixi: Num quem diligit anima mea, vidistis? id est, estisne desideratam sponsi præsentiam, opem et consolationem experti? Quibus super sponsi recessu dolentibus, pertransivi.
paras.en: [[3:3|The watchmen who keep the city, found me|Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem]], that is, the prelates and teachers of the faithful, whose office it is, with watchfulness of heart, to guard the faithful themselves from the wolves of hell, from the perils of temptations, from the snares of vices. Hence the Lord speaks through Isaias: [[Is 62:6|Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen|Super muros tuos, Jerusalem, constitui custodes]]. And Paul exhorts: [[Rom 12:8|he that ruleth, with carefulness|Qui præest, in sollicitudine]]; supply: let him rule. At times also in the Scriptures the holy angels are understood by the watchmen, according to that saying: [[Dan 4:14|This is the decree by the sentence of the watchers|In sententia vigilum decretum est]]; and again: [[Dan 4:10|a watcher, and a holy one came down|Descendit sanctus vigil]] [Denis's wording is shorter: "a holy watcher came down"]. Let the shepherds of the faithful therefore keep watch continually over the flock entrusted to them, as is commanded to one of them, and in his person to them all: [[Apoc 3:2|Be watchful and strengthen the things that remain, which are ready to die|Esto vigilans, et confirma cetera quæ moritura erant]]. So when these watchmen met me I asked them: [[3:3|Have you seen him, whom my soul loveth?|Num quem diligit anima mea, vidistis?]] that is, have you experienced the longed-for presence of the Bridegroom, his help and consolation? And as they grieved over the Bridegroom's going away, I passed on by them.

paras.t: Paululum quum pertransissem eos, totam spem meam ponendo in pietate et gratia sponsi, eumque perseveranter quærendo, omni humano relicto solatio, inveni quem diligit anima mea. Quis enim speravit in Domino, et relictus est ab eo? Et sponsus ipse promisit: Omnis qui quærit, invenit. Sed necesse est perseverare in bono incepto. Non enim repellit in sempiternum Dominus: quia etsi abjecit, tamen miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum; et ipse post tempestatem donat tranquillitatem, atque post fletum consolationem infundit. Sic et frequenter ad tempus reliquit vastari ac deformari et affligi Ecclesiam, et postmodum gratiosissime visitavit, consolatus est, et reformavit eamdem; et ipsa mater Ecclesia in synodis suis frequenter impetravit adsistentiam sponsi optatam, atque per sanctos viros desuper missos, concupitam reformationem adepta est.
paras.en: [[3:4|When I had a little passed by them|Paululum quum pertransissem eos]], putting all my hope in the loving-kindness and grace of the Bridegroom and seeking him perseveringly, leaving all human comfort behind, [[3:4|I found him whom my soul loveth|inveni quem diligit anima mea]]. For who hath [[Ecclus 2:11|hoped in the Lord|speravit in Domino]], and been forsaken by him? [Denis's wording joins Ecclus 2:11, "no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded", with 2:12, "who hath continued in his commandment, and hath been forsaken?"] And the Bridegroom himself promised: [[Matt 7:8|every one that|Omnis qui]] [[Matt 7:8|seeketh, findeth|quærit, invenit]]. But one must persevere in the good begun. For [[Lam 3:31|the Lord will not cast off for ever|repellit in sempiternum Dominus]]: for even [[Lam 3:32|if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies|etsi abjecit, tamen miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum]]; and after the storm he gives calm, and after weeping he pours in consolation[[Tob 3:22||]]. So too he has often let the Church be laid waste, disfigured and afflicted for a time, and afterwards most graciously visited, consoled and reformed her; and Mother Church herself has often obtained in her synods the help of the Bridegroom she longed for, and through holy men sent from on high has gained the reform she desired.

paras.t: Tenui eum, id est, constanter ei adhæsi ac obedivi, et brachiis caritatis amplexata sum eum tanto avidius, quanto quæsivi eum diutius, et quo amplius ejus gratiosa præsentia modo indigeo; nec dimittam, id est, mentem non avertam ab eo per negligentiam aut transgressionem, ne rursus ab eo relinquar. Hæc sunt verba boni et fervidi ac constantis propositi. Sic et Apostolus dixit: Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? Et Psalmista: Mihi adhærere Deo, bonum est.
paras.en: [[3:4|I held him|Tenui eum]], that is, I clung to him constantly and obeyed him, and embraced him with the arms of charity the more eagerly the longer I had sought him, and the more I now stand in need of his gracious presence; [[3:4|and I will not let him go|nec dimittam]], that is, I will not turn my mind away from him through negligence or transgression, lest I be forsaken by him again. These are the words of a good, fervent and constant resolve. So too the Apostle said: [[Rom 8:35|Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ?|Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi?]] And the Psalmist: [[Ps 72:28|it is good for me to adhere to my God|Mihi adhærere Deo, bonum est]].

paras.t: Donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ, et in cubiculum genitricis meæ, id est, quousque simul cum illo introducar in regnum triumphantis Ecclesiæ, quæ est mater et domina Ecclesiæ militantis: quod in die novissimo, completo generali judicio, universaliter fiet ac consummate, quum dixerit Judex ac sponsus: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi. Interim autem Ecclesia tenet sponsum suum per fidem, spem, et caritatem; tunc vero deinceps possessura est eum sine difficultate atque renisu ac pugna, per visionem, conjunctionem ac fruitionem felicem. Cubiculum vero triumphantis Ecclesiæ, est pax illa supernæ Jerusalem, omnem sensum exsuperans, seu puritas Beatorum confirmata in bono, in qua securissime conquiescunt. Rursus, domus illa, est tota patria illa beata. Cubicula vero illius, sunt diversi gradus præmiorum, juxta diversitatem et exigentiam meritorum. De qua ait Apostolus: Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis corrumpatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis.
paras.en: [[3:4|till I bring him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that bore me|Donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ, et in cubiculum genitricis meæ]], that is, until together with him I am brought into the kingdom of the Church triumphant, which is the mother and mistress of the Church militant[[Gal 4:26||]]: which will be done universally and in full on the last day, when the general judgement is completed, when the Judge and Bridegroom shall have said: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi]]. Meanwhile the Church holds her Bridegroom by faith, hope and charity; but then and thenceforth she will possess him without difficulty, resistance or struggle, by vision, union and blissful enjoyment [*fruitio*: the delight of possessing God as one's last end]. And the chamber of the Church triumphant is that peace of the heavenly Jerusalem which [[Phil 4:7|surpasseth all understanding|omnem sensum exsuperans]], or the purity of the blessed confirmed in good, in which they rest most securely. Again, the house is that whole blessed fatherland; and its chambers are the different degrees of reward, according to the difference and the claim of merits. Of this the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 5:1|we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven|Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis corrumpatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis]].

paras.t: Vel sic: donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ, etc., id est ad particulares Ecclesias, reformando eas per auxilium sponsi: quæ sunt domus et congregationes matris meæ, id est filiæ ortæ ex primitiva Ecclesia, quæ est mater et genitrix mea, quia prior me tempore, et ex ea gratiam et doctrinam suscepi. Cubicula autem, sunt diversi status et gradus ordinesque credentium. Unde et dicitur in Psalmo: Quæ dicitis in cordibus vestris, in cubilibus vestris compungimini.
paras.en: Or thus: [[3:4|till I bring him into my mother's house|donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ]], etc., that is, to the particular Churches, reforming them by the Bridegroom's help: these are the houses and congregations of my mother, that is, daughters sprung from the primitive Church, who is my mother and she that bore me, since she is before me in time, and from her I received grace and doctrine. And the chambers are the different states, degrees and orders of believers. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 4:5|the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds|Quæ dicitis in cordibus vestris, in cubilibus vestris compungimini]] [*cubilia*, "beds", answers to the *cubiculum*, "chamber", of the verse].

paras.t: Hoc tam sancto sponsæ generalis audito proposito, Christus jubet filiabus Jerusalem, ne sponsam a suis avellant amplexibus, dicens: Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas, cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit. Estque iste versus præcedenti capitulo expositus: quem sponsus ad insinuandum magnitudinem suæ caritatis sollicitudinisque ad sponsam, hic repetit. Vel ibi protulit versum hunc ad Ecclesiam ex Judaismo conversam, hic ad Ecclesiam ex gentilitate collectam, vel potius ad eamdem, quantum ad diversas partes ipsius. Attamen etiam infra repetitur idem.
paras.en: Hearing so holy a resolve of the universal bride, Christ commands the daughters of Jerusalem not to tear the bride from his embraces, saying: [[3:5|I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor awake my beloved, till she please|Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas, cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit]]. This verse was explained in the preceding chapter[[Cant 2:7||]]; the Bridegroom repeats it here to make known the greatness of his charity and solicitude for the bride. Or else there he spoke this verse to the Church converted from Judaism, and here to the Church gathered from the Gentiles; or rather to the same Church, as regards her different parts. And the same is repeated further on as well[[Cant 8:4||]].

paras.t: Deinde sponsus quasi admirans sponsæ decorem, agilitatem ac gracilitatem, subjungit: Quæ est ista, quæ ascendit per desertum? id est, per solitudinem hujus sæculi, per medium nationis perversæ a Deo desertæ, per hoc sæculum nequam divina inhabitatione privatum, scandit ad sublimitatem virtutum, ad contemplationis fastigium, ad altitudinem regni cœlorum; sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrhæ et thuris et universi pulveris pigmentarii, id est, subtilis, gracilis, ornata, suavis, et in altum se erigens per spiritualem profectum, contemplationem sinceram, fervidumque affectum, instar vaporis per modum virgulæ in altum tendentis: qui vapor consurgit ac oritur ex incensione aromaticæ confectionis, factæ ex myrrha et thure, ceterisque pulveribus arte pigmentarii præparatis: per myrrham amaram, intelligendo corporis mortificationem, et cruciformem Christi imitationem; per thus, quod in sacrificio Deo offertur, devotionis suavitatem, sine qua corporalis exercitatio parum aut nihil valet, seu bonæ famæ odorem, et delectationem in actu virtutum, aut certe ferventium orationum fragrantiam, juxta illud in Apocalypsi: Data sunt ei incensa multa de orationibus Sanctorum. Porro, per ceteros pulveres aromaticos, intelligendæ sunt ceterarum virtutum atque donorum actiones ac delectationes, luce discretionis commixtæ ac divini igne amoris succensæ. Ex quibus omnibus procedit a mente tam virtuosa exhalatio spiritualis, rectissima prorsum, subtilis, id est pura, dulcis ac fervens ad Deum affectio; cui sponsa assimilatur, quoniam ad hoc tendit totus conatus Ecclesiæ, ut affectione hujusmodi impleatur, atque in spiritum transformetur, quatenus ab omni carnalitate et vitiorum grossitie emundata, feratur ad sponsum cœlestem libere ac ferventer, assidue ac manenter.
paras.en: Then the Bridegroom, as if marvelling at the bride's comeliness, nimbleness and slenderness, adds: [[3:6|Who is she that goeth up by the desert|Quæ est ista, quæ ascendit per desertum]]? that is, through the wilderness of this world, through [[Phil 2:15|the midst of a crooked and perverse generation|per medium nationis perversæ]] deserted by God [*desertum*, "desert", is also "deserted"], through this wicked world bereft of God's indwelling, she climbs to the height of the virtues, to the summit of contemplation, to the heights of the kingdom of heaven, [[3:6|as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer?|sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrhæ et thuris et universi pulveris pigmentarii]] that is, fine, slender, adorned, sweet, and rising on high through spiritual progress, sincere contemplation and fervent affection, like a vapour going up on high in the manner of a slender rod [*virgula*, "little rod", which the Douay-Rheims renders "pillar"]: a vapour that rises and springs from the burning of an aromatic compound made of myrrh and frankincense and the other powders prepared by the perfumer's art. By the bitter myrrh is understood the mortification of the body and the imitation of Christ in the form of the cross; by the frankincense, which is offered to God in sacrifice, the sweetness of devotion, without which bodily exercise avails little or nothing; or else the odour of good repute, and delight in the practice of the virtues; or at any rate the fragrance of fervent prayers, according to that saying in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 8:3|there was given to him much incense, that he should offer of the prayers of all saints|Data sunt ei incensa multa de orationibus Sanctorum]]. Further, by the other aromatic powders are to be understood the acts and delights of the other virtues and gifts, mingled with the light of discretion and kindled by the fire of divine love. From all these there proceeds from a mind so virtuous a spiritual exhalation: an affection towards God wholly upright, fine (that is, pure), sweet and fervent; and to this the bride is likened, since the whole endeavour of the Church tends to this, that she be filled with such affection and transformed into spirit, so that, cleansed of all carnality and of the grossness of vices, she may be borne to the heavenly Bridegroom freely and fervently, constantly and abidingly.

paras.t: En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israel. Per lectulum Salomonis, designatur mens sponsæ, in qua cum sponsa sponsus quiescit. Hunc ambiunt sexaginta fortes electi ex omni plebe fidelium, id est universi pastores idonei et prædicatores condigni, qui gregem dominicum et lectulum Dei in eo custodiunt, sicut prædictum est. Frequenter autem in Scripturis ponitur numerus determinatus pro indeterminato, sicut in Psalmo: Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis. Horum autem universitas per sexaginta innuitur, quoniam sexaginta sunt sexies decem, seu decies sex. Per denarium vero, adimpletio Decalogi; per senarium, ipsa observantiæ hujus insinuatur perfectio.
paras.en: [[3:7|Behold threescore valiant ones of the most valiant of Israel, surrounded the bed of Solomon?|En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israel]] By the bed of Solomon is signified the mind of the bride, in which the Bridegroom rests with the bride. About it stand threescore valiant ones chosen out of all the people of the faithful: that is, all fit pastors and worthy preachers, who guard the Lord's flock and God's bed within it, as was said above. Now in the Scriptures a definite number is often put for an indefinite one, as in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:7|A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand|Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis]]. And the whole of them is signified by sixty, since sixty is six times ten, or ten times six. By the ten is signified the fulfilment of the Decalogue; by the six, the perfection of this observance [six being a perfect number, the sum of its divisors 1, 2 and 3].

paras.t: Omnes tenentes gladios, id est arma virtutum contra aerias potestates et aciem vitiorum. Specialiter vero, teste Apostolo, gladius spiritualis est verbum Dei, quo resecantur peccata, et cordis aperitur duritia. Rursus, gladius est rigor justitiæ, justa sententia ac ultio debita: juxta quod scribitur in Apocalypsi, De ore ejus procedebat gladius ex utraque parte acutus; atque in Psalmo, Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum. Prælati ergo et prædicatores gladios tenent, quoniam verba sacræ Scripturæ prompte habent in ore, in memoria, in effectu: per quæ verba custodiunt lectulum Christi, quoniam prædicando, hortando, comminando, corripiendo, adversarios humanæ expellunt salutis, et oves Salvatoris purgant, illuminant, et inflammant, ac coram Deo sollicitas reddunt: quia, ut ait Apostolus, Omnis Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, ad exhortandum, ad corripiendum, ad erudiendum in justitia, ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum instructus. Hinc Christus de se ipso ait in Isaia: Posuit Dominus os meum quasi gladium acutum. Et de ipso increato sermone dicitur ad Hebræos: Vivus est sermo Dei et efficax, et penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti.
paras.en: [[3:8|All holding swords|Omnes tenentes gladios]], that is, the arms of the virtues against the powers of the air and the battle line of the vices. But in particular, as the Apostle testifies, the spiritual sword is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]], by which sins are cut away and the hardness of the heart is laid open. Again, the sword is the rigour of justice, just sentence and due vengeance, according to what is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:15|out of his mouth proceedeth a sharp two-edged sword|De ore ejus procedebat gladius ex utraque parte acutus]][[Apoc 1:16||]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 149:6|two-edged swords in their hands|Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum]]. So prelates and preachers hold swords, since they have the words of holy Scripture ready in their mouths, in their memory and in their deeds; and by these words they guard the bed of Christ, since by preaching, exhorting, threatening and rebuking they drive out the adversaries of man's salvation, and cleanse, enlighten and inflame the Saviour's sheep and make them watchful before God; for, as the Apostle says, [[2 Tim 3:16|All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice|Omnis Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, ad exhortandum, ad corripiendum, ad erudiendum in justitia]], [[2 Tim 3:17|That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work|ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum instructus]]. Hence Christ says of himself in Isaias that the Lord [[Is 49:2|hath made my mouth like a sharp sword|Posuit Dominus os meum quasi gladium acutum]]. And of the uncreated Word himself it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 4:12|the word of God is living and effectual and more piercing than any two edged sword|Vivus est sermo Dei et efficax, et penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti]].

paras.t: Et ad bella doctissimi. Hoc plane pertinet ad pastores et prædicatores, et ad universos curam animarum sortitos, ut sint valde exercitati in conversatione virtutum, in prælio spirituali, in modo ac arte resistendi ac prævalendi hostibus animarum: quatenus valeant non solum se ipsos a vitiorum læsionibus præservare, a tentationum circumventione eruere, in dubiis informare, et de spirituali profectu instruere; sed et subditis suis ac imperitis providere de omnibus istis.
paras.en: [[3:8|and most expert in war|Et ad bella doctissimi]]. This plainly concerns pastors and preachers and all who have been given the care of souls: that they be well practised in the life of the virtues, in spiritual combat, in the way and art of resisting and overcoming the enemies of souls; so that they may be able not only to keep themselves from the wounds of vices, to free themselves from the snares of temptations, to inform themselves in doubts and instruct themselves in spiritual progress, but also to provide all these things for their subjects and for the unskilled.

paras.t: Uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos. Spirituale femur, est vis intellectiva seu intellectus, per fidem et sapientiam informatus: per quem homo generat filios spirituales, instruendo convertendoque proximos, sicut quibusdam scribit Apostolus: In Christo Jesu per Evangelium ego vos genui. Super hoc femur habet unusquisque bonus prælatus ac eruditor gladium, id est verbum Dei: quia Scripturæ verba habet in intellectu, et ex intellectus discretione pronuntiat ea; verbaque oris sui sunt effectus et signa intellectualium suorum verborum. Unde et sponso ait Psalmista: Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime. Sic autem unusquisque talium est accinctus, propter timores nocturnos, id est, ad præcavendum sponsæ ac lectulo Christi ab inordinatis timoribus, et a terribilibus, quæ in tenebris et ignorantiis, adversitatibus et tentationibus vitæ præsentis solent occurrere: a quibus omnibus eripitur homo per verbum Dei, quemadmodum scriptum est: Scuto circumdabit te veritas ejus; non timebis a timore nocturno. Sponsus quoque in Evangelio: Nolite, inquit, timere eos qui corpus occidunt; sed eum timete, qui habet potestatem corpus et animam mittere in gehennam: hoc est, inordinatam propulsare formidinem. Sicque eruditus quicumque fidelis fiducialiter psallit: Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea: quem timebo? Propter quod dixit Michæas: Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est.
paras.en: [[3:8|every man's sword upon his thigh, because of fears in the night|Uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos]]. The spiritual thigh is the intellective power or intellect, informed by faith and wisdom, by which a man begets spiritual children, instructing and converting his neighbours, as the Apostle writes to some: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|In Christo Jesu per Evangelium ego vos genui]]. Upon this thigh every good prelate and teacher has a sword, that is, the word of God: for he has the words of Scripture in his intellect, and utters them out of the intellect's discernment; and the words of his mouth are the effects and signs of his intellectual words [that is, the inner words or concepts of the mind]. Hence the Psalmist says to the Bridegroom: [[Ps 44:4|Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O thou most mighty.|Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime.]] And thus each of these is girded [[3:8|because of fears in the night|propter timores nocturnos]], that is, to guard the bride and the bed of Christ against inordinate fears, and against the terrors that are wont to befall us in the darkness and ignorance, the adversities and temptations of this present life: from all of which a man is rescued by the word of God, as it is written: [[Ps 90:5|His truth shall compass thee with a shield: thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.|Scuto circumdabit te veritas ejus; non timebis a timore nocturno]] The Bridegroom too, in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not|Nolite]], he says, [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]; but [[Matt 10:28|fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|eum timete, qui habet potestatem corpus et animam mittere in gehennam]] [Denis's wording, "who hath power to cast body and soul into hell", is close to Luke 12:5]: that is, to drive away inordinate dread. And so every faithful soul thus taught sings with confidence: [[Ps 26:1|The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?|Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea: quem timebo?]] For which reason Micheas said: [[Mich 7:8|when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light|Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est]].

paras.t: Præterea, per sexaginta istos fortissimos et accinctos, intelligi possunt angeli sancti, hominibus pro custodia deputati, juxta illud Psalmistæ: Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis. Omnes quippe sunt administratorii spiritus. Hi expertissimi peritissimique consistunt ad præliandum pro suis contra nequissimos spiritus, quos coercent, ne quantum volunt ac possent, impugnent et vexent nos. Illuminant quoque mentes nostras allocutione et instructione interna.
paras.en: Moreover, by these threescore most valiant and girded ones may be understood the holy angels, appointed to men as their guard, according to that saying of the Psalmist: [[Ps 90:11|he hath given his angels charge over thee; to keep thee in all thy ways|Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis]]. For they are [[Heb 1:14|all ministering spirits|Omnes quippe sunt administratorii spiritus]]. These, most expert and most skilled, stand ready to fight for their own against the most wicked spirits, whom they hold in check, lest these assail and harass us as much as they would and could. They also enlighten our minds by inward speech and instruction.

paras.t: Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani. Per ferculum, quod dicitur cibus seu solium, designatur tota Ecclesia: in qua moratur ac residet sponsus, et eam quasi manducando incorporat sibi. Igne quoque caritatis consumit in ea quod pravum est, ac privatum amorem, ut cum Apostolo dicere queat: Vivo autem, jam non ego; vivit vero in me Christus. Hoc ferculum fecit Christus per se ipsum et suos discipulos, prædicando fidem et gratiam influendo, et eos quos prædestinavit pie vocando, sicut in Actibus legitur: Crediderunt, quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam. Hinc in Zacharia de Christo prædictum est: Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, et ædificabit templum Domino: et erit sacerdos super solio suo. Hoc ferculum construxit artifex summus de lignis Libani, id est ex electis personis: quæ sic per gratiarum charismata eminent hominibus ceteris, sicut ligna Libani, hoc est cedrus et cypressus quæ in monte Libano oriuntur, ceteris lignis præfulgent, quia secundum Glossam, imputribilis sunt naturæ, et boni odoris, fortia, candida, et formosa. Sic electi vitiorum abhorrent putredinem, boni sunt nominis, caritate ac pietate dulcescunt, virtutibus roborantur, donis ornantur, caritate et gratia sunt decori.
paras.en: [[3:9|King Solomon hath made him a litter of the wood of Libanus|Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani]]. By the litter, which is called a dish or a throne [*ferculum* can mean a dish of food, and also a litter or seat of state], is signified the whole Church, in which the Bridegroom dwells and abides, and which he incorporates into himself as if by eating it. By the fire of charity, too, he consumes in her whatever is perverse, and private love, so that she may say with the Apostle: [[Gal 2:20|And I live, now not I: but Christ liveth in me|Vivo autem, jam non ego; vivit vero in me Christus]]. Christ made this litter through himself and his disciples, by preaching the faith and pouring in grace, and by lovingly calling those whom he predestinated[[Rom 8:30||]], as we read in the Acts: [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting believed|Crediderunt, quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam]]. Hence it was foretold of Christ in Zacharias: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]], [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]]: [[Zach 6:13|and he shall be a priest upon his throne|et erit sacerdos super solio suo]]. This litter the supreme craftsman built [[3:9|of the wood of Libanus|de lignis Libani]], that is, of chosen persons, who by the charisms of graces stand out above other men as the woods of Libanus (that is, the cedar and the cypress that grow on Mount Libanus) outshine other woods; for, according to the Gloss, they are of an incorruptible nature, sweet-smelling, strong, white and beautiful. So the elect abhor the rottenness of vices, are of good name, grow sweet with charity and piety, are strengthened by virtues, adorned with gifts, and made comely by charity and grace.

paras.t: Columnas ejus fecit argenteas: id est, sanctos Apostolos et apostolicos viros ac virtuosos præsules et pastores fecit ceteris clariores, et in scientia Scripturarum ac eloquentia præfulgentes: Ego, inquiens, dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri; itemque, Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem. De talibus inclytissimis viris scripsit et Paulus: Cephas, Jacobus et Joannes, qui videbantur columnæ esse, etc.
paras.en: [[3:10|The pillars thereof he made of silver|Columnas ejus fecit argenteas]]: that is, he made the holy Apostles and apostolic men, and virtuous prelates and pastors, brighter than the rest and shining in the knowledge of the Scriptures and in eloquence: [[Luke 21:15|I|Ego]], he says, [[Luke 21:15|will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]]; and again: [[John 16:13|when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]]. Of such most renowned men Paul too wrote: [[Gal 2:9|James and Cephas and John, who seemed to be pillars|Cephas, Jacobus et Joannes, qui videbantur columnæ esse]], etc.

paras.t: Reclinatorium aureum. Reclinatorium appellatur pars throni superior, super quod caput reclinat se. Aureum ergo reclinatorium, est excellentissima illa persona Ecclesiæ, auro sapientiæ ac caritatis præ cunctis ornata, incomparabilis virgo Maria: in qua Rex omnipotens habitare, incarnari, quiescere præelegit, altitudinem suæ deitatis quasi reclinans in ea. Aureum quoque reclinatorium, sunt personæ eminenter contemplativæ ac fervidæ, ut anachoretæ, in quibus Dominus majestatis præcipue conquiescere perhibetur. Apostolis tamen nec in hac perfectione quisquam præfertur.
paras.en: [[3:10|the seat of gold|Reclinatorium aureum]]. The *reclinatorium* [literally "a thing to lean back on"; the Douay-Rheims has "seat"] is the name for the upper part of a throne, against which the head is leaned back. The seat of gold, then, is that most excellent person of the Church, adorned above all with the gold of wisdom and charity, the incomparable Virgin Mary: in whom the almighty King chose to dwell, to become incarnate and to rest, as it were reclining the height of his Godhead upon her. The seat of gold is also persons eminently contemplative and fervent, such as anchorites, in whom the Lord of majesty is said especially to take his rest. Yet not even in this perfection is anyone preferred to the Apostles.

paras.t: Ascensum purpureum. Ascensus iste tam pulcher, est ordinata virtutum connexio, in quibus ab inferioribus ad sublimiora oportet paulatim ascendere. Rursus iste ascensus, est coaptatio trium statuum, utpote status incipientium, status proficientium, et status perfectorum, per quos oportet gradatim et ordinate ascendere; seu distinctio triplicis viæ, videlicet purgativæ, illuminativæ et perfectivæ; vel cohabitudo virtutum moralium, intellectualium, et theologicarum. Est quoque ascensus Ecclesiæ purpureus, quia per sanguinis effusionem pro fide aut æquitate ad regnum cœleste a præsenti exsilio feliciter atque celerrime scanditur.
paras.en: [[3:10|the going up of purple|Ascensum purpureum]]. This going up, so beautiful, is the ordered connection of the virtues, in which one must climb little by little from the lower to the higher. Again, this going up is the fitting together of the three states, namely the state of beginners, the state of the proficient and the state of the perfect, through which one must climb step by step and in order; or the distinction of the threefold way, namely the purgative, the illuminative and the perfective [the three stages of the spiritual life: cleansing from sin, enlightenment and growth in virtue, and union with God]; or the mutual bond of the moral, the intellectual and the theological virtues. The going up of the Church is also of purple because, by the shedding of blood for the faith or for justice, one climbs happily and most swiftly from this present exile to the heavenly kingdom.

paras.t: Media caritate constravit. Media ferculi hujus, puta Ecclesiæ, sunt præcepta, per quæ a via ad patriam pervenitur; et ecclesiastica sacramenta, quæ ad hujus itineris expeditionem valde cooperantur: in quorum primo, id est Baptismo, omnia relaxantur peccata, quantum ad culpam et pœnam; in Confessione autem, ad minus quoad culpæ remissionem: quorum etiam sacramentorum dignissimum, quod Eucharistia nominatur, alio nomine viaticum nuncupatur, quia de via ad cœlestem elevat paradisum. Media quoque sunt evangelica Christi consilia, gratia, virtutes, ac merita: medium equidem dicitur, quod inter duo extrema locatur. Omnia media ista, sunt caritate constrata, complanata et informata: quoniam absque caritate nil prosunt, et ad caritatis plenitudinem omnia ordinantur, atque per eam faciliter adimplentur, quæ sine ea essent utique dura ac gravia ad implendum. Ideo omnibus his Dominus et Salvator caritatem superfudit et conjungi præcepit, mandans ex caritate omnia fieri, et universas ecclesiasticas personas in caritate uniri, unumque effici: In hoc, inquiens, cognoscent omnes, quia discipuli mei estis, si caritatem habueritis ad invicem; et item: Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut sint unum, sicut et nos unum sumus.
paras.en: [[3:10|the midst he covered with charity|Media caritate constravit]]. The midst [*media*, "the middle parts", can also mean "the means"; Denis reads it both ways] of this litter, that is, of the Church, are the commandments, by which one comes from the way to the fatherland; and the sacraments of the Church, which greatly help to speed this journey: in the first of which, that is Baptism, all sins are remitted as to both guilt and punishment; and in Confession at least as to the remission of guilt; and the most worthy of these sacraments, which is named the Eucharist, is called by another name the viaticum [that is, provision for the journey], because it lifts us from the way to the heavenly paradise. The means are also the gospel counsels of Christ, grace, the virtues and merits; for a mean is what is placed between two extremes. All these means are covered with charity, levelled and informed by it [*informata*: given their form, that is, made living and meritorious]: since without charity they profit nothing[[1 Cor 13:1||]] [the margin gives only 1 Cor. xiii; the words are closest to v. 3], and all things are ordered to the fulness of charity[[Matt 22:40||]] [the margin reads Matth. xxii, 10; v. 40, on the two commandments of love, fits the sense], and by it they are easily fulfilled which without it would surely be hard and heavy to fulfil. Therefore our Lord and Saviour poured charity over all these and commanded that they be joined to it, bidding that all things be done out of charity and that all the persons of the Church be united in charity and made one: [[John 13:35|By this|In hoc]], he says, [[John 13:35|shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another|cognoscent omnes, quia discipuli mei estis, si caritatem habueritis ad invicem]]; and again: Father, [[John 17:11|whom thou hast given me|quos dedisti mihi]], I will [[John 17:22|that, they may be one, as we also are one|ut sint unum, sicut et nos unum sumus]][[John 17:21||]] [the margin gives John xvii, 21, 11, 22; "Father, whom thou hast given me, I will" stands word for word in John 17:24].

paras.t: Sic ergo caritate constrata sunt propter filias Jerusalem, id est ad salutem animarum fidelium, quæ sunt filiæ militantis Ecclesiæ, quæ ubertim Jerusalem nuncupatur. Propter has filias, ad subveniendum eisdem, media sunt caritate constrata: quatenus filiæ istæ per caritatem accensæ, prompte obediant, ac perseverare in unitate Ecclesiæ delectentur, atque in communione mystici corporis Christi sponsi sui permaneant ac ditentur, quoniam omnes in caritate exsistentes, sibi invicem suffragantur, et merita sua communicant atque participant, juxta illud: Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te.
paras.en: So, then, they are covered with charity [[3:10|for the daughters of Jerusalem|propter filias Jerusalem]], that is, for the salvation of the souls of the faithful, who are the daughters of the Church militant, which is often called Jerusalem. For these daughters, to help them, the means are covered with charity: so that these daughters, kindled by charity, may readily obey, and delight to persevere in the unity of the Church, and may remain and be enriched in the communion of the mystical body of Christ their Bridegroom; since all who abide in charity help one another and share and partake of one another's merits, according to that saying: [[Ps 118:63|I am a partaker with all them that fear thee|Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam Unigenitus Dei fecit hæc per assumptam humanitatem, recte subinfertur monitio, ut incarnationis ejus pensemus mysteria, et assumptæ humanitatis glorificationem intueamur. Egredimini, id est, mentes vestras levate ad considerandum sequentia; exite de lacu miseriæ, de consuetudine prava, de negligentia ac torpore, de terrenis ad superna, de intellectus obtenebratione, distractione, imaginationeque fœda, vana ac stolida; et videte oculo fidei, o filiæ Sion, id est, o animæ speculativæ, seu ad speculandum divina creata, regem Salomonem, id est Christum verum Pacificum, reconciliatorem perfectum, in diademate, quo coronavit eum mater sua in assumpta humanitate, quam ex Virgine gloriosa ac benedicta assumpsit, pulcherrime cunctis divinis charismatibus in extremo termino excellentiæ decoratam. Qua humanitate Verbum æternum, quasi diademate coronatur: quoniam quamvis in sua deitate perfectum sit, nulliusque indigens; tamen in sua humanitate et incarnatione inenarrabiliter ac præclarissime relucet ac declaratur infinita pietas, dignatio, caritas, munificentia ejus ad genus humanum, et ipsum Verbum æternum, per suam incarnationem et assumptam humanitatem, nos coronavit, ac nostram naturam maxime honoravit. Sic autem mater sponsi istius coronavit filium suum in die desponsationis illius, id est in hora incarnationis, quando Filius Dei desponsavit sibi Ecclesiam, et Virginem matrem fecit suam sponsam singularem, ac cum assumpta natura nuptias celebravit ac iniit personales: quod totum jucundissime fecit ex caritate plenissima, exsultans ut gigas ad currendam viam, et ad peragendum nostræ salutis mysteria. Ideo subditur: et in die lætitiæ cordis ejus: quia de recuperatione honoris Patris æterni, ac salvatione generis humani summe gaudebat.
paras.en: But since the Only-begotten of God did these things through the humanity he assumed, an admonition fittingly follows, that we ponder the mysteries of his incarnation and gaze upon the glorification of the humanity he assumed. [[3:11|Go forth|Egredimini]], that is, lift up your minds to consider what follows: come out of [[Ps 39:3|the pit of misery|lacu miseriæ]], out of evil habit, out of negligence and torpor, from earthly things to things above, out of the darkening and distraction of the understanding and its foul, vain and foolish imaginings; [[3:11|and see|et videte]] with the eye of faith, [[3:11|ye daughters of Sion|o filiæ Sion]], that is, O contemplative souls, souls created to contemplate divine things, [[3:11|king Solomon|regem Salomonem]], that is, Christ, the true Peaceable One [the name Solomon means "peaceable"], the perfect reconciler, [[3:11|in the diadem, wherewith his mother crowned him|in diademate, quo coronavit eum mater sua]]: in the humanity he assumed, which he took from the glorious and blessed Virgin, most beautifully adorned with all the divine charisms to the utmost bound of excellence. With this humanity the eternal Word is crowned as with a diadem: for although in his Godhead he is perfect and in need of nothing, yet in his humanity and incarnation his infinite loving-kindness, condescension, charity and munificence towards mankind shine out and are made known unspeakably and most clearly; and the eternal Word himself, by his incarnation and the humanity he assumed, has crowned us and most highly honoured our nature. Thus the mother of this Bridegroom crowned her son [[3:11|in the day of his espousal|in die desponsationis illius]], that is, in the hour of the incarnation, when the Son of God espoused the Church to himself, made the Virgin his mother his singular bride, and celebrated and entered upon a personal marriage with the nature he assumed [that is, the union of the two natures in the one Person of the Word]. All this he did most joyfully, out of the fullest charity: he [[Ps 18:6|rejoiced as a giant to run the way|exsultans ut gigas ad currendam viam]], and to accomplish the mysteries of our salvation. Therefore it is added: [[3:11|in the day of the joy of his heart|et in die lætitiæ cordis ejus]]: for he rejoiced supremely at the recovery of the eternal Father's honour and the salvation of mankind.

paras.t: Insuper potest et ita exponi: Videte regem Salomonem in diademate, quo coronavit eum mater sua, id est Christum in glorificatione suæ humanitatis: qua glorificatione accidentalique præmio, quod sua passione promeruit, tanquam diademate coronatur, sicut in Psalmo habetur: Posuisti in capite ejus coronam de lapide pretioso. Et Apostolus protestatur: Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum; et denuo, Propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen. Propter quod in Apocalypsi asserunt Sancti: Dignus est Agnus, qui occisus est, accipere virtutem et divinitatem, et sapientiam et honorem et gloriam. Hinc passione instante, deprecatus est Patrem: Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Denique hoc diademate coronavit Christum mater sua, id est Judæa seu Synagoga, de qua secundum carnem est ortus, quia crucifixit eumdem: quam crucifixionem ipse Christus ex summa caritate, obedientia, pietate, et patientia libentissime sustinendo, promeruit taliter coronari a Deo Patre. In die desponsationis suæ, id est in sua resurrectione et gloriosa ascensione ad dextram Patris: in qua die desponsavit sibi Ecclesiam excellentiori modo quam ante, conferendo ei ex tunc affluentissima gratiæ dona. Imo et tunc dicitur sibi etiam triumphantem desponsasse Ecclesiam, lætificando eam speciali recentique modo de sua corporali præsentia ac triumpho, et præda quam secum tulit in ascendendo, quoniam secum deduxit animas Sanctorum, quas eduxit de limbo. Sicque dies illa fuit dies lætitiæ cordis sui, quam deinceps nunquam amittit.
paras.en: It can also be explained thus: [[3:11|see king Solomon in the diadem, wherewith his mother crowned him|Videte regem Salomonem in diademate, quo coronavit eum mater sua]], that is, Christ in the glorification of his humanity: with which glorification and accidental reward [that is, a reward added to the essential beatitude, such as the glory of his body and the exaltation of his name], which he merited by his passion, he is crowned as with a diadem; as we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 20:4|thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones|Posuisti in capite ejus coronam de lapide pretioso]]. And the Apostle declares: [[Heb 2:9|we see Jesus|Videmus Jesum]] [[Heb 2:9|for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour|propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum]]; and again: [[Phil 2:9|For which cause, God also hath exalted him and hath given him a name which is above all names|Propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen]]. For this reason the saints declare in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 5:12|The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power and divinity and wisdom and strength and honour and glory|Dignus est Agnus, qui occisus est, accipere virtutem et divinitatem, et sapientiam et honorem et gloriam]]. Hence, as his passion drew near, he prayed to the Father: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. Lastly, his mother crowned Christ with this diadem, that is, Judæa or the Synagogue, from which he sprang according to the flesh, since she crucified him; by bearing which crucifixion most willingly, out of supreme charity, obedience, loving-kindness and patience, Christ himself merited to be so crowned by God the Father. [[3:11|in the day of his espousal|In die desponsationis]], that is, in his resurrection and glorious ascension to the right hand of the Father: on which day he espoused the Church to himself in a more excellent manner than before, bestowing on her from then on the most abundant gifts of grace. Nay, he is said then to have espoused to himself the Church triumphant as well, gladdening her in a special and new manner with his bodily presence and triumph, and with the spoil he took with him in ascending, since he led with him the souls of the saints, whom he brought out of limbo. And so that day was [[3:11|the day of the joy of his heart|dies lætitiæ cordis sui]], which he never loses thereafter.

paras.t: Itaque, o fideles animæ, hoc modo considerate Regem et sponsum vestrum, qui tanta propter vos toleravit, tamque gloriosissime triumphavit: quatenus ejus exemplo patientiam addiscatis, atque in omni afflictione, injuria, persecutione maneatis immobiles ac tranquilli, ut sic vestro conformemini sponso, et paulo post glorificemini ab eodem. Omnes namque qui pie vivere volunt in ipso, hac via oportet incedere; nec dignus est glorificari, qui respuit compati.
paras.en: So then, O faithful souls, consider in this way your King and Bridegroom, who bore so much for your sakes and triumphed so most gloriously: so that by his example you may learn patience, and remain unmoved and calm in every affliction, wrong and persecution, and thus be conformed to your Bridegroom and shortly be glorified by him. For [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly|Omnes namque qui pie vivere volunt]] in him must walk by this way; nor is he worthy to be glorified who refuses to suffer with him.

3.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM CAPITULI TERTII, DE CHRISTO ET SPONSA PARTICULARI.
3.title_en: Exposition of the same third chapter: of Christ and the particular bride

paras.t: In lectulo meo per noctes quæsivi quem diligit anima mea. Immaterialis et incorporeæ animæ, ad supergloriosæ adorandæque Trinitatis imaginem conditæ, lectulus utique simplex et immaterialis est: utpote tranquillitas cordis, quando affectionibus reformatis ac simplificatis in Deo, passionum cessat inquietudo et vitiorum tumultus, ipsis quoque tentationibus cito faciliterque resistitur. Anima ergo sic tranquillata, sine delectatione diu esse non valens, nec tamen in vanitatibus atque insaniis falsis consolationem admittere volens, magis vero cupiens adimplere quod scriptum est, Gaudete in Domino semper; et rursus, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur: protestatur et ait: In lectulo meo, id est in quiete et confidentia conscientiæ meæ, per noctes, id est in subtractionibus illuminationum, consolationum, dulciumque præsentiarum sponsi ac Domini mei, et in ariditate ac contristationibus cordis mei, quæsivi speciosum forma præ filiis hominum, quem diligit anima mea, id est vis animalis seu ego ipsa, quæ mea sum, quia post Deum specialiter amo me.
paras.en: [[3:1|In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth|In lectulo meo per noctes quæsivi quem diligit anima mea]]. The bed of the immaterial and incorporeal soul, which was made to the image of the supremely glorious and adorable Trinity[[Gen 1:27||]], is assuredly a simple and immaterial bed: namely, tranquillity of heart, when, the affections having been reformed and made simple in God, the restlessness of the passions and the tumult of the vices cease, and temptations themselves are resisted quickly and easily. The soul, then, thus made tranquil, being unable to be long without delight, and yet unwilling to admit consolation in [[Ps 39:5|vanities, and lying follies|vanitatibus atque insaniis falsis]], but desiring rather to fulfil what is written, [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]]; and again, [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]: declares and says: [[3:1|In my bed|In lectulo meo]], that is, in the quiet and confidence of my conscience; [[3:1|by night|per noctes]], that is, in the withdrawals of the enlightenments, the consolations and the sweet presences of my spouse and Lord, and in the dryness and the sorrows of my heart, [[3:1|I sought|quæsivi]] him who is [[Ps 44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosum forma præ filiis hominum]], [[3:1|him whom my soul loveth|quem diligit anima mea]], that is, the power of my soul [*vis animalis*, the power belonging to the soul, *anima*], or I myself, who am my own, since after God I love myself in a special way.

paras.t: Interdum etenim anima amorosa dispensative relinquitur sibimetipsi, et consueta alacritate, lætitia, fervore, meditationumque subtilitate privatur, et quamdam insipiditatem, ariditatem, ac mœrorem illabitur: ita quod cœlum sibi æneum esse videtur, terraque ferrea, et se esse relictam veretur; atque ex consideratione propriæ imperfectionis, fragilitatis, ac defectuositatis, grandem incurrit tristitiam. In hujuscemodi igitur noctibus restat, ut quærat dilectum in lectulo suo: ita ut ab exterioribus occupationibus et curis se abstrahat, et se pro posse recolligat, miserationesque Domini pensans, dicat: O Domine gratiosissime, sponse super omnia prædilecte, in me non est fortitudo emergendi a calamitatum istarum abysso; sed quum ignorem quid agere debeam, hoc solum residui habeo, ut dirigam oculos ad te.
paras.en: For at times the loving soul is, by God's dispensation [that is, by a providential arrangement, for its good], left to herself, and is deprived of her wonted eagerness, joy, fervour and subtlety of meditation, and sinks into a certain tastelessness, dryness and grief: so that the heaven seems to her to be of brass, and the earth of iron, and she fears that she has been forsaken; and from considering her own imperfection, frailty and deficiency, she falls into great sadness. In such nights, therefore, it remains for her to seek her beloved in her bed: that is, to withdraw herself from outward occupations and cares, and to gather herself together as far as she can, and, pondering the mercies of the Lord, to say: O most gracious Lord, my spouse beloved above all things, there is no strength in me to rise out of the abyss of these calamities; but since I know not what I ought to do, this alone is left me, to direct my eyes to thee[[2 Par 20:12||]].

paras.t: Quæsivi illum, ad obtinendum ab eo bona præfatis malis contraria. Quæsivi illum, et non inveni ita celeriter atque suaviter, ut optavi. Sic et sanctus Job loquitur Deo: Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me: mutatus es mihi in crudelem. Hinc Psalmista loquitur Deo: Usquequo, Domine, oblivisceris me in finem? usquequo avertis faciem tuam a me? Sed non est cessandum ab ista inquisitione salubri, quum scriptum sit: Quærite Dominum, et confirmamini; quærite faciem ejus semper. Certumque est, quod quærens non frustrabitur suæ quæsitionis effectu et fructu, quantum est ex parte benignissimi Dei; verumtamen ex parte quærentis, posset impedimentum accidere: ideo spei sit quidam timor admixtus. Hinc etenim scriptum est: Quis scit, si convertatur et ignoscat Deus, et relinquat post se benedictionem? Unde et rex Ninive loquitur: Quis scit, si convertatur et ignoscat Deus, et revertatur a furore iræ suæ, et non peribimus? Idcirco subjungitur:
paras.en: [[3:1|I sought him|Quæsivi illum]], to obtain from him good things contrary to the evils spoken of. [[3:1|I sought him, and found him not|Quæsivi illum, et non inveni]] so quickly and so sweetly as I wished.
