But in the hour of her Son's resurrection and appearing the sweetest south wind followed, and gladdened her with its sweet flowing, so that her spices spread themselves on every side.

paras.t: Postremo in ejus felicissima assumptione recessit ab ea finaliter omnis mœror, quando a Filio suo tam suaviter ac frequenter est invitata, dicente : Veni de Libano, sponsa mea, veni de Libano, veni. Tunc etenim a candore gratiæ, a luce puritatis internæ, a suorum munditia meritorum, perducta est ad splendorem gloriæ æternalis, ad lucem deificæ visionis, ad ineffabilium plenitudinem præmiorum. Et quanto præ ceteris fuit hæc Christo magis compassa, tanto abundantius cum eo, in eo, et ab eo est glorificata et coronata. De capite Amana, de vertice Sanir et Hermon, de cubilibus leonum, de montibus pardorum, id est de conversione et salute innumerabilium peccatorum, inquietorum, carnalium, et a Deo antea anathematizatorum, per præfata designatorum : qui ipsius benignissimæ ac misericordissimæ virgineæ Matris meritis ac precibus, gratiam conversionis et gloriam sunt sortiti. Nam et ipsa Filio suo tam intentissime condolendo, innumerabilibus peccatoribus gratiam et salutem promeruit, quos Deus per eam convertere ac salvare ab æterno decrevit.
paras.en: Lastly, in her most happy assumption all sorrow finally departed from her, when she was invited so sweetly and so often by her Son, saying: [[4:8|Come from Libanus, my spouse, come from Libanus, come|Veni de Libano, sponsa mea, veni de Libano, veni]]. For then from the whiteness of grace [Libanus was taken to mean "whiteness"], from the light of inward purity, from the cleanness of her merits, she was brought to the splendour of eternal glory, to the light of the deifying vision, to the fullness of ineffable rewards. And the more she, above others, suffered with Christ, the more abundantly was she glorified and crowned with Him, in Him and by Him: [[4:8|from the top of Amana, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards|De capite Amana, de vertice Sanir et Hermon, de cubilibus leonum, de montibus pardorum]], that is, from the conversion and salvation of innumerable sinners, the restless, the carnal, and those formerly accursed by God, who are signified by these names: who through the merits and prayers of this most kind and most merciful Virgin Mother have obtained the grace of conversion and glory. For she too, by suffering so most intently with her Son, merited grace and salvation for innumerable sinners, whom God decreed from eternity to convert and save through her.

5.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI QUINTI : VENIAT DILECTUS MEUS IN HORTUM SUUM ; DE CHRISTO ET ECCLESIA.
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: Let my beloved come into his garden; of Christ and the Church

paras.t: Præcedenti capitulo Christus vocavit Ecclesiam hortum. Huic ergo appellationi se conformans Ecclesia, Christum invitat, ut intret hunc hortum, id est in corda fidelium. Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, id est, gratiose me visitet, dona sua infundendo, conservando, augendo, et perficiendo in me. Tanquam dicat Ecclesia: Unusquisque in horto suo amœno et concluso solet libenter deambulare, et cum dilecta sibi persona quiescere. Sponsus ergo cœlestis, qui me hortum appellavit conclusum, dignetur mihi adesse, consolationem, protectionem, amplexum impendere: quia continua præsentia ejus clementi indigeo, et sine gratioso ejus auxilio prorsus nil valeo. Veniat ergo, obsecro, ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum, id est, actus fidelium pie acceptet, et delectetur in eis, ac cœnet et vescatur cum ipsis, quoniam ipse in Apocalypsi fatetur: Si quis aperuerit mihi, intrabo ad illum, et cœnabo cum eo. De quo in Esdra asseritur, Gaudium Domini est fortitudo vestra; et in Psalmo, Lætabitur Dominus in operibus suis. Qui per Jeremiam testatur: Lætabor super eis, quum benefecero ipsis. Itaque poma Dei sunt ipsi fideles, quos profert arbor sapientiæ Christus Dominus, quia regenerat eos in Baptismo: quorum pomorum fructus, sunt boni eorum actus. Poma quoque possunt intelligi dona gratiæ, beneficia ac virtutes, ex quibus procedunt hujusmodi actus.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter Christ called the Church a garden. Conforming herself, then, to this name, the Church invites Christ to enter this garden, that is, into the hearts of the faithful. [[5:1|Let my beloved come into his garden|Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum]]: that is, let him graciously visit me, pouring his gifts into me, preserving, increasing and perfecting them in me. As if the Church were saying: Everyone gladly walks about in his own pleasant and enclosed garden, and takes his rest there with the person dear to him. Let the heavenly Spouse, then, who has called me a garden enclosed, deign to be present with me, and bestow on me consolation, protection, his embrace: for I need his continual and clement presence, and without his gracious help I can do nothing at all. Let him come, then, I beseech, [[5:1|and eat the fruit of his apple trees|ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum]] [Denis has *ut comedat*, "that he may eat"]: that is, let him kindly accept the acts of the faithful and delight in them, and sup and feed with them, since he himself declares in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:20|If any man|Si quis]] [[Apoc 3:20|open to me|aperuerit mihi]], [[Apoc 3:20|I will come in to him and will sup with him|intrabo ad illum, et cœnabo cum eo]]. Of which it is said in Esdras: [[2 Esd 8:10|the joy of the Lord is our strength|Gaudium Domini est fortitudo vestra]] [Denis reads *vestra*, "your strength"]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 103:31|the Lord shall rejoice in his works|Lætabitur Dominus in operibus suis]]. And he testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 32:41|I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|Lætabor super eis, quum benefecero ipsis]]. And so the apples of God are the faithful themselves, whom Christ the Lord, the tree of wisdom, bears, since he regenerates them in Baptism; and the fruit of these apples is their good acts. The apples can also be understood as the gifts of grace, the benefits and virtues, from which such acts proceed.

paras.t: Ad prætactam petitionem sponsus respondet: Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa. Tanquam dicat: Tu invitas me ingredi in hortum meum, id est in te: et ego te invito ingredi hortum meum, id est paradisum cœlestem seu triumphantem Ecclesiam, jam per fidem, spem, contemplationem, et appetitionem ferventem, ut conversatio tua in cœlis sit, et dicas assidue: Quando veniam et apparebo ante faciem Dei? itemque: Domine, dilexi decorem domus tuæ, et locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ. Vel, In hortum meum, id est in cor meum, ita ut per contemplationem et ferventem affectum conjungas te intime mihi. Ideo namque mucrone diræ lanceæ permisi latus meum aperiri, ut ingrediaris per illud in cor meum. Vel, In hortum meum, id est, tu ipsa, o Ecclesia, intra temetipsam, considerando statum, deformationem, indigentiam filiorum tuorum, sicque procedendo ad providam reformationem, instructionem, custodiam filiorum tuorum.
paras.en: To the request just mentioned the Spouse answers: [[5:1|I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse|Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa]] [Denis takes *Veni* as "Come!", an invitation, where the Douay-Rheims reads "I am come"]. As if he were saying: Thou invitest me to enter into my garden, that is, into thee; and I invite thee to enter my garden, that is, the heavenly paradise or the Church triumphant, even now, by faith, hope, contemplation and fervent desire, so that thy conversation may be in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], and thou mayest say continually: [[Ps 41:3|when shall I come and appear before the face of God?|Quando veniam et apparebo ante faciem Dei?]] and again: [[Ps 25:8|I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; and the place where thy glory dwelleth.|Domine, dilexi decorem domus tuæ, et locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ]] Or, [[5:1|into my garden|In hortum meum]], that is, into my heart, so that by contemplation and fervent affection thou mayest join thyself intimately to me. For it was for this that I let my side be opened by the point of the cruel lance[[John 19:34||]], so that through it thou mayest enter into my heart. Or, [[5:1|into my garden|In hortum meum]], that is, thou thyself, O Church, within thyself, considering the state, the deformity and the need of thy children, and so going on to the provident reformation, instruction and guarding of thy children.

paras.t: Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis: id est, spiritualia tibi fercula præparavi, quoniam fructum seu meritum amarissimæ passionis meæ collegi, et posui in thesauro sapientiæ meæ, in incessabili memoria mea, ut tibi ex isto thesauro communicem et succurram, id est, meritis passionis meæ subveniam, gratiam conferendo atque salutem. Messui, inquam, myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis, id est, etiam fructum et merita actuum meorum virtuosorum ex caritatis dulcedine provenientium, prætacto modo collegi, ac pro tua refectione et opere reposui. Etenim tota Christi vita in sæculo isto, fuit meritoria nobis: de cujus plenitudine accipimus universi; et ipse ex plenissima ac suavissima caritate laboravit, egit, oravit pro nobis. Comedi favum meum cum melle meo. Posset hoc accipi, quod Dominus ac Salvator in Cœna proprium corpus divinæ naturæ conjunctum, sub specie Sacramenti suscepit ac manducavit: quod fecit cum melle suo, id est dilectionis et summæ devotionis pinguedine ac dulcore, in quibus incessabiliter fuit, quantum ad superiorem portionem animæ suæ. Denique post resurrectionem, sicut Evangelista fatetur, comedit partem piscis assi et favum mellis. Bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo, id est sanguinem sub specie vini, non in medelam ut ceteri, sed cum omnimoda puritate et innocentia mea: quæ nomine lactis signantur. Hinc dixit in Cœna: Non bibam amplius de hoc genimine vitis, donec bibam illud vobiscum novum in regno Patris mei. Porro spiritualis loquendo, sponsus Ecclesiæ comedit favum cum melle, id est, contemplatione dulcissima propriæ deitatis, atque assumptæ humanitatis mysteriorumque ejus, refecit se ipsum. Bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo, id est, operatione justitiæ meæ, quæ signatur per vinum, ac pietatis atque munditiæ, quæ exprimuntur per lac, animam meam refeci, sicut in Evangelio sum testatus: Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei; et rursum, Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio; itemque, Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper.
paras.en: [[5:1|I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices|Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis]]: that is, I have prepared spiritual dishes for thee, since I have gathered the fruit or merit of my most bitter passion and laid it up in the treasury of my wisdom, in my unceasing memory, so that out of this treasury I may share with thee and succour thee, that is, help thee by the merits of my passion, bestowing grace and salvation. [[5:1|I have gathered|Messui]], I say, [[5:1|my myrrh, with my aromatical spices|myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis]]: that is, I have also gathered in the way just mentioned the fruit and merits of my virtuous acts, which proceeded from the sweetness of charity, and have laid them up for thy refreshment and use. For the whole life of Christ in this world was meritorious for us: [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de cujus plenitudine accipimus universi]]; and he laboured, acted and prayed for us out of the fullest and sweetest charity. [[5:1|I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey|Comedi favum meum cum melle meo]]. This could be taken to mean that our Lord and Saviour at the Supper received and ate his own body, joined to the divine nature, under the species of the Sacrament[[Matt 26:26||]]: and this he did with his honey, that is, with the richness and sweetness of love and of the highest devotion, in which he was unceasingly as to the higher part of his soul. Then too, after the resurrection, as the Evangelist declares, he ate [[Luke 24:42|a piece of a broiled fish and a honeycomb|partem piscis assi et favum mellis]][[Luke 24:43||]]. [[5:1|I have drunk my wine with my milk|Bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo]]: that is, the blood under the species of wine, not as a remedy, as others do, but with my entire purity and innocence, which are signified by the name of milk. Hence he said at the Supper: [[Matt 26:29|I will not drink from henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I shall drink it with you new in the kingdom of my Father|Non bibam amplius de hoc genimine vitis, donec bibam illud vobiscum novum in regno Patris mei]] [Denis reads *donec*, "until", without "that day"]. Speaking more spiritually, again, the Spouse of the Church ate the honeycomb with honey, that is, refreshed himself with the sweetest contemplation of his own Godhead, and of the humanity he assumed and of its mysteries. [[5:1|I have drunk my wine with my milk|Bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo]]: that is, I have refreshed my soul with the working of my justice, which is signified by wine, and of my piety and cleanness, which are expressed by milk; as I testified in the Gospel: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem]] of my Father [the Gospel has "of him that sent me"]; and again: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and likewise: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]].

paras.t: Quidam vero exponunt sic: Messui myrrham meam, id est, sanctos martyres de acerbitate martyrii remuneravi, ac transtuli ad regnum cœleste, cum aromatibus meis, id est cum caritativis et insignibus confessoribus, qui in devotionis sanctæ dulcedine mihi sunt obsecuti. Comedi favum meum, id est, per gratiam et gloriam mihi incorporavi prælatos et prædicatores idoneos, qui cœlestium documentorum refectionem et suavitatem distillaverunt et infuderunt ovibus meis, cum melle meo, id est cum devotis et obedientibus auditoribus eorumdem. Unde dictum est per Joelem: In illa die stillabunt montes dulcedinem, et colles fluent lac et mel. Bibi vinum meum, id est, eos qui in austeritate pœnitentiæ et operibus vitæ activæ exercentur, mihi per incorporationis unionem conjunxi, cum lacte meo, id est cum innocentibus, simplicibus purisque cordibus. Præterea de prælatis et prædicatoribus congrue ait, Comedi: de aliis vero, Bibi. Quod enim comeditur, non ita faciliter deglutitur, sed masticatur ac teritur; quod autem potatur, celerrime absorbetur. Sic eorum qui præsunt et prædicant, conversationem Judex cœlestis districtius discutit, et quidquid mali invenerit, rigorosius punit; alios vero misericordius tractat. Quemadmodum ait Scriptura: Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet; exiguo autem concedetur misericordia.
paras.en: Some, however, expound it thus: [[5:1|I have gathered my myrrh|Messui myrrham meam]], that is, I have rewarded the holy martyrs for the bitterness of their martyrdom and carried them over to the heavenly kingdom, [[5:1|with my aromatical spices|cum aromatibus meis]], that is, with the charitable and distinguished confessors, who have served me in the sweetness of holy devotion. [[5:1|I have eaten the honeycomb|Comedi favum meum]], that is, by grace and glory I have incorporated into myself fit prelates and preachers, who have distilled and poured into my sheep the refreshment and sweetness of heavenly teaching, [[5:1|with my honey|cum melle meo]], that is, with their devout and obedient hearers. Hence it was said through Joel: [[Joel 3:18|in that day|In illa die]] [[Joel 3:18|the mountains shall drop down sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk|stillabunt montes dulcedinem, et colles fluent lac]] and honey. [[5:1|I have drunk my wine|Bibi vinum meum]], that is, I have joined to myself by the union of incorporation those who are exercised in the austerity of penance and in the works of the active life, [[5:1|with my milk|cum lacte meo]], that is, with the innocent, the simple and the pure of heart. Moreover, it is fittingly of the prelates and preachers that he says [[5:1|I have eaten|Comedi]], and of the others [[5:1|I have drunk|Bibi]]. For what is eaten is not swallowed so easily, but is chewed and ground; while what is drunk is taken in very quickly. So the heavenly Judge examines more strictly the conduct of those who govern and preach, and punishes more rigorously whatever evil he finds; but the others he treats more mercifully. As the Scripture says: [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]; [[Wis 6:7|to him that is little, mercy is granted|exiguo autem concedetur misericordia]].

paras.t: Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi. Tanquam dicat: Quia tot spiritualia alimenta vobis paravi, reposui, præbeo, et quoniam eos qui vos præcesserunt Sanctos tam copiose remuneravi; idcirco et vos, qui adhuc estis in isto exsilio, et in via peregrinationis præsentis, reficite animas vestras spiritualibus cibis ac potibus, gratiis et charismatibus, doctrinis atque exemplis meis, ac præcedentium patrum et totius Scripturæ, ecclesiasticis sacramentis, potissime Eucharistiæ sacris mysteriis. At vero ad istam manducationem et potationem non sunt apti, nisi amici mei, qui divina implent præcepta: quibus locutus sum, Vos amici mei estis, si feceritis quæ ego præcipio vobis. Et inebriamini, carissimi: id est, vos, contemplativi et perfecti prælati ac viri heroici, præfatis refectionibus non mediocriter, ut ceteri, sed abundantissime vescamini: ita ut præ caritatis ardore, præ divinarum illuminationum inundatione, ex internæ consolationis plenitudine spiritualiter ebrii sitis, et de vestra exuberantia aliis eructetis, communicetis, et superinfundatis, juxta illud, Memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis tuæ eructabunt: quod ad aliorum pastores ac prædicatores præcipue spectat.
paras.en: [[5:1|eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi]]. As if he were saying: Since I have prepared, laid up and offer you so many spiritual foods, and since I have so plentifully rewarded the Saints who went before you, therefore do you also, who are still in this exile and on the way of the present pilgrimage, refresh your souls with spiritual meats and drinks: with graces and charisms, with my teachings and examples and those of the fathers who went before and of the whole of Scripture, with the sacraments of the Church, and above all with the sacred mysteries of the Eucharist. But none are fit for this eating and drinking except my friends, who fulfil the divine commandments, to whom I said: [[John 15:14|You are my friends, if you do the things that I command you.|Vos amici mei estis, si feceritis quæ ego præcipio vobis]] [[5:1|and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Et inebriamini, carissimi]]: that is, you contemplatives, you perfect prelates and heroic men, feed on the refreshments just named not moderately, as others do, but most abundantly: so that from the ardour of charity, from the flood of divine illuminations, out of the fulness of inward consolation, you may be spiritually drunk, and out of your overflowing may pour forth [*eructetis*, literally "belch forth", the word of the Psalm that follows] to others, share with them and pour over them, according to that saying: [[Ps 144:7|They shall publish the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness|Memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis tuæ eructabunt]]; which concerns above all the pastors and preachers of others.

paras.t: Præterea carissimis suis Deus gloriosus ac adorandus opulentiam suam immensam pandit, communicatque præclarius, eo quod caritas sit virtus communicativa, faciens omnia esse communia. Imo quanto ardentior fuerit, tanto liberaliorem parit communicationem, et ecstasim facit: non sinens diligentem esse sui ipsius dumtaxat, sed transferens ac transformans diligentem in dilectum cum munificentissima utique suarum communione divitiarum. Sicque sponsus, cujus natura est caritas, et qui essentialiter amor est, carissimis suis per limpidissimam illustrationem ostendit se, et suas demonstrat eis divitias, prout in hac vita fieri potest: qui mox tam superserenissimi ac superdeliciosissimi amabilitate objecti, totaliter accenduntur, validissime attrahuntur, et in spiritu fervoris vehementissimi uniuntur eidem, et introducuntur ab ipso in suæ infinitatis oceanum: sicque rapiuntur in divitias gloriæ sponsi, et igne immensi liquefiunt amoris, ac deliquunt a se ipsis, et in superdilectissimo obdormiunt sponso: quem quo clarius contemplantur, eo profundius ac intentius parvipendunt et aspernantur se ipsos. Illi mysticæ unionem atque intuitum theologiæ experientes, medio modo se habere censentur inter comprehensores ac viatores communes: quibus misericordissime datur gustare, quam dulcis sit Dominus, et experiri quam magna et infinita sit multitudo dulcedinis ejus; quos sponsus abscondit in abscondito vultus sui a conturbatione et inquietudine hominum, et protegit eos in tabernaculo suo a contradictione linguarum. In quorum persona dixit Apostolus: Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur a claritate in claritatem, tanquam a Domini Spiritu. Isti igitur sunt non solum amici interni, sed et secretissimi filii Dei et velut consiliarii ac secretarii Dei. De qualibus loquitur Amos, talium unus: Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas.
paras.en: Moreover, to his dearly beloved the glorious and adorable God lays open his immense wealth and shares it more splendidly, because charity is a communicative virtue, making all things common. Indeed, the more ardent it is, the more liberal the sharing it brings forth; and it makes ecstasy [that is, a going out of oneself], not suffering the lover to belong to himself alone, but carrying the lover over and transforming him into the beloved, with a most munificent sharing of all his riches. And so the Spouse, whose nature is charity and who is love in his essence, shows himself to his dearly beloved by a most limpid enlightening, and displays his riches to them, so far as can be done in this life. They at once, by the loveliness of so supremely serene and supremely delightful an object, are wholly set on fire, most powerfully drawn, united to him in a spirit of most vehement fervour, and brought in by him into the ocean of his infinity: and so they are rapt into the riches of the Spouse's glory, melted by the fire of immense love, and fail away from themselves, and fall asleep in the Spouse beloved above all; and the more clearly they contemplate him, the more deeply and intently they make little of themselves and despise themselves. Those who experience the union and the gaze of mystical theology are held to stand midway between the blessed in heaven [*comprehensores*, those who already possess God] and ordinary wayfarers [*viatores*, those still on the way]: to them it is most mercifully given to taste [[1 Pet 2:3|that the Lord is sweet|quam dulcis sit Dominus]], and to experience how great and infinite is the multitude of his sweetness[[Ps 30:20||]]. The Spouse hides them in the secret of his face from the disturbance and disquiet of men, and protects them in his tabernacle [[Ps 30:21|from the contradiction of tongues|a contradictione linguarum]]. In their person the Apostle said: [[2 Cor 3:18|But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with open face, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord|Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur a claritate in claritatem, tanquam a Domini Spiritu]] [Denis reads *Nos autem*, "But we", without "all"]. These, then, are not only inward friends, but also the most intimate sons of God, and as it were the counsellors and secretaries of God. Of such Amos speaks, himself one of them: [[Amos 3:7|the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets|Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas]].

paras.t: Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat. Hoc quidam exponunt in persona Christi, ut sit sensus: Ego dormio, id est, in cœlesti throno ad dexteram Patris glorificatus quiesco; quandoque preces servorum meorum exaudire differo, ita quod videor eis dormire. Consimiliter impiorum scelera ad tempus punire dissimulo: quæ dum districte ulciscor, evigilare perhibeor. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Excitatus est tanquam dormiens Dominus; et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora; et rursus, Exsurge, quare obdormis, Domine? Dormivit etiam Dominus Jesus in triduo sepulturæ in monumento. Dispensative quoque ac voluntarie dormivit interdum in sæculo isto, sicut dum erat super cervical dormiens in navi, et suscitaverunt eum. Verumtamen cor ejus jugiter ac incessabiliter vigilavit, neque ex corporis somno intellectus ejus humanus seu ratio a suo impediebatur actu, usu, judicio: imo in beatifica sine interpolatione fuit fruitione. Insuper vigilat semper, quia non deserit universorum vitam inspicere, nec curam gregis sui unquam relinquit, juxta quod legitur in Psalmo: Ecce non dormitabit neque dormiet, qui custodit Israel. Imo dum preces suorum differt implere, aut peccantium vitia vindicare, cor ejus vigilare asseritur: quia servorum suorum fidelitatem, patientiam, perseverantiam probat, ut tempore opportuno plenius exaudiantur; et pravorum mores ac vitia tolerat, ut convertantur: quod si noluerint, justior appareat eorum damnatio, pietasque divina gloriosius innotescat. Ideo namque dicit Apostolus: Ignoras quia benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit? Secundum duritiam autem tuam, et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die justi judicii Dei. Noli ergo, o sponsa mea Ecclesia, a spe tua deficere, aut frangi adversis, aut pusillanimis effici, dum te ad tempus affligi permitto, exaudireque differo, quia cor meum jugiter vigilat super te.
paras.en: [[5:2|I sleep, and my heart watcheth|Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat]]. Some expound this in the person of Christ, so that the sense is: [[5:2|I sleep|Ego dormio]], that is, glorified on the heavenly throne at the right hand of the Father, I rest; at times I put off hearing the prayers of my servants, so that I seem to them to be asleep. In the same way I for a time forbear to punish the crimes of the wicked; and when I avenge them strictly, I am said to awake. For which reason the Psalmist says: [[Ps 77:65|the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep|Excitatus est tanquam dormiens Dominus]]; [[Ps 77:66|And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts|et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora]]; and again: [[Ps 43:23|Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord?|Exsurge, quare obdormis, Domine?]] The Lord Jesus also slept in the monument for the three days of his burial[[Matt 27:60||]][[Matt 27:63||]][[Matt 27:64||]]. By dispensation, too, and of his own will, he sometimes slept in this world, as when he was [[Mark 4:38|sleeping upon a pillow|super cervical dormiens]] in the ship, and they woke him. Yet his heart watched continually and without ceasing, nor was his human understanding or reason hindered by the sleep of his body from its act, use and judgement: rather, he was in the beatific enjoyment without interruption. Moreover, he watches always, since he never ceases to look upon the life of all, nor ever leaves off the care of his flock, according to what is read in the Psalm: [[Ps 120:4|Behold he shall neither slumber nor sleep, that keepeth Israel.|Ecce non dormitabit neque dormiet, qui custodit Israel]] Indeed, when he puts off fulfilling the prayers of his own, or avenging the vices of sinners, his heart is said to watch: because he proves the faithfulness, patience and perseverance of his servants, so that at the fitting time they may be heard more fully; and he bears with the ways and vices of the wicked, that they may be converted; and if they will not, their damnation may appear the more just, and the divine goodness be made known the more gloriously. For this is why the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:4|Knowest thou not that the benignity of God leadeth thee to penance?|Ignoras quia benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit?]] [[Rom 2:5|But according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up to thyself wrath|Secundum duritiam autem tuam, et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram]] on the day [[Rom 2:5|of the just judgment of God|justi judicii Dei]]. Do not then, O my spouse the Church, fall away from thy hope, or be broken by adversities, or grow faint-hearted, when I let thee be afflicted for a time and put off hearing thee: for my heart watches over thee continually.

paras.t: Amplius, potest hoc verbum in persona Ecclesiæ explanari. Ego dormio: id est, a sponso desuper refecta, atque, ut dictum est, quantum ad perfectiores filios meos inebriata, in ipso Domino, creatore et salvatore meo, per fidem, spem et caritatem quiesco, per contemplationem obdormio, per raptum amplector, per ecstasim quoque in ipsum transformor. Et cor meum vigilat: id est, ex quo nondum plene beata sum, nec diu in tali somno persisto; ideo et in hujusmodi elevatione ecstatica, pro communi salute mea et filiorum meorum sollicite oro, pro generali reformatione fervidissime precor, ac maternæ sollicitudinis vigilias cordiales exercere non negligo. Vel dormit Ecclesia, quantum ad imperfectos, qui frequenter per negligentiam torpent; sed vigilat cor ipsius, id est, perfecti et præsidentes condigni super commissum vigilant gregem, juxta illud in Apocalypsi: Vigila, et confirma cetera quæ moritura erant.
paras.en: Further, this word can be explained in the person of the Church. [[5:2|I sleep|Ego dormio]]: that is, refreshed from on high by the Spouse and, as was said, inebriated as regards my more perfect children, I rest in the Lord himself, my creator and saviour, by faith, hope and charity; I fall asleep by contemplation, I embrace him by rapture, and by ecstasy I am even transformed into him. [[5:2|and my heart watcheth|Et cor meum vigilat]]: that is, since I am not yet fully blessed and do not remain long in such a sleep, therefore even in this ecstatic elevation I pray anxiously for the common salvation of myself and my children, I entreat most fervently for a general reformation, and I do not neglect to keep the heartfelt watches of a mother's care. Or: the Church sleeps as to the imperfect, who are often sluggish through negligence; but her heart watches, that is, the perfect and the worthy rulers watch over the flock entrusted to them, according to that saying in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:2|Be watchful and strengthen the things that remain, which are ready to die|Vigila, et confirma cetera quæ moritura erant]].

paras.t: Deinde subdit Ecclesia, ostendens vigilare se corde: Vox dilecti mei pulsantis, id est, jussio seu admonitio sponsi mei, est ista: Aperi mihi, soror mea, mecum communicans in natura, quam assumpsi, humana, amica mea per mutuum amorem præcipuum, columba mea, ad me simplici et sincera intentione conversa, immaculata mea, quia non habes maculam neque rugam culpæ mortalis, quantum ad perfectiores exsistentes in te, et quoad membra mea per fidem et caritatem; quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium. Apostolus ait, Caput Christi, Deus: sicque Verbum æternum est caput assumptæ humanitatis. Hoc Caput causaliter plenum est rore totius gratiæ, consolationis, ac refrigerii, quia ab illo bonum omne procedit. Rursus caput Christi hominis, est mens sua humana, quæ formaliter plena est omnium supernorum rore charismatum: de quo in Isaia asseritur, Ros tuus, ros lucis. Porro cincinni dicuntur collectiones pilorum in seriem unam: per quos intelliguntur ordinatissimæ cogitationes et affectiones mentis Christi præfatæ: qui dicuntur pleni noctium guttis, id est stillicidiis gratiarum communicabilium seu influxivarum in viatores: quæ comparatione comprehensorum, noctes dicuntur, utpote in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedentes.
paras.en: Then the Church adds, showing that she watches in heart: [[5:2|the voice of my beloved knocking|Vox dilecti mei pulsantis]], that is, the command or admonition of my Spouse is this: [[5:2|Open to me, my sister|Aperi mihi, soror mea]], who sharest with me in the human nature which I have assumed; [[5:2|my love|amica mea]] [*amica*, "friend"], by our mutual and special love; [[5:2|my dove|columba mea]], turned to me with a simple and sincere intention; [[5:2|my undefiled|immaculata mea]], since thou hast neither spot nor wrinkle of mortal sin, as regards the more perfect who are in thee, and as regards those who are my members by faith and charity; [[5:2|for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights|quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium]]. The Apostle says: [[1 Cor 11:3|the head of Christ is God|Caput Christi, Deus]]; and so the eternal Word is the head of the humanity he assumed. This Head is full, as cause, of the dew of all grace, consolation and refreshment, since every good proceeds from it. Again, the head of Christ as man is his human mind, which is full, formally [that is, as possessing it in itself, not only as its cause], of the dew of all heavenly charisms: of which it is said in Isaias: [[Is 26:19|thy dew is the dew of the light|Ros tuus, ros lucis]]. Locks, further, are hairs gathered into a single row: by them are understood the most well-ordered thoughts and affections of that mind of Christ; and they are said to be full of the drops of the nights, that is, of the droppings of the graces that are shared with, or flow into, wayfarers, who in comparison with the blessed in heaven are called nights, as being those [[Luke 1:79|that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death|in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedentes]].

paras.t: Itaque sponsus loquens per modum fervidi amatoris (qui nocturno tempore intemperataque aura ex amoris magnitudine currit ad dilectam, ita quod caput ejus rore perfunditur, et crines ejus imbre rorem sequente, sic quod nec intemperie auræ, nec noctis horrore a tali revocatur itinere), hortatur Ecclesiam, ut sibi aperiat, id est, in cor suum recipiat ipsum sponsum, et omne obstaculum gratiæ a se, omnem obicem inhabitationis divinæ a suis filiis studeat removere: quoniam ipse sponsus toto affectu ad eam accelerat, et gratiam capitis existentem in se, per quam in sua influit membra, paratus omnino est ei communicare, stillasque suorum charismatum membris ejus infundere. Vel ideo ait, Quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium: quoniam ipse in hac vita tempestatibus tribulationum, et pluviis persecutionum amore sponsæ suæ repletus est, quemadmodum protestatur: Intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam; veni in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me. Ideo sponsa debet sibi merito protinus aperire et grata existere.
paras.en: And so the Spouse, speaking after the manner of a fervent lover (who by night and in raw weather runs to his beloved out of the greatness of his love, so that his head is drenched with dew, and his hair with the rain that follows the dew, and yet neither the rawness of the weather nor the dread of the night calls him back from such a journey), exhorts the Church to open to him: that is, to receive the Spouse himself into her heart, and to strive to remove from herself every obstacle to grace, and from her children every bar to the divine indwelling: for the Spouse himself hastens to her with his whole affection, and is altogether ready to share with her the grace of the head that is in him, by which he flows into his members, and to pour the drops of his charisms into her members. Or he says [[5:2|for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights|Quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium]] because in this life, out of love for his spouse, he was filled with the storms of tribulations and the rains of persecutions, as he declares: [[Ps 68:2|the waters are come in even unto my soul|Intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam]]; [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea, and a tempest hath overwhelmed me|veni in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me]]. Therefore the spouse ought rightly to open to him at once and to be grateful.

paras.t: Verumtamen grave est ei, interrupta et suspensa contemplatione sponsi ac amoroso ejus amplexu, exercitiis vitæ occupari activæ, ac emigrare atque discurrere ad præsidendum prædicandumque aliis. Idcirco respondet: Exspoliavi me tunica mea, id est, occupationem circa terrena et exteriora agenda rejeci, ut contemplationi insistam liberius; quomodo induar illa? quasi dicat: Grave mihi videtur occupationem illam laboriosam et anxiam rursus assumere, et implicari terrenis. Lavi pedes meos, id est, affectus meos purgavi a culpis, quæ occasione occupationis hujusmodi contrahi solent; quomodo inquinabo illos? id est, indecens aliqualiter mihi videtur, affectus meos soli summo bono intentos, atque in ipso simplificatos ac fixos, rursus dispergere circa multa, et per hoc contrahere maculam aliquam.
paras.en: Yet it is hard for her, when the contemplation of the Spouse and his loving embrace are broken off and suspended, to be taken up with the exercises of the active life, and to go out and run about ruling and preaching to others. Therefore she answers: [[5:3|I have put off my garment|Exspoliavi me tunica mea]], that is, I have cast off the business of earthly and outward affairs, so as to give myself more freely to contemplation; [[5:3|how shall I put it on?|quomodo induar illa?]] As if she said: It seems hard to me to take up again that laborious and anxious business, and to be entangled in earthly things. [[5:3|I have washed my feet|Lavi pedes meos]], that is, I have cleansed my affections from the faults that are usually contracted on the occasion of such business; [[5:3|how shall I defile them?|quomodo inquinabo illos?]] that is, it seems to me somewhat unbecoming to scatter again about many things my affections, which are intent on the supreme good alone and made simple and fixed in it, and by this to contract some stain.

paras.t: Quid autem ad piam et sapientialem istam querelam fecerit sponsus, subjungit Ecclesia: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, id est, operationem ac opem potestatis suæ secreta inspiratione, seu per vim intellectivam, mihi infudit, me illustravit, accendit et animavit; et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus: id est, mens mea ex hujusmodi infusione et tactu interno, vehementer est admirata, expavit, accensa est. Frequenter autem in Scripturis per ventrem mens designatur: sicut in Psalmo, Ex utero ante luciferum genui te; et iterum, Flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Loquitur autem sponsa instar fervidæ amatricis, quæ ex tactu sponsi tam intente accenditur corde, ut passio sensualis amoris redundet in corpus, et ventrem faciat tremere.
paras.en: What the Spouse did in answer to this devout and wise complaint the Church adds: [[5:4|My beloved put his hand through the key hole|Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen]] [*foramen*, simply "opening" or "hole"], that is, by a secret inspiration, or through the power of the understanding, he poured into me the working and help of his power, enlightened me, set me on fire and quickened me; [[5:4|and my bowels were moved at his touch|et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus]] [*venter*, literally "belly"]: that is, my mind, from such an infusion and inward touch, was greatly amazed, was struck with awe and set on fire. Now in the Scriptures the mind is often signified by the belly: as in the Psalm: [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]; and again: [[John 7:38|Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|Flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]]. The spouse speaks here like a fervent lover, who at the touch of the Spouse is so intensely set on fire in heart that the passion of sensible love overflows into the body and makes the belly tremble.

paras.t: Surrexi, id est, ad obedientiam me accinxi, et a quiete contemplationis ad actum mihi injunctum processi, ut aperirem dilecto meo, id est, ingressui ejus gratioso mentem meam obediendo pararem, corda quoque subditorum hortarer ad removendum a se impedimenta visitationis divinæ: sicut beatissimus quoque Joannes legitur peregisse. Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham: id est, potentiæ meæ operativæ seu actiones virtutum mihi desuper præstitarum, mortificationem carnis salubrem, amaram compunctionem, et dura pœnitentiæ opera assumpserunt, exercuerunt, et docuerunt. Hæc enim (ut patuit) per myrrham, quæ amara ac putrefactionis expulsiva est, designantur.
paras.en: [[5:5|I arose up|Surrexi]], that is, I girded myself for obedience, and went forth from the quiet of contemplation to the work enjoined on me, [[5:5|to open to my beloved|ut aperirem dilecto meo]], that is, so that by obeying I might prepare my mind for his gracious entering, and might also exhort the hearts of those under me to remove from themselves the hindrances to the divine visitation: as the most blessed John too is read to have done[[Matt 3:1||]][[Matt 3:2||]][[Matt 3:3||]]. [[5:5|my hands dropped with myrrh|Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham]]: that is, my working powers, or the acts of the virtues given me from above, have taken up, practised and taught the wholesome mortification of the flesh, bitter compunction and the hard works of penance. For these (as has been shown) are signified by myrrh, which is bitter and drives out putrefaction.

paras.t: Et digiti mei pleni sunt myrrha probatissima. Sicut per manus significatur operatio seu potestas, ita per digitos discretio ac sapientialis directio. Digiti igitur sponsæ pleni sunt probatissima myrrha, id est, discretio et recta ejus intentio, præfatam mortificationem et mortificationis doctrinam, compunctionis amaricationem ac dominicæ passionis imitationem, Deo præcipue placitam exhibent, ut sit prorsus rationabile nostrum obsequium. Itaque myrrha probata, est castigatio carnis assumpta, et crucifixio ejus per pœnitentiæ opera; myrrha probatior, est sensitivi appetitus a suis concupiscentiis et peccatis coercitio; myrrha probatissima, est compunctio seu contritio cordis, abnegatio propriæ voluntatis, consideratio et sequela dominicæ passionis. Hæ myrrhæ corruptionem dissolutionis, vanæ gloriæ, concupiscentiæ, invidiæ, gulæ, obscenitatis excludunt, sanant, abjiciunt: ita quod habens eas, dicere potest cum Ezechia, Ecce in pace amaritudo mea amarissima; et cum Jeremia, A facie manus tuæ, Domine, solus sedebam, quoniam comminatione replesti me.
paras.en: [[5:5|and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh|Et digiti mei pleni sunt myrrha probatissima]] [*probatissima*, literally "most tried" or "most approved"; Denis goes on to grade myrrh as *probata*, *probatior*, *probatissima*: tried, more tried, most tried]. As by the hands is signified working or power, so by the fingers discretion and wise direction. The fingers of the spouse, then, are full of the most tried myrrh: that is, her discretion and right intention make the mortification just named, and the teaching of mortification, the bitterness of compunction and the imitation of the Lord's passion, especially pleasing to God, so that it may be wholly our [[Rom 12:1|reasonable service|rationabile nostrum obsequium]]. And so tried myrrh is the chastisement of the flesh taken up, and its crucifixion by the works of penance; more tried myrrh is the restraining of the sensitive appetite from its concupiscences and sins; the most tried myrrh is compunction or contrition of heart, the denial of one's own will, the consideration and following of the Lord's passion. These myrrhs shut out, heal and cast off the corruption of dissoluteness, vainglory, concupiscence, envy, gluttony and impurity: so that he who has them can say with Ezechias: [[Is 38:17|Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter|Ecce in pace amaritudo mea amarissima]]; and with Jeremias: Because [[Jer 15:17|of the presence of thy hand|A facie manus tuæ]], O Lord, [[Jer 15:17|I sat alone, because thou hast filled me with threats|solus sedebam, quoniam comminatione replesti me]] [Denis joins *a facie manus tuæ*, "before the face of thy hand", to "I sat alone"; the Douay-Rheims joins it to the clause before].

paras.t: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo. Pessulum dicitur lignea sera quæ pellitur, ostium dum seratur : per quod intelligitur divinæ ingressionis obstaculum, ex carne proveniens. Ostium vero est capacitas seu dispositio cordis. Pessulum ergo ostii aperit, qui in servitutem spiritus redigit corpus, et inordinatam ejus appetitionem repellit, quatenus Deus dignetur invisere animam. At ille declinaverat atque transierat : id est, inchoatam visitationem, consolationem, inflammationem, et gratiæ affluentiam subtraxit ad tempus; et quando se obtulit et prævenit, protinus se abscondit, ut quæreretur ardentius, et copiosius inveniretur : sicque aliqualiter habitus, insensibiliter est elapsus.
paras.en: [[5:6|I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved|Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo]]. The bolt is the name for the wooden bar that is driven across when a door is fastened: by it is understood the obstacle to God's coming in, which arises from the flesh. And the door is the capacity or disposition of the heart. So he opens the bolt of the door who brings the body into subjection to the spirit and drives back its disordered craving, so that God may deign to visit the soul. [[5:6|but he had turned aside, and was gone|At ille declinaverat atque transierat]]: that is, for a time he withdrew the visitation, consolation, kindling and abundance of grace that he had begun; and when he had offered himself and come first, he at once hid himself, that he might be sought more ardently and found more abundantly: and so, after being held in some measure, he slipped away imperceptibly.

paras.t: Anima mea liquefacta est, ut dilectus locutus est : id est, mox ut sponsi exhortationem audivi, resoluta est in amorem anima mea, et omnis duritia est ab ea sublata. Nam sicut ignis resolvit plumbum, sic animam amorosam spiritualiter liquefacit flamma dilectionis, atque in fletum compunctionis, compassionis, complacentiæ et abundantis lætitiæ, eam resolvit. Denique, quo habitus caritatis est in aliquo intensior circa personam quamcumque, tanto ex personæ illius adspectu, affatu, auditu, aut recordatione, citius valentiusque accenditur, liquefit, atque resolvitur. Ideo sponsa mox ut memor fit Christi, aut vocem ejus audierit, inflammatur, juxta quod legitur in Psalmo : In meditatione mea exardescet ignis. Ex qua utique liquefactione, quæ fluidum facit, sponsa incitatur ad obtinendum, intuendum, degustandumque ipsum sponsum plenius clariusque quam ante, juxta illud : Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient; et qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient. Nam et spirituales deliciæ quo amplius degustantur, eo avidius cupiuntur. Unde et Beati in patria asseruntur cum desiderio frui Deo, intuerique eum, prout sacratissimus ait princeps Apostolorum : In quem desiderant angeli prospicere. Hinc subditur : Quæsivi, id est, sponsum clarius intueri, suavius degustare, stabilius amplexari desideravi ac studui, et non inveni illum taliter tamque celeriter ut concupivi; vocavi, id est, ferventer rogavi, ut ita se demonstraret mihi, et non respondit mihi, id est, non exaudivit, neque reale responsum donavit mihi juxta desiderium meum.
paras.en: [[5:6|My soul melted when he spoke|Anima mea liquefacta est, ut dilectus locutus est]]: that is, as soon as I heard the exhortation of the spouse, my soul was dissolved into love, and all hardness was taken from it. For as fire melts lead, so the flame of love spiritually melts the loving soul, and dissolves it into tears of compunction, of compassion, of loving delight and of abundant gladness. In short, the more intense the habit of charity is in anyone towards any person, the more quickly and strongly it is kindled, melts and is dissolved at the sight of that person, at speaking with him, hearing him or remembering him. Therefore the bride, as soon as she calls Christ to mind or hears his voice, is set on fire, according to what we read in the Psalm: [[Ps 38:4|in my meditation a fire shall flame out|In meditatione mea exardescet ignis]]. And by this melting, which makes her fluid, the bride is stirred to gain, to behold and to taste the spouse himself more fully and more clearly than before, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 24:29|They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst|Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient; et qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient]]. For spiritual delights, the more they are tasted, the more eagerly they are desired. Hence the Blessed in the fatherland, too, are said to enjoy God and to behold him with desire, as the most holy prince of the Apostles says: [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|In quem desiderant angeli prospicere]]. Hence it is added: [[5:6|I sought him|Quæsivi]], that is, I desired and strove to behold the spouse more clearly, to taste him more sweetly, to embrace him more firmly, [[5:6|and found him not|et non inveni illum]] in such a way and as quickly as I longed; [[5:6|I called|vocavi]], that is, I fervently begged him to show himself so to me, [[5:6|and he did not answer me|et non respondit mihi]], that is, he did not hear me, nor give me a real answer according to my desire.

paras.t: Invenerunt me custodes, qui circumeunt civitatem. Ista consonant his, quæ dicta sunt supra tertio capitulo : Quæsivi illum, et non inveni; invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem. Nempe qui ibi vigiles, hic custodes vocantur. Ideo ex dictis ibidem, patet intelligentia horum; sed hic subduntur, quæ ibi non continentur.
paras.en: [[5:7|The keepers that go about the city found me|Invenerunt me custodes, qui circumeunt civitatem]]. These words agree with what was said above in the third chapter: [[Cant 3:2|I sought him, and I found him not|Quæsivi illum, et non inveni]]; [[Cant 3:3|The watchmen who keep the city, found me|invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem]]. For those who are called watchmen there are here called keepers. So the meaning of these words is plain from what was said there; but here things are added which are not contained there.

paras.t: Percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me. Custodes, id est prælati ac prædicatores, percutiunt Ecclesiam, id est fideles subditos et dociles auditores, dum eorum corda ad compunctionem, ad erubescentiam de peccatis præteritis, ad castigandum se ipsos per opera satisfactionis inducunt: et item, dum eos juste et caritative corripiunt. Sic percusserat sanctissimus Christi Præcursor venientes ad suum baptismum Judæos, dicendo : Genimina viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira? Unde percussi dixerunt : Quid ergo faciemus? Vulnerant quoque eos, quos divini amoris jaculis perforant, quos ad caritatis vehementiam trahunt, ac præcordiali contritionis dolore adimplent. Tulerunt mihi pallium meum custodes murorum: id est, rectores et principes Ecclesiarum abstulerunt a me pristinæ conversationis imperfectionem, ignorantiæ meæ velamen, ac mœroris mei operimentum.
paras.en: [[5:7|they struck me: and wounded me|Percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me]]. The keepers, that is, prelates and preachers, strike the Church, that is, faithful subjects and docile hearers, when they lead their hearts to compunction, to shame for past sins, to chastising themselves by works of satisfaction; and again, when they rebuke them justly and charitably. So the most holy Forerunner of Christ had struck the Jews who came to his baptism, saying: [[Luke 3:7|Ye offspring of vipers, who hath shewed you to flee from the wrath to come?|Genimina viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira?]] Whence, being struck, they said: [[Luke 3:10|What then shall we do?|Quid ergo faciemus?]] [the margin gives Luke 3:12, where the publicans ask; Denis's words are those of the people at Luke 3:10]. They also wound those whom they pierce with the darts of divine love, whom they draw to the vehemence of charity and fill with heartfelt sorrow of contrition. [[5:7|the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me|Tulerunt mihi pallium meum custodes murorum]] [*pallium*: a cloak or mantle; the Douay-Rheims has ‘veil’]: that is, the rulers and princes of the Churches have taken from me the imperfection of my former way of life, the veil of my ignorance and the covering of my grief.

paras.t: Amplius, vitiosi et scandalosi pastores ac prædicatores, verbis et exemplis pestiferis male percutiunt, et læsione peccati ac mortis vulnerant simplices Deum quærentes. Et pallium, id est vestem gratiæ ac virtutis, tollunt ab eis, dum ipsos enormiter scandalizant. De qua percussione ait Apostolus : Peccantes in fratres, et percutientes conscientiam eorum infirmam, in Christum peccatis.
paras.en: Further, vicious and scandalous pastors and preachers strike wrongly with pestilent words and examples, and wound with the hurt of sin and of death the simple who seek God. And they take from them their cloak, that is, the garment of grace and virtue, when they give them grievous scandal. Of this striking the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 8:12|when you sin thus against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ|Peccantes in fratres, et percutientes conscientiam eorum infirmam, in Christum peccatis]] [*percutientes*, ‘wound’, is literally ‘striking’, the word of the Canticle].

paras.t: Præterea, de duplici custodia loquitur Scriptura sacra : videlicet de custodia caritatis et sollicitudinis pastoralis ac justæ diligentiæ, juxta illud, Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite : et iterum, Custodiens parvulos Dominus: et supra, Posuerunt me custodem in vineis. Et rursus de custodia maligne observationis, sicut in Psalmo : Qui custodiebant animam meam, consilium fecerunt in unum, dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum; persequimini et comprehendite eum, quia non est qui eripiat. Hoc modo custodes et observatores Ecclesiæ circumeuntes Ecclesiam, sunt dæmones : quorum unus dixit ad Dominum, Circuivi terram et perambulavi eam. Propter quod et beatissimus Petrus : Adversarius, inquit, vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret. Hi custodes maligni frequenter tentationibus suis percutiunt ac sauciant corda quærentium sponsum. Propter quod oravit Propheta : Custodi me a laqueo quem absconderunt mihi. Et Christus in Evangelio : Deinde (ait) venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde eorum, ne credentes salvi fiant.
paras.en: Moreover, Holy Scripture speaks of a twofold keeping [*custodia*: keeping, guarding or watching, whence *custodes*, ‘keepers’]: namely of the keeping of charity, of pastoral care and of just diligence, according to that saying: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; and again: [[Ps 114:6|The Lord is the keeper of little ones|Custodiens parvulos Dominus]] [the margin gives Ps. cxxiv, 6; the words are Ps 114:6]; and above: [[Cant 1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]. And again of the keeping of malicious watching, as in the Psalm: [[Ps 70:10|they that watched my soul have consulted together|Qui custodiebant animam meam, consilium fecerunt in unum]], [[Ps 70:11|Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, for there is none to deliver him|dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum; persequimini et comprehendite eum, quia non est qui eripiat]]. In this way the keepers and watchers of the Church, who go about the Church, are the demons, one of whom said to the Lord: [[Job 1:7|I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it|Circuivi terram et perambulavi eam]]. For which reason blessed Peter too says: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary|Adversarius]], he says, [[1 Pet 5:8|the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]. These malicious keepers often strike and wound with their temptations the hearts of those who seek the spouse. For which reason the Prophet prayed: [[Ps 140:9|Keep me from the snare, which they have laid for me|Custodi me a laqueo quem absconderunt mihi]]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[Luke 8:12|then|Deinde]] (he says) [[Luke 8:12|the devil cometh and taketh the word out of their heart, lest believing they should be saved|venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde eorum, ne credentes salvi fiant]].

paras.t: Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, o particulares Ecclesiæ seu animæ virtuosæ, si inveneritis dilectum meum, id est, si specialem aliquam devotionem, contemplationem, visitationem, a sponso susceperitis, et ei gratiose conjunctæ fueritis; ut annuntietis ei, quia amore langueo, id est, ut ferventer oretis pro me, profitendo in orationibus vestris desiderium meum ad sponsum, quod adeo magnum est, ut præ vehementia suæ desideratæ præsentiæ valde affligar : quæ afflictio, langor amoris, juxta præhabita nuncupatur. Dicitur autem aliquid Deo annuntiari, non quasi ignoranti, sed ut Domino omnia cognoscenti, ut humili recognitione ab eo aliqua impetrentur. Vult ergo universalis Ecclesia a particularibus Ecclesiis et filiabus suis et a devotis personis orari pro se, pro reformatione communi in omni statu et politia, et pro finali universorum salute.
paras.en: [[5:8|I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem|Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem]], O particular Churches or virtuous souls, [[5:8|if you find my beloved|si inveneritis dilectum meum]], that is, if you receive from the spouse some special devotion, contemplation or visitation, and are graciously joined to him; [[5:8|that you tell him that I languish with love|ut annuntietis ei, quia amore langueo]], that is, that you pray fervently for me, declaring in your prayers my desire for the spouse, which is so great that I am sorely afflicted through the vehemence of my longing for his presence: which affliction is called the languor of love, as was said before. Now a thing is said to be told to God, not as to one who does not know it, but as to the Lord who knows all things, so that by humble acknowledgement something may be obtained from him. So the universal Church wishes to be prayed for by the particular Churches and her daughters and by devout persons: for herself, for the common reform in every state and commonwealth, and for the final salvation of all.

paras.t: Videns autem Synagoga conversa, seu sanctus quicumque, et præsertim filiæ Jerusalem, Ecclesiam ex gentilitate conversam, tam spiritualem, ferventem et speciosam, quæritur non ex ignorantia, sed præ admiratione, et ut audiat responsum notabile pro communi instructione : Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum? id est, o sponsa Ecclesia gentium, præ cunctis gentibus formosa, sancta, electa, dic qualis est sponsus tuus tibi tam carus, et ex dilecto procedens, id est, ex Patre æterno super omnia creata incomparabiliter diligendo æternaliter genitus. Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto (sicut expositum est), id est, quam pulcher, amabilis, elegans, et excellens? quia sic adjurasti nos, id est, quia tam ardentissime diligis eum, quod langues ejus amore, atque ob hoc nos adjurasti, ut si inveniremus eum, annuntiemus ei quod taliter langues.
paras.en: Now the converted Synagogue, or any saint, and especially the daughters of Jerusalem, seeing the Church converted from the Gentiles so spiritual, so fervent and so beautiful, asks, not from ignorance but from wonder, and so as to hear a notable answer for the instruction of all: [[5:9|What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women?|Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum?]] that is, O bride, Church of the Gentiles, fair, holy and chosen above all nations, tell us what manner of one is thy spouse, who is so dear to thee and proceeds *of the beloved*, that is, is begotten eternally of the eternal Father, who is to be loved incomparably above all created things. [[5:9|what manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved|Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto]] (as has been explained), that is, how fair, how lovely, how elegant and excellent? [[5:9|that thou hast so adjured us|quia sic adjurasti nos]], that is, because thou lovest him so very ardently that thou languishest with love of him, and for this hast adjured us, that if we should find him we should tell him that thou languishest so.

paras.t: Ad hoc respondet Ecclesia : Dilectus meus candidus : quia secundum suam divinam naturam est lux, puritas, pulchritudo immensa, ex Patre æterno se ipsum æternaliter intelligente, et conceptum suum invariabiliter intra se proferente, emanans ac genitus, splendor gloriæ, character paternæ substantiæ, candor lucis æternæ; et rubicundus, secundum naturam assumptam : utpote speciosus forma præ filiis hominum, qui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus; et in passione sua rubore proprii cruoris perfusus, factus est rubicundus, sicut Jacob patriarcha prædixit : Lavabit in vino stolam suam, et in sanguine uvæ pallium suum. Unde fertur in Isaia : Quare ergo rubrum est indumentum tuum?
paras.en: To this the Church answers: [[5:10|My beloved is white|Dilectus meus candidus]], because according to his divine nature he is light, purity, immense beauty, issuing and begotten from the eternal Father, who understands himself eternally and utters his concept unchangeably within himself: the brightness of glory, the figure of the Father's substance, the brightness of eternal light [phrases of Heb 1:3 and Wis 7:26; *candor*, ‘brightness’, is literally ‘whiteness’, answering to *candidus*, ‘white’]; [[5:10|and ruddy|et rubicundus]], according to the nature he assumed: as being [[Ps 44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]], [[1 Pet 2:22|Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth|qui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]]; and in his passion, drenched in the redness of his own blood, he was made ruddy, as the patriarch Jacob foretold: [[Gen 49:11|He shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape|Lavabit in vino stolam suam, et in sanguine uvæ pallium suum]]. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 63:2|Why then is thy apparel red|Quare ergo rubrum est indumentum tuum]]?

paras.t: Electus ex millibus, id est præ universis et singulis : qui secundum naturam assumptam prædestinatus est Filius Dei in virtute, secundum Apostolum ad Romanos. De quo sanctus evangelista Matthæus ex Isaia allegat : Ecce puer meus quem elegi; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea. Unde in passione dixerunt iniqui : Si rex Israel est, et, Si hic est Christus Dei electus, descendat de cruce.
paras.en: [[5:10|chosen out of thousands|Electus ex millibus]], that is, above all and each: he who according to the nature he assumed [[Rom 1:4|was predestinated the Son of God in power|prædestinatus est Filius Dei in virtute]], according to the Apostle to the Romans. Of him the holy evangelist Matthew alleges from Isaias: [[Matt 12:18|Behold my servant whom I have chosen|Ecce puer meus quem elegi]]; [[Is 42:1|my elect, my soul delighteth in him|electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]]. Whence in the passion the wicked said: [[Matt 27:42|If he be the king of Israel|Si rex Israel est]], and, [[Luke 23:35|if he be Christ, the elect of God|Si hic est Christus Dei electus]], let him [[Matt 27:42|come down from the cross|descendat de cruce]].

paras.t: Caput ejus aurum optimum : id est, mens ejus sapientissima, est omni sapientia ac caritate plenissima : quorum utrumque significatur per aurum, juxta illud Apocalypsis, Suadeo tibi emere aurum ignitum probatum. Vel, Caput ejus aurum optimum, id est, pretiosissima aurea corona in capite ejus. Item, Caput ejus, id est deitas sua, seu Deus Pater, qui caput est Christi; est optimum aurum, id est præstantissimum entium, cujus respectu, omne creatum est vile ac modicum, sicut aurum cetera excedit metalla.
paras.en: [[5:11|His head is as the finest gold|Caput ejus aurum optimum]]: that is, his most wise mind is most full of all wisdom and charity, both of which are signified by gold, according to that saying of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy|Suadeo tibi emere]] [[Apoc 3:18|gold, fire tried|aurum ignitum probatum]]. Or, [[5:11|His head is as the finest gold|Caput ejus aurum optimum]], that is, a most precious golden crown is upon his head. Again, [[5:11|His head|Caput ejus]], that is, his Godhead, or God the Father, who is the head of Christ[[1 Cor 11:3||]], is [[5:11|the finest gold|optimum aurum]], that is, the most excellent of beings, in comparison with whom every created thing is vile and small, as gold surpasses the other metals.

paras.t: Comæ ejus, sicut elatæ palmarum : id est, cæsaries capillorum ipsius assimilatur foliis palmarum, non deorsum pendentibus, sed sursum elevatis : propter quod dicuntur elatæ, quasi elevatæ; nigræ quasi corvus, id est, protestantes grandem vigorem et immarcescibilitatem esse in sponso : secundum quod pilorum nigredo ostendit fortitudinem ac juventutem esse in taliter capillato. Porro per comam sponsi, intelligi possunt congeries cogitationum affectionumque ejus, quæ semper erant præclarissimæ, ad Deum erectæ, ordinatæ, perfectæ, ostendentes in ipso esse universarum robur virtutum ac virilem ætatem, de cetero nullatenus marcescentes. Rursus, per comam sponsi, intelliguntur vel prælati atque vicarii ejus, ei prælatica potestate propinquiores, sicut coma immediate ex capite generatur et ei inhæret. Gregorius tamen per comas Christi, intelligit generaliter ipsos fideles, per fidem et caritatem Christo ut capiti inhærentes, et quæ sursum sunt quærentes ac sapientes : sicque de suæ salutis hostibus triumphantes, sicut palmæ ascendunt in altum, et sua significatione ostendunt triumphum.
paras.en: [[5:11|his locks as branches of palm trees|Comæ ejus, sicut elatæ palmarum]]: that is, the growth of his hair is likened to the leaves of palms, not hanging down but raised upward: for which reason they are called *elatæ*, as if to say ‘elevated’ [*elatæ palmarum* is literally ‘the raised (fronds) of palms’; the Douay-Rheims has ‘branches’]; [[5:11|black as a raven|nigræ quasi corvus]], that is, declaring that there is great vigour and unfading freshness in the spouse: inasmuch as blackness of hair shows strength and youth in one who has such hair. Further, by the locks of the spouse may be understood the gathered mass of his thoughts and affections, which were always most excellent, raised up to God, ordered and perfect, showing that in him is the strength of all the virtues and the age of full manhood, and never withering thereafter. Again, by the locks of the spouse are understood his prelates and vicars, who are nearer to him by their prelatical power, as the hair grows immediately from the head and clings to it. Gregory, however, by the locks of Christ understands the faithful in general, who cling to Christ as to their head by faith and charity, and seek and savour the things that are above[[Col 3:1||]][[Col 3:2||]]: and so, triumphing over the enemies of their salvation, they rise on high like palms, and by what the palm signifies they show forth triumph.

paras.t: Oculi ejus sicut columbæ super rivos aquarum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima. In Christo sunt oculi deitatis, juxta illud, Oculi Domini super justos; et alibi, Oculi Domini multo lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias filiorum hominum. Illi oculi, sunt intellectus et sapientia Dei, seu pietatis suæ respectus : et oculis columbarum possunt assimilari, quoniam simplicissimi sunt atque purissimi, ab omni malitia alienissimi. Unde et Spiritus Sanctus in forma columbæ voluit apparere. Oculi quoque interiores humanitatis Christi, videlicet ratio et intellectus, sapientia et scientia ejus infusæ, omni utique columbina simplicitate fuerunt persplendidi, et omni sinceritate plenissimi. Sed et exteriores oculi ejus vino fuerunt puriores ac pulchriores: in quibus interna simplicitas resplenduit columbina, et omni pudicitia erant ornati, non vagi, sed venustissima compositione facti.
paras.en: [[5:12|His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams|Oculi ejus sicut columbæ super rivos aquarum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima]]. In Christ are the eyes of the Godhead, according to that saying: [[Ps 33:16|The eyes of the Lord are upon the just|Oculi Domini super justos]]; and elsewhere: [[Ecclus 23:28|the eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men|Oculi Domini multo lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias filiorum hominum]]. Those eyes are the understanding and wisdom of God, or the regard of his loving-kindness: and they can be likened to the eyes of doves, since they are most simple and most pure, utterly far from all malice. Hence the Holy Ghost too willed to appear in the form of a dove. The inner eyes of Christ's humanity also, namely his reason and understanding, his infused wisdom and knowledge, were resplendent with all dovelike simplicity and most full of all sincerity. And his outward eyes, too, were purer and fairer than wine [an echo of Gen 49:12, ‘his eyes are more beautiful than wine’]: in them the inner dovelike simplicity shone out, and they were adorned with all modesty, not wandering, but most gracefully composed.

paras.t: Itaque omnes hi oculi sponsi, sunt sicut columbæ exsistentes super rivos aquarum, id est juxta aquas fluentes : per quas abundantia sapientiæ, exuberantia gratiæ, puritas, opulentia, communicabilitas, designantur. Quæ perfectissime fuerunt in Christo et in oculis ejus, vel per identitatem aut causalitatem, aut per inhærentiam, aut per resplendentiam : quia in increatis oculis ejus fuerunt per essentialem identitatem seu causalitatem, in intellectualibus autem oculis suæ humanitatis fuerunt per inhæsionem formalem ; sed in corporalibus ejus oculis erant per resplendentiam ac resultantiam quamdam, prout interior dispositio cordis relucet in vultu et oculis, juxta illud : In facie prudentis lucet sapientia. Quæ columbæ lacte sunt lotæ, id est albæ et candidæ instar lactis, quoniam tales sunt gratiosiores. Et sicut universi oculi Christi sunt congruo sibi candore perlucidi, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima, juxta quæ libenter sedent columbæ, quatenus in eis cernant imagines rapacium avium, sicque super aquas se projiciendo, evadant ungues illarum : sic interiores oculi animæ Christi, semper juncti fuerunt plenissimæ exuberantiæ sapientiæ et opulentiæ increatæ : in qua conspiciebant cuncta futura, dæmonumque insidias, a quibus præcavebat suis electis ; imo et Judæorum insidiantium sibi evasit manus usque ad tempus suæ passioni præordinatum.
paras.en: So all these eyes of the spouse are [[5:12|as doves|sicut columbæ]] that are [[5:12|upon brooks of waters|super rivos aquarum]], that is, beside flowing waters: by which are signified abundance of wisdom, overflowing of grace, purity, wealth and the power of imparting itself. These were most perfectly in Christ and in his eyes, whether by identity or causality, or by inherence, or by shining forth: for in his uncreated eyes they were by essential identity or causality, in the intellectual eyes of his humanity by formal inherence, but in his bodily eyes by a certain shining forth and reflection, as the inner disposition of the heart shines out in the face and the eyes, according to that saying: [[Prov 17:24|Wisdom shineth in the face of the wise|In facie prudentis lucet sapientia]]. Which doves [[5:12|are washed with milk|lacte sunt lotæ]], that is, white and bright like milk, since such are more pleasing. And so all the eyes of Christ are bright with a whiteness befitting them [the Latin has *sicut*, ‘as’; the sense seems to want *sic*, ‘so’]; [[5:12|and sit beside the plentiful streams|et resident juxta fluenta plenissima]], beside which doves gladly sit, so as to see in them the images of birds of prey, and so, by throwing themselves upon the waters, to escape their claws: so the inner eyes of Christ's soul were always joined to the most full abundance of uncreated wisdom and wealth, in which they beheld all things to come and the snares of the demons, against which he guarded his elect; nay, he even escaped the hands of the Jews who lay in wait for him until the time foreordained for his passion.

paras.t: Amplius possunt per oculos sponsi, doctores, prædicatores et prælati intelligi : qui aliis vident ac monstrant necessaria ad salutem ; et sedent super rivos aquarum, id est ecclesiastica sacramenta, ex quibus gratiarum munera profluunt, et juxta libros divinæ Scripturæ, in quibus jugiter occupantur; et columbina simplicitate ornantur. Sicque rivulos sapientiæ hauriunt ex Scripturis ; et gratia baptismali virtutibusque infusis seu per contritionem, tanquam lacte, sunt loti, atque a vitiis emundati ; et resident juxta fluenta plenissima, id est Testamentum utrumque, et juxta universos catholicorum libros doctorum, ac redundantiam ecclesiasticorum sacramentorum, donisque gratiæ, non propriis viribus, innituntur. In Scripturis quoque considerant versutias dæmonum, impugnationesque vitiorum, a quibus secundum Scripturarum doctrinam præcavent sibi ac aliis.
paras.en: Further, by the eyes of the spouse may be understood doctors, preachers and prelates, who see for others and show them what is needful for salvation; and they sit [[5:12|upon brooks of waters|super rivos aquarum]], that is, the sacraments of the Church, from which the gifts of graces flow forth, and beside the books of divine Scripture, with which they are continually occupied; and they are adorned with dovelike simplicity. And so they draw little streams of wisdom from the Scriptures; and by baptismal grace and infused virtues, or by contrition, they are washed as with milk and cleansed from vices; and they [[5:12|sit beside the plentiful streams|resident juxta fluenta plenissima]], that is, both Testaments, and all the books of the catholic doctors, and the overflowing abundance of the Church's sacraments; and they rest upon the gifts of grace, not upon their own strength. In the Scriptures too they consider the wiles of the demons and the assaults of the vices, against which they guard themselves and others according to the teaching of the Scriptures.

paras.t: Genæ illius sicut areolæ aromatum, consitæ a pigmentariis. Areolæ dicuntur areæ parvæ, ut hortus aut aliquod spatium modicum : quæ consitæ a pigmentariis, id est seminatæ ac complantatæ a cultoribus aptis, valde sunt pulchræ et delectabiles ad videndum, dum aromaticæ herbæ inibi seminatæ aut plantatæ, egrediuntur ac virent. Sic genæ sponsi, formosæ sunt atque ad intuendum jucundæ. Quod et de corporalibus ejus genis verificatur ; potius tamen de genis mentis, id est de memoria ac providentia animæ Christi, inter quas intellectus seu consideratio præsentium mediat, sicut os inter genas corporeas. Porro anima Christi, universa præterita, præsentia et futura cognovit : ideo genæ ejus multiplici fulgore radiabant notitiæ. Quidam per genas Christi, intelligunt martyres sanctos, qui instar genarum, rubore fulserunt martyrii. Alii per genas ejus, suam humilitatem et pudicissimum apparatum in exteriori conversatione intelligunt.
paras.en: [[5:13|His cheeks are as beds of aromatical spices set by the perfumers|Genæ illius sicut areolæ aromatum, consitæ a pigmentariis]]. *Areolæ* [beds] are small plots, such as a garden or some small space: which, [[5:13|set by the perfumers|consitæ a pigmentariis]], that is, sown and planted by skilled growers, are very beautiful and delightful to look at when the aromatic herbs sown or planted there come up and grow green. So the cheeks of the spouse are fair and pleasant to behold. This is true of his bodily cheeks too; but rather of the cheeks of the mind, that is, of the memory and the foresight of Christ's soul, between which the understanding or consideration of present things stands in the middle, as the mouth between the bodily cheeks. Now the soul of Christ knew all things past, present and to come: therefore his cheeks shone with a manifold radiance of knowledge. Some understand by the cheeks of Christ the holy martyrs, who like cheeks shone with the redness of martyrdom. Others understand by his cheeks his humility and his most modest bearing in his outward conduct.

paras.t: Labia ejus lilia (vel, ut alii legunt, Labia autem) distillantia myrrham primam : id est, interiora exterioraque labia sponsi, saluberrima documenta proposuerunt ad refrenandum se a putrefactione culparum, et ad amplectendum mortificationem iniquitatum, amaritudinem contritionis, dolorem compunctionis. Propterea comparantur myrrhæ primæ seu optimæ, quæ sponte, non ex incisione, emanat, sicut præhabitum est.
paras.en: [[5:13|His lips are as lilies|Labia ejus lilia]] (or, as others read, *But his lips*) [[5:13|dropping choice myrrh|distillantia myrrham primam]]: that is, the inner and outer lips of the spouse set forth most wholesome teachings for restraining oneself from the corruption of sins, and for embracing the mortification of iniquities, the bitterness of contrition, the sorrow of compunction. Therefore they are compared to the first or best myrrh [*myrrha prima*, literally ‘first myrrh’, the Douay-Rheims ‘choice myrrh’], which flows of its own accord, not from a cut, as was said before.

paras.t: Manus illius tornatiles, id est celeriter mobiles, aureæ, plenæ hyacinthis. Per manus Christi, intelliguntur ejus opera virtuosa ac miraculosa, ad quæ peragenda expeditissimus ac efficacissimus fuit ad libitum suum : quæ aurea exstiterunt, id est excellentissima, atque ex ardentissima caritate manantia, et instar auri delectabilia ad videndum ac speciosa, quia nil culpæ fuit eis admixtum ; eratque plena hyacinthis, id est gemmis sic dictis, seu floribus, id est sapientialibus documentis, venustissimis moribus, et rationabilissimis ac utilissimis causis, propter quas fiebant a sponso, videlicet, ad Dei Patris honorem, ad supernaturalis doctrinæ ac fidei confirmationem, ac totius mundi conversionem atque salutem.
paras.en: [[5:14|His hands are turned|Manus illius tornatiles]] [*tornatiles*: ‘turned’, as on a lathe], that is, swift in moving, [[5:14|and as of gold, full of hyacinths|aureæ, plenæ hyacinthis]]. By the hands of Christ are understood his works of virtue and of miracle, in the doing of which he was most ready and most effective at his pleasure: which were golden, that is, most excellent, flowing from most ardent charity, and like gold delightful to look on and beautiful, because no fault was mingled with them; and they were full of hyacinths, that is, of the gems so called, or of flowers, that is, of teachings of wisdom, of most graceful conduct, and of the most reasonable and most useful causes for which they were done by the spouse: namely, for the honour of God the Father, for the confirmation of supernatural doctrine and of faith, and for the conversion and salvation of the whole world.

paras.t: Venter illius eburneus, distinctus sapphiris. Ebur, secundum Anselmum, est os elephantis, qui est castissimum animal frigidi sanguinis : super cujus os ignis (ut fertur) accendi non valet ; atque (ut dicitur) si alicujus viscera ardore libidinis aut alterius infirmitatis ferverent, potato sanguine elephantis, relevamen acciperent. Itaque per ventrem Christi, ejus mortalitas, et naturalis, quam assumpsit, infirmitas designatur : sed hæc fuit eburnea, id est omni castitate et virtutum constantia decorata ; distincta quoque sapphiris, id est cœlestibus ac supernis operibus. Sapphirus quippe lapis est pretiosus, ætherei seu cœlestis coloris.
