Potest quoque per ventrem Christi eburneum, sapphiris fulcitum, solidissima atque purissima mens ejus intelligi, quia per ventrem solet mens significari. Rursus, venter sponsi, est amplissima ejus capacitas et occultatio incomprehensibilium judiciorum ipsius, quæ in eo quasi in ventre latent.
paras.en: [[5:14|His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires|Venter illius eburneus, distinctus sapphiris]]. Ivory, according to Anselm, is the bone of the elephant, which is a most chaste animal, of cold blood: on its bone, so it is said, fire cannot be kindled; and, as they say, if anyone's bowels were burning with the heat of lust or of some other sickness, they would find relief by drinking an elephant's blood. So by the belly of Christ is signified his mortality, and the natural weakness which he assumed: but this was of ivory, that is, adorned with all chastity and constancy of the virtues; and [[5:14|set with sapphires|distincta quoque sapphiris]] too, that is, with heavenly and supernal works. For the sapphire is a precious stone of an ethereal or heavenly colour. By the ivory belly of Christ, furnished with sapphires, may also be understood his most solid and most pure mind, since the mind is often signified by the belly. Again, the belly of the spouse is his most ample capacity and the hiddenness of his incomprehensible judgements, which lie hidden in him as in a belly.

paras.t: Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ, quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas. Crura sponsi sunt firma et inviolabilia mysteria ejus, quibus processit ad redimendum genus humanum : ideo columnis marmoreis, quæ valde sunt fortes, assimilantur. Et fundata sunt super bases aureas, id est super beatissimæ Trinitatis sapientissimum piissimumque consilium et decretum, voluntatem ac omnipotentiam, de humani generis redemptione per Christum : quibus innituntur, et quorum judicio ac virtute facta et impleta sunt illa mysteria, scilicet incarnatio, generatio ex Virgine, conversatio in hoc mundo, passio, resurrectio, ascensio. Possunt quoque per crura Christi, intelligi gloriosi Apostoli : qui prædicando tulerunt Dominum Jesum ad omnes terminos mundi ; quibus præcepit, Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ ; qui per Spiritum Sanctum instar marmorearum columnarum constantissimi insuperabilesque fuerunt. Et super aureas bases erant fundati, id est super dona charismatum Christi, et super miracula ac doctrinas ipsius; vel super Scripturas legis ac Prophetarum. Unde dixit Salvator : Si crederetis Moysi, crederetis forsitan et mihi : de me enim ille scripsit. Princeps quoque Apostolorum : Habemus, inquit, firmiorem propheticum sermonem, cui benefacitis intendentes tanquam lucernæ ardenti. Rursus, crura sponsi, sunt sapientia et omnipotentia ejus, qui totum universum sustentat, portans (juxta Apostolum) omnia verbo, id est præcepto, virtutis suæ : sicut ait Psalmista, Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit.
paras.en: [[5:15|His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold|Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ, quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas]]. The legs of the spouse are his firm and inviolable mysteries, by which he went forth to redeem the human race: therefore they are likened to pillars of marble, which are very strong. And they [[5:15|are set upon bases of gold|fundata sunt super bases aureas]], that is, upon the most wise and most loving counsel and decree, the will and almighty power of the most blessed Trinity concerning the redemption of the human race through Christ: on which they rest, and by whose judgement and power those mysteries were done and fulfilled, namely the incarnation, the birth from the Virgin, his life in this world, the passion, the resurrection, the ascension. By the legs of Christ may also be understood the glorious Apostles, who by preaching carried the Lord Jesus to all the ends of the world; whom he commanded: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and who through the Holy Ghost were most constant and unconquerable, like pillars of marble. And they were founded upon bases of gold, that is, upon the gifts of the charisms of Christ, and upon his miracles and teachings; or upon the Scriptures of the Law and the Prophets. Whence the Saviour said: [[John 5:46|if you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also: for he wrote of me|Si crederetis Moysi, crederetis forsitan et mihi : de me enim ille scripsit]]. And the prince of the Apostles: [[2 Pet 1:19|we have|Habemus]], he says, [[2 Pet 1:19|the more firm prophetical word: whereunto you do well to attend, as to a light that shineth|firmiorem propheticum sermonem, cui benefacitis intendentes tanquam lucernæ ardenti]]. Again, the legs of the spouse are his wisdom and almighty power, for he sustains the whole universe, [[Heb 1:3|upholding|portans]] (as the Apostle says) [[Heb 1:3|all things by the word|omnia verbo]], that is, by the command, [[Heb 1:3|of his power|virtutis suæ]]: as the Psalmist says, [[Ps 148:6|he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away|Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit]] [*præceptum*, ‘decree’, is the word Denis has just used for ‘command’].

paras.t: Species ejus ut Libani : id est, pulchritudo ejus monti Libano pulcherrimo assimilatur : qui mons arboribus valde sublimibus ac odoriferis consitus est. Sic sponsus altissimus odorisque optimi exstat, in quo omnes Sancti fundantur ac sustentantur. Electus ut cedri, id est, inter Sanctos præfulgens ac eminens, quemadmodum cedrus inter ligna plura et arbores. Cedrus autem est arbor valde excelsa, imputribilis, odorifera et præclara, ut dictum est sæpe.
paras.en: [[5:15|His form as of Libanus|Species ejus ut Libani]]: that is, his beauty is likened to Mount Libanus, which is most beautiful, a mountain planted with very lofty and fragrant trees. So the spouse stands forth most high and of the sweetest fragrance, he in whom all the Saints are founded and sustained. [[5:15|excellent as the cedars|Electus ut cedri]] [*electus*, ‘chosen’, as in v. 10], that is, shining forth and eminent among the Saints, as the cedar among many woods and trees. Now the cedar is a very lofty tree, incorruptible, fragrant and splendid, as has often been said.

paras.t: Guttur illius suavissimum. Per guttur verba promuntur, et voces emittuntur. Idcirco per guttur Christi, doctrina ejus accipitur : quæ vere dulcissima est. Per guttur quoque cibaria trajiciuntur in alvum, et incorporantur. Sicque per guttur sponsi, potest intelligi benignitas ejus, qua electos in via per gratiam, atque in patria per gloriam, sibi incorporat : quod guttur prorsus infinitæ consistit dulcedinis. Sed et guttur ejus, quo post resurrectionem in Apostolos insufflavit Spiritum Sanctum, dulce est valde. Et totus desiderabilis : quia secundum deitatis suæ naturam, est naturaliter et penitus infinite appetibilis atque amabilis, delectabilis et jucundus, utpote bonitas pura ac incircumscripta, substantialiter felix, et interminabiliter gloriosa, imo ipsa beatitudo immensa. Secundum naturam quoque assumptam, universis et singulis puris creaturis desiderabilior præstantiorque consistit, eo quod sua humanitas sit ad hypostaticum esse Verbi æterni assumpta, et in illo suppositata.
paras.en: [[5:16|His throat most sweet|Guttur illius suavissimum]]. Through the throat words are brought forth and sounds sent out. Therefore by the throat of Christ his teaching is understood, which is truly most sweet. Through the throat, too, food is passed into the belly and incorporated. And so by the throat of the spouse may be understood his kindness, by which he incorporates the elect into himself, on the way by grace and in the fatherland by glory: and this throat is of a sweetness altogether infinite. And his throat too, with which after the resurrection he breathed the Holy Ghost upon the Apostles[[John 20:22||]], is very sweet. [[5:16|and he is all lovely|Et totus desiderabilis]] [*desiderabilis*, literally ‘desirable’]: because according to the nature of his Godhead he is by nature and wholly, infinitely, to be desired and loved, delightful and pleasant, being pure and uncircumscribed goodness, substantially happy and endlessly glorious, nay, immense beatitude itself. According to the nature he assumed, too, he is more desirable and more excellent than all and each of mere creatures, since his humanity was assumed into the hypostatic being of the eternal Word and subsists in him [*suppositata*: having the Word as its ‘supposit’, that is, as the person in whom it subsists].

paras.t: Talis est dilectus meus, et ipse est amicus meus, o filiæ Jerusalem. Quamvis enim sit Dominus, rex, creator et judex meus, caritatis tamen vehementia impellente, fiduciamque præstante, confidenter voco eum amicum, tanquam carissimum sponsum, qui prior dilexit me, et tam gratiose ac familiariter conjunxit se mihi, et dixit : Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos. Merito igitur laudo eum, et ejus langueo caritate, nec alibi quam in eo possum quiescere.
paras.en: [[5:16|such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Talis est dilectus meus, et ipse est amicus meus, o filiæ Jerusalem]]. For though he is my Lord, king, creator and judge, yet, since the vehemence of charity drives me on and gives me confidence, I boldly call him friend, as my dearest spouse, who first loved me[[1 John 4:10||]][[1 John 4:19||]], and joined himself to me so graciously and familiarly, and said: [[John 15:15|I will not now call you servants|Jam non dicam vos servos]], but [[John 15:15|friends|amicos]]. Rightly therefore do I praise him, and languish with love of him, and nowhere but in him can I find rest.

5.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM CAPITULI QUINTI, DE SPONSO ET ANIMA VIRTUOSA.
5.title_en: Explanation of the same fifth chapter: of the Bridegroom and the virtuous soul

paras.t: Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Variis modis visitat sponsus ille cœlestis animam sibi devotam : quia interdum quasi nondum rogatus adest, ac prævenit, et tanquam saliens celerrime advenit, ut caritatem et pietatem suam demonstret ; interdum quasi occultat ac subtrahit se, ne anima prosperitate spiritualium suorum successive extollatur, aut sibi adscribat quod Dei est, sed propriam debilitatem advertat, seque humiliet, et suspirando, orando, laborando pro gratiæ incremento, copiosius mercatur.
paras.en: [[5:1|Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees|Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum]]. In various ways does that heavenly Bridegroom visit the soul devoted to him: for at times he is present as though not yet asked, and comes before her, and arrives with all speed as if leaping, to show his charity and loving-kindness; at times he as it were hides and withdraws himself, lest the soul be lifted up by an unbroken run of spiritual prosperity, or ascribe to herself what is God's, but that she may mark her own weakness and humble herself, and by sighing, praying and labouring for the increase of grace may win it more abundantly.

paras.t: Anima igitur spirituali alacritate ac gaudio ad tempus privata, precatur : Veniat dilectus meus in hortum meum, id est in superiorem partem meam, in qua summæ Trinitatis resplendet imago : hoc est, intellectum meum radio sapientiæ suæ illustret, contemplationis luce perfundat totum, totumque rapiat in se ipsum, et stabiliat in divinis ; voluntatem quoque ab omni purget malitia, inordinato affectu, improboque amore sui ipsius privato, et in summi boni amore accendat, conservet, perficiat ; sed et memoriam a suis distractionibus recolligat, et confortet semper in se. Veni igitur, o dilecte, et totum hortum hunc meum occupa, posside, ac jugiter immorare : dignare eum, o fons totius fecunditatis, incessabiliter irrigare, purgare, fecundare, circumummunire, omnique flore ac fructu gratiæ ac virtutum, donorum ac beatitudinum adimplere. Hoc oro, ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum, id est, mecum cœnet, et actus meos pie acceptet, quamvis imperfecti sint nimis, præstetque mihi eos tam humiliter exercere, et eorum defectuositatem tam contrite deflere, quod delectetur in eis. Etenim ejus poma, sunt virtutes et dona mihi ab eo collata, quorum fructus, est actio eorum virtuosa, seu delectatio bona actioni annexa.
paras.en: The soul, then, deprived for a time of spiritual eagerness and joy, prays: [[5:1|Let my beloved come into|Veniat dilectus meus in]] my garden [the soul says here *my garden*, where the verse has *his*], that is, into my higher part, in which the image of the most high Trinity shines: that is, let him enlighten my understanding with the ray of his wisdom, flood it wholly with the light of contemplation, carry it wholly away into himself, and settle it firmly in divine things; let him also cleanse my will from all malice, from disordered affection and from its wicked private love of itself, and kindle it in the love of the highest good, keep it and perfect it; and let him also gather my memory back from its distractions, and strengthen it ever in himself. Come, then, O beloved, and occupy this whole garden of mine, possess it, and dwell in it continually: deign, O fountain of all fruitfulness, to water it unceasingly, to cleanse it, to make it fruitful, to wall it round about, and to fill it with every flower and fruit of grace and virtues, of gifts and beatitudes. This I pray, that he may [[5:1|eat the fruit of his apple trees|comedat fructum pomorum suorum]], that is, may sup with me, and kindly accept my acts, though they be all too imperfect, and grant me to perform them so humbly, and to bewail their defectiveness [the print reads *defructuositatem*, 'fruitlessness'; the margin corrects it to *defectuositatem*, 'defectiveness', which is followed here as fitting 'imperfect' just before] so contritely, that he may take delight in them. For his apples are the virtues and gifts bestowed on me by him, and their fruit is the virtuous exercise of them, or the good delight joined to the act.

paras.t: Ad hanc petitionem, quasi absenti factam, sponsus ubique præsens et omnia audiens, sponsæ particulari respondet : Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa. Tanquam dicat dignantissimus ac munificentissimus sponsus : Tu, o anima amorosa, invitas me ad introeundum hortum tuum ut vescar tecum ; sed ego vice versa invito te ut intres hortum meum, reficiarisque mecum : quia melius habeo præparatum ad comedendum, quam tu, quia in me sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ atque scientiæ, in me omnium bonorum et pulchrorum ac desiderabilium perfecta et superdives possessio, in me status omnium bonorum aggregatione perfectus. Veni ergo in hortum meum, nec verearis aut verecunderis : non enim ancillam, sed sororem et sponsam te voco. Veni, non corporis gressu, sed spirituali profectu, consideratione intimoque affectu, in hortum meum, id est in cor meum, in deitatis meæ floridissimam amœnitatem, in plenitudinem gratiarum animæ meæ desuper præstitarum, in opulentiam deliciosissimam meritorum meorum.
paras.en: To this petition, made as if to one absent, the Bridegroom, who is present everywhere and hears all things, answers his particular bride: [[5:1|I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse|Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa]] [Denis takes *Veni* as a command, 'Come into my garden', where the Douay-Rheims reads 'I am come'; so in what follows]. As if the most condescending and most bountiful Bridegroom were to say: Thou, O loving soul, invitest me to enter thy garden that I may feed with thee; but I in turn invite thee to enter my garden and be refreshed with me: for I have better things prepared to eat than thou hast, since in me are [[Col 2:3|all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge|omnes thesauri sapientiæ atque scientiæ]], in me is the perfect and superabundant possession of all things good and beautiful and desirable, in me is the state made perfect by the gathering together of all goods [Boethius' definition of beatitude]. Come, then, into my garden, and do not fear or be abashed: for I call thee not handmaid, but sister and spouse. Come, not with the steps of the body, but by spiritual progress, by consideration and inward affection, into my garden, that is, into my heart, into the most flowery delightfulness of my Godhead, into the fulness of the graces bestowed from above upon my soul, into the most delicious wealth of my merits.

paras.t: Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis : id est, totius vitæ meæ laboriosæ et dolorosæ in sæculo isto ac acerbissimæ passionis merita, quasi in unum collegi ac colligavi fasciculum, ut tibi ex eo communicem, et refectionem exuberantem impendam. Comedite ergo ex spiritualibus alimoniis, donis ac meritis meis, o amici, id est, spiritus rationales, quorum cibus est contemplatio veritatis, dilectio bonitatis, consolatio spiritualis interiorque profectus, sacra communio, gratiæ ac virtutum infusio et augmentum. Et bibite ex fontibus Salvatoris, ex torrente deificæ voluptatis, ex fontali sapientia Creatoris ; et inebriamini, carissimi. Ego enim abundantia pietatis meæ excedo preces votaque supplicum, et ad dandum paratissimus sum, dummodo obicem non ponatis. Imo frequenter tam liberalissime præsto, infundo, et visito animas præelectas, ut totum capere non valentes, clamare cogantur ac dicere, O Domine, contine undas gratiæ tuæ; defluantque a se ipsis, et sui ipsorum obliti, transferantur ac transformentur omnino in me, corpore soporato, sensibusque sopitis, et parte sensitiva a suis actibus ad tempus suspensa. Accedite ergo ad me fontem luminis ac totius sapientiæ salutaris, et illuminamini. Accedite ad me fontem amoris immensi, et accendimini. Accedite ad me omnipotentem, ut confortemini. Accedite ad me indeficienter opulentissimum, ut ditetur cor vestrum. Accedite ad me interminabiliter misericordissimum, ut misericordiam consequamini consummatam.
paras.en: [[5:1|I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices|Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis]]: that is, the merits of my whole life, laborious and sorrowful in this world, and of my most bitter passion, I have as it were gathered and bound into one bundle, to share it with thee and to bestow on thee an overflowing refreshment. Therefore [[5:1|eat|Comedite]] of my spiritual nourishments, gifts and merits, [[5:1|O friends|o amici]], that is, rational spirits, whose food is the contemplation of truth, the love of goodness, spiritual consolation and inward progress, holy communion, the infusion and increase of grace and virtues; [[5:1|and drink|Et bibite]] [[Is 12:3|out of the saviour's fountains|ex fontibus Salvatoris]], from the torrent of divine pleasure[[Ps 35:9||]], from the fountain-wisdom of the Creator; [[5:1|and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|et inebriamini, carissimi]]. For in the abundance of my loving-kindness I go beyond the prayers and wishes of suppliants, and I am most ready to give, provided you put no obstacle. Nay, I often bestow, pour in and visit chosen souls so very liberally that, unable to hold the whole, they are compelled to cry out and say: O Lord, hold back the waves of thy grace; and they flow out of themselves, and, forgetting themselves, are carried over and wholly transformed into me, the body lulled to sleep, the senses stilled, and the sensitive part suspended for a time from its acts. [[Ps 33:6|Come ye|Accedite ergo]], then, to me, the fountain of light and of all saving wisdom, [[Ps 33:6|and be enlightened|et illuminamini]]. Come to me, the fountain of boundless love, and be kindled. Come to me, the almighty, that you may be strengthened. Come to me, who am unfailingly most rich, that your heart may be enriched. Come to me, who am endlessly most merciful, that you may obtain mercy made perfect.

paras.t: Ego, o sponsa mea, dormio, in Deo patre invariabiliter quiescendo; sed cor meum vigilat, nunquam immemor tui, sed tibi semper intentum, et ad auxiliandum tibi paratum. Idcirco et tu sic dormias, ut vigiles mente; tam devote ac sobrie vivas, tam ardenter te occupa jugiter in divinis, ut corpore dormiente, et te cum illo ab exterioribus repausante, vigiles corde, ut in somno, in visione nocturna appaream tibi, loquensque tecum, te instruam de secretis atque salubribus ; sed et in somno quasi in vigilia psallas, ores, et mediteris ex assidua talium consuetudine actuum, quatenus semper parata vocem meam audire, dicere queas : Vox dilecti mei pulsantis ac dicentis : Aperi mihi, soror. Invitasti quippe me sicut et ego te; verum te tardante paulisper venire in hortum meum, mox veni ad te, et verbis affectuosissimis atque dulcissimis te invito, ut me nunc suscipias hospitem ultra se offerentem ad ingrediendum, quem paulo ante rogasti venire. Itaque aperi mihi januam mentis tuæ, soror mea, quia mihi cohæres, amica mea, quæ non servili, sed filiali servis timore ac caritate, columba mea, quæ ad me dumtaxat tuum moves adspectum, immaculata mea, quia in sanctitate et justitia mihi obsequeris ; quia caput meum plenum est rore, id est, de rore cœli, de benedictione cœlesti, tibi communicare paratus sum.
paras.en: [[5:2|I|Ego]], O my spouse, [[5:2|sleep|dormio]], resting unchangeably in God the Father; but [[5:2|my heart watcheth|cor meum vigilat]], never unmindful of thee, but ever intent on thee and ready to help thee. Therefore do thou also so sleep that thou watch in mind; live so devoutly and soberly, busy thyself so ardently and continually with divine things, that while thy body sleeps, and thou with it art at rest from outward things, thou mayest watch in heart, so that in sleep, [[Job 33:15|in a vision by night|in visione nocturna]], I may appear to thee, and speaking with thee instruct thee in secret and wholesome things; and that even in sleep, as when awake, thou mayest sing psalms, pray and meditate, from the constant habit of such acts; so that, ever ready to hear my voice, thou canst say: [[5:2|the voice of my beloved knocking|Vox dilecti mei pulsantis]], and saying: [[5:2|Open to me, my sister|Aperi mihi, soror]]. For thou didst invite me, as I did thee; but since thou wert slow for a while to come into my garden, I soon came to thee, and with most loving and sweetest words I invite thee to receive me now as a guest who of his own accord offers to come in, whom a little before thou didst ask to come. Open to me, therefore, the door of thy mind, [[5:2|my sister|soror mea]], for thou art co-heir with me; [[5:2|my love|amica mea]], who servest with no servile but with filial fear and charity; [[5:2|my dove|columba mea]], who turnest thy gaze to me alone; [[5:2|my undefiled|immaculata mea]], for thou servest me in holiness and justice; [[5:2|for my head is full of dew|quia caput meum plenum est rore]], that is, I am ready to share with thee of the dew of heaven, of the heavenly blessing.

paras.t: Ad hoc anima virtuosa respondet : Exspoliavi me tunica mea : id est, absit a me aliter agere, quam tu, o sponse, hortaris : nam exui veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et omni inobedientiæ et transgressioni renuntiavi, et renuntiare semper propono : ideo præsto sum obedire. Lavi pedes meos, id est, affectus meos ab omni rebellione et carnalitate interiorique fornicatione, per contritionem, confessionem, satisfactionem purgavi ; quomodo inquinabo illos ? id est, nequaquam decet nec fas est recidivare. Ideo volo tibi jugiter aperire ac obedire, ne priori remissioni ingrata inveniar. Nam et vulnera repetita, sunt graviora ; et servo ingrato dimissa debita, rursus imposita sunt et ab eo exacta.
paras.en: To this the virtuous soul answers: [[5:3|I have put off my garment|Exspoliavi me tunica mea]]: that is, far be it from me to do otherwise than thou, O Bridegroom, urgest: for I have put off [[Col 3:9|the old man with his deeds|veterem hominem cum actibus suis]][[Eph 4:22||]], and have renounced all disobedience and transgression, and purpose ever to renounce them; therefore I am ready to obey. [[5:3|I have washed my feet|Lavi pedes meos]], that is, I have cleansed my affections from all rebellion and carnality and inward fornication, by contrition, confession and satisfaction; [[5:3|how shall I defile them?|quomodo inquinabo illos ?]] that is, it is by no means fitting nor lawful to fall back. Therefore I will open to thee and obey thee continually, lest I be found ungrateful for the former pardon. For wounds reopened are the more grievous; and the debts forgiven the ungrateful servant were laid on him again and exacted of him[[Matt 18:32||]][[Matt 18:34||]].

paras.t: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, id est, secreta visitatione me tetigit, vel paternaliter castigando peccantem, aut validius inflammando paratam, adjiciens gratiam super gratiam : quia habenti datur, et bonæ ac fervidæ voluntati pax interna augetur, profectus conceditur, effectus præstatur. Hinc orat Propheta : Emitte manum tuam de alto. Et Jeremias fatetur : Misit Dominus manum suam, et tetigit os meum. Hoc foramen est vena divini susurrii tam secreta, ut sanctus Job protestetur : Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum ; et si abierit, non intelligam. Et ipsemet sponsus : Spiritus, inquit, ubi vult spirat ; et vocem ejus audis, et nescis unde veniat aut quo vadat. Denique Deus visitat, hortatur, inflammatque animam modis duobus. Primo, per apparitionem quamdam imaginariam aut allocutionem sensibilem, quantum ad exteriorem interioremve sensum. Quumque sic mittit manum suam per foramen, potest ipsum foramen intelligi alicujus sensus apertio, vel ipsa imaginaria visio seu allocutio. Secundo, per anagogicam seu pure intellectualem illuminationem seu allocutionem : et hæc ipsa illuminatio seu allocutio, vel intellectus advertentia sive apertio, potest vocari foramen, per quod virtus seu pietas sponsi se mittit, tangitque sponsam.
paras.en: [[5:4|My beloved put his hand through the key hole|Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen]], that is, he touched me by a secret visitation, either chastising me as a father when I sinned, or inflaming me more strongly when I was ready, adding grace upon grace: for [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given|habenti datur]], and to a good and fervent will inward peace is increased, progress granted, effect bestowed. Hence the Prophet prays: [[Ps 143:7|Put forth thy hand from on high|Emitte manum tuam de alto]]. And Jeremias confesses: [[Jer 1:9|the Lord put forth his hand, and touched my mouth|Misit Dominus manum suam, et tetigit os meum]]. This key hole [*foramen*, any opening] is a vein of divine whispering so secret that holy Job declares: [[Job 9:11|If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart, I shall not understand|Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum ; et si abierit, non intelligam]]. And the Bridegroom himself: [[John 3:8|The Spirit|Spiritus]], he says, [[John 3:8|breatheth where he will and thou hearest his voice: but thou knowest not whence he cometh and whither he goeth|ubi vult spirat ; et vocem ejus audis, et nescis unde veniat aut quo vadat]]. Lastly, God visits, exhorts and inflames the soul in two ways. First, by some imaginary apparition or sensible speech, to the outward or the inward sense [*imaginary*, that is, presented to the imagination in images, not unreal]. And when he thus puts his hand through the key hole, the key hole itself may be understood as the opening of some sense, or the imaginary vision or speech itself. Secondly, by an anagogical or purely intellectual illumination or speech: and this illumination or speech itself, or the attention or opening of the understanding, may be called the key hole through which the power or loving-kindness of the Bridegroom sends itself and touches the bride.

paras.t: Et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus. Anagogicos etenim motus, et spirituales attactus mentis a Deo, excessivasque illustrationes, atque flammigeras sancti amoris inflammationes et visitationes divinas concomitatur grandis alteratio corporis, debilitatio virium, distemperatio harmoniæ ex redundantia superioris partis in inferiorem. Propter quod locutus est Isaias : Venter meus ad Moab quasi cithara sonabit. Joannes quoque : Amaricatus est, inquit, venter meus (ex imaginaria videlicet comestione voluminis). Unde et Daniel dixit : Langui post visionem. Verumtamen in hoc loco mens per ventrem potest intelligi, et per ventris tremorem, reverentialis ac formidolosa admiratio majestatis ipsius sponsi, ut sit sensus : Venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus, id est, ex illuminatione et inflammatione divinæ potestatis in me facta, mens mea cum reverentia et filiali pavore admirata est immensitatem majestatis divinæ, atque interminabilem plenitudinem perfectionis ac gloriæ ejus. Hinc Seraphim ac Cherubim dicuntur Deo cum reverentia et metu adsistere.
paras.en: [[5:4|and my bowels were moved at his touch|Et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus]]. For anagogical movements, and spiritual touchings of the mind by God, and overwhelming illuminations, and the flaming kindlings of holy love and the divine visitations, are accompanied by a great alteration of the body, a weakening of its powers, an upsetting of its balance [*distemperatio harmoniæ*: the even tempering of the body is disturbed], from the overflow of the higher part into the lower. Wherefore Isaias said: [[Is 16:11|my bowels shall sound like a harp for Moab|Venter meus ad Moab quasi cithara sonabit]]. John too: [[Apoc 10:10|was bitter|Amaricatus est]], he says, [[Apoc 10:10|my belly|venter meus]] (that is, from the imaginary eating of the book). And so Daniel also said: I [[Dan 8:27|languished|Langui]] after the vision. Yet in this place the mind may be understood by the belly [*venter*, which the Douay-Rheims renders 'bowels'], and by the trembling of the belly a reverential and fearful wonder at the majesty of the Bridegroom himself, so that the sense is: [[5:4|my bowels were moved at his touch|Venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus]], that is, from the illumination and inflaming of the divine power wrought in me, my mind with reverence and filial dread wondered at the immensity of the divine majesty and the boundless fulness of his perfection and glory. Hence the Seraphim and Cherubim are said to stand before God with reverence and fear.

paras.t: Surrexi, ut aperirem dilecto meo : id est, ad amorosiorem ejus amplexum, ad validiorem suæ bonitatis affectum, ad clariorem suæ sapientiæ contemplationem me præparavi ac adspiravi. Siquidem quanto quis amplius crescit, et quanto plus divinæ gustum dulcedinis experitur, quanto increatam Creatoris pulchritudinem limpidius cœperit intueri : tanto ferventius ad profectum in omnibus istis, et ad beatificam fruitionem, et ad facialem adspectum afficitur et anhelat, cum Apostolo loquens : Ego non arbitror me apprehendisse : et rursus, Quæ priora sunt obliviscens, in anteriora extendo me ipsum. Hinc profectus profectibus deservire dicuntur, et merita ex meritis oriuntur. Et sicut unum peccatum pondere suo trahit ad aliud ; sic una actio virtuosa expedit, disponit, ac trahit ad aliam, quousque habitus bonus seu consuetudo in anima generetur : per quam ipsa facillime ac jucunde, quæ bona sunt, operetur.
paras.en: [[5:5|I arose up to open to my beloved|Surrexi, ut aperirem dilecto meo]]: that is, I prepared myself and aspired to his more loving embrace, to a stronger affection for his goodness, to a clearer contemplation of his wisdom. For the more one grows, and the more one tastes the divine sweetness, and the more clearly one has begun to gaze on the uncreated beauty of the Creator, the more fervently is one moved and does one pant for progress in all these things, and for the beatific fruition, and for the sight face to face, saying with the Apostle: [[Phil 3:13|I do not count myself to have apprehended|Ego non arbitror me apprehendisse]]; and again: [[Phil 3:13|Forgetting the things that are behind and stretching forth myself to those that are before|Quæ priora sunt obliviscens, in anteriora extendo me ipsum]] [Denis's wording, *quæ priora sunt obliviscens, in anteriora extendo me ipsum*, differs a little from the Vulgate's]. Hence progress is said to serve progress, and merits arise from merits. And as one sin by its own weight draws to another [a saying of Gregory the Great], so one virtuous act makes ready, disposes and draws to another, until a good habit or custom is formed in the soul, by which she does what is good most easily and gladly.

paras.t: Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham : id est, ex gratiosa Dei visitatione præfata processi mox copiose ad bona opera, ad corporis edomationem, ad crucifixionem carnis et vitiorum concupiscentiarumque ejus : sicut hortatus est Paulus, Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram. Digiti mei pleni sunt myrrha probatissima : id est, per discretionem et rectam intentionem, ac vitæ meæ examinationem, castigavi corpus meum et in servitutem redegi, amore imitationis Christi : cujus etiam intuitu et amore abnegavi me ipsum, et mentem meam jugo obedientiæ plene subjeci, sicut ipse propter me factus est obediens Patri usque ad crucis patibulum. Etenim qui se dicit in Christo manere, et qui vere ab ipso Christianus vocatur, debet instar illius ambulare, suæque passionis sequi vestigia. De spirituali autem significatione digitorum, et de optima myrrha et myrrhæ designatione, dictum est articulo præcedenti.
paras.en: [[5:5|my hands dropped with myrrh|Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham]]: that is, from the gracious visitation of God spoken of above, I went forth at once and abundantly to good works, to the taming of the body, to the crucifying of the flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]]: as Paul exhorted: [[Col 3:5|Mortify|Mortificate]] [[Col 3:5|your members which are upon the earth|membra vestra quæ sunt super terram]]. [[5:5|my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh|Digiti mei pleni sunt myrrha probatissima]]: that is, through discretion and right intention, and the examination of my life, [[1 Cor 9:27|I chastise my body and bring it into subjection|castigavi corpus meum et in servitutem redegi]] [Denis puts the Apostle's words in the past: *I have chastised*], for love of the imitation of Christ: in regard and love of whom I have also denied myself, and fully submitted my mind to the yoke of obedience, as he for my sake became obedient to the Father even to the gibbet of the cross[[Phil 2:8||]]. For he who says he abides in Christ, and who is truly called a Christian after him, ought to walk as he walked[[1 John 2:6||]], and to follow the footsteps of his passion. Of the spiritual meaning of the fingers, and of the best myrrh and what myrrh signifies, we have spoken in the preceding article.

paras.t: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo, id est, aditum cordis mei plene atque totaliter ei aperui : non solum repagula, vectes et ostia, sed pessulum quoque a thalamo cordis mei removi, non tantum vitando peccata graviora, sed etiam leviora, et quidquid gratiam vultus sponsi potest offendere. Quemadmodum enim cæcutiens domum ingrediens, non nisi magna, ut scamnum, tripodem et consimilia videt, in alia vero minora impingit; qui autem visus acumine mediocriter viget, etiam parva videt ; qui autem acutissimi visus est, videt et minima, imo et atomos, præsertim sole splendente in radiis ejus : sic pusilli, imperfecti et incipientes, modice illustrati, non nisi mortalia vitia ponderant et vitare nituntur, propter quod frequenter incidunt in ea, quoniam venialia sunt via ac dispositio ad peccata mortalia ; proficientes vero, notabiliter illustrati, venialia quoque, præsertim grossiora, abhorrent et evitare conantur. Porro perfecti, radio Solis æterni fulgurosæ perfusi, etiam minima venialia acute perpendunt, vehementer detestantur, et cum jugi custodia ac consideratione assidua divinæ præsentiæ effugere satagunt; quæ inciderunt, amarissime deflent, tanquam mortalia, incessanter solliciti pro cordis sui custodia ac puritate interna. Hi pessulum ostii sui reserant sponso, omnemque mentis aditum claudunt infernali adultero.
paras.en: [[5:6|I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved|Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo]], that is, I opened the entrance of my heart to him fully and wholly: I removed from the chamber of my heart not only the barriers, bars and doors, but the bolt as well, avoiding not only the graver sins but the lighter ones too, and whatever can offend the favour of the Bridegroom's countenance. For as a dim-sighted man entering a house sees only large things, such as a bench, a tripod and the like, but stumbles against others that are smaller; while one whose sight is of middling sharpness sees small things too; and one of the keenest sight sees even the least, nay even the motes, especially when the sun shines, in its rays: so the little ones, the imperfect and beginners, being but moderately enlightened, weigh and strive to avoid only mortal vices, and for this reason often fall into them, since venial sins are the way and disposition to mortal sins; but the proficient [beginners, proficient and perfect: the three stages of the spiritual life], being notably enlightened, abhor and try to avoid venial sins too, especially the grosser ones. The perfect, again, flooded with the flashing ray of the eternal Sun, keenly weigh even the least venial sins, vehemently detest them, and strive to flee them by continual watchfulness and constant consideration of the divine presence; those into which they have fallen they bewail most bitterly, as though they were mortal, unceasingly anxious for the guarding of their heart and for inward purity. These unbolt their door to the Bridegroom, and shut every entrance of the mind to the hellish adulterer.

paras.t: At ille declinaverat atque transierat. Quanto perfectius et virtuosius disponit se homo ad caritatem et gratiam, sapientiam ac virtutes, tanto plenius desuper ea sortitur, dummodo in inquisitione hujusmodi perseveret ; et quamvis perseverando inveniat atque proficiat, non tamen semper invenit juxta votum, hoc est quantum ad eos caritatis, sapientiæ et virtutum effectus, quos appetit valde, utpote quoad alacritatem, consolationem, gustum, affluentiamque sensibilem. Et quantum ad hæc, dicitur sponsus declinare ac pertransire, et magis ad latus secedere, quam recedere : siquidem ex una parte incitat animam ad quærendum, et ex alia parte differt ac protrahit eam. Hinc in tali eventu oportet animam patientem manere, atque in fide et spe sine omni hæsitatione inquirere : ita ut dicat, Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo : certa quam verissime dicat Psalmista Deo, Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine.
paras.en: [[5:6|but he had turned aside, and was gone|At ille declinaverat atque transierat]]. The more perfectly and virtuously [the margin gives the variant *affectuosius*, 'lovingly', for *virtuosius*] a man disposes himself for charity and grace, wisdom and the virtues, the more fully does he receive them from above, provided he perseveres in such seeking; and though by persevering he finds and makes progress, yet he does not always find as he wishes, that is, as to those effects of charity, wisdom and the virtues which he greatly desires, namely eagerness, consolation, relish and sensible abundance. And as to these the Bridegroom is said to turn aside and pass on, and rather to step to one side than to go away: for on the one hand he stirs the soul to seek, and on the other he puts her off and keeps her waiting. Hence in such a case the soul must remain patient, and seek in faith and hope without any hesitation, so as to say: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]]; being most certain that the Psalmist says truly to God: [[Ps 9:11|let them trust in thee who know thy name: for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, O Lord|Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine]].

paras.t: Anima mea liquefacta est, ut dilectus locutus est. Dulcissime enim sonant in auribus meis ejus eloquia, ejus præconia, et quidquid spectat ad eum inflammat me. Quæsivi, et non inveni illum ad votum, seu juxta desiderium meum : sicut expositum est. Vocavi, et non respondit mihi. Semel enim loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit : quoniam in Scripturis dat sapientialia documenta, ex quibus possunt elici et haberi responsa ad omnia : ideo non oportet ut singulis singillatim respondeat. Juxta hunc modum sanctus Job loquitur Deo : Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me; mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi.
paras.en: [[5:6|My soul melted|Anima mea liquefacta est]] [[5:6|when he spoke|ut dilectus locutus est]] [Denis reads *ut dilectus locutus est*, 'when my beloved spoke']. For his words and his praises sound most sweetly in my ears, and whatever concerns him inflames me. [[5:6|I sought him, and found him not|Quæsivi, et non inveni illum]] as I wished, or according to my desire, as has been explained. [[5:6|I called, and he did not answer me|Vocavi, et non respondit mihi]]. For [[Job 33:14|God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time|Semel enim loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit]]: since in the Scriptures he gives teachings of wisdom, from which answers to all things can be drawn and had; and so there is no need for him to answer each one singly. In this manner holy Job speaks to God: [[Job 30:20|I cry to thee, and thou hearest me not: I stand up, and thou dost not regard me|Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me]]; [[Job 30:21|Thou art changed to be cruel toward me, and in the hardness of thy hand thou art against me|mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi]].

paras.t: Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem; percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me. Custodes isti, sunt angeli sancti, virtuosi prælati, prædicatores idonei : qui animam sponsum anxie exquirentem inveniunt, corripiunt, accendunt, et jaculo perforant caritatis, suisque hortamentis amorem sic incendunt in anima, ut langueat diligendo. Tulerunt mihi pallium meum. Dum anima per imaginarias considerationes et per sensibilium inspectionem sponsum inquirens, illuminatur ab angelis aut eruditis et virtuosis hominibus, qualiter sponsum quærat ex immaterialium et spiritualium rerum speculatione, et per fidem rationibus credendorum imbutam cum illuminatæ mentis intelligentia, atque per sapientiæ donum, et per supernaturales effectus, aut juxta profundiora dogmata sacræ Scripturæ : tunc salubriter auferetur animæ tali pallium suum, et pallio subtiliori induitur ac ornatur.
paras.en: [[5:7|The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me: and wounded me|Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem; percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me]]. These keepers are the holy angels, virtuous prelates, fit preachers: who find the soul anxiously seeking the Bridegroom, rebuke her, kindle her, and pierce her with the dart of charity, and by their exhortations so set love alight in the soul that she languishes with loving. [[5:7|took away my veil from me|Tulerunt mihi pallium meum]] [*pallium*, a cloak or mantle]. When the soul, seeking the Bridegroom through imaginative considerations and by looking upon sensible things, is enlightened by angels or by learned and virtuous men as to how she should seek the Bridegroom from the contemplation of immaterial and spiritual things, and through faith imbued with the reasons for what is to be believed, together with the understanding of an enlightened mind, and through the gift of wisdom, and through supernatural effects, or according to the deeper teachings of holy Scripture: then her mantle is taken from such a soul to her profit, and she is clothed and adorned with a finer mantle.

paras.t: Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, id est, o animæ virtuosæ, Christi sponsæ, si invenéritis dilectum meum, ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo. Ecce quomodo amor præfervidus modum ignorat, ruborem excludit, et quasi præcipitem facit. Quum enim Christus sit omnium fidelium atque ferventium sponsus et dilectus animarum, quælibet tamen hujusmodi anima loquitur sic de eo, quasi sit solum suus dilectus : Si invenéritis, inquiens, dilectum meum. Sic sancti viri Deo omnium dicere consueverunt : Deus meus. Porro divinus et magnus Dionysius, in suis interdum voluminibus ait : Deus, et (si fas est dicere) meus. Nempe, quo quis aliquid intentius amat, eo amplius sibi illud appropriat : non alios excludendo, sed illud tanquam sui solius sit, diligendo.
paras.en: [[5:8|I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem|Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, O virtuous souls, brides of Christ, [[5:8|if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love|si invenéritis dilectum meum, ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo]]. See how love that is very fervent knows no measure, shuts out shame, and makes one as it were headlong. For though Christ is the Bridegroom of all the faithful and fervent, and the beloved of souls, yet every such soul speaks of him thus, as if he were her beloved alone: [[5:8|if you find|Si invenéritis]], she says, [[5:8|my beloved|dilectum meum]]. So holy men have been wont to say to the God of all: My God. And the divine and great Dionysius at times says in his books: God, and (if it be lawful to say so) mine. For the more intently one loves something, the more one makes it one's own: not by shutting others out, but by loving it as though it were one's own alone.

paras.t: Si ergo invenéritis dilectum per devotionem optatam; ut annuntietis ei, qui me non exaudit ad votum, quatenus vestra oratione me audiat, compatiaturque mihi : et si non mereor, tamen quia amore langueo, non puræ alicujus creaturæ aut rei variabilis et caducæ, sed ejus solius (et ipse qui totius puri amoris magister est, optime novit quam gravis et afflictivus sit languor amoris, quam molesta sit ei optata amici absentia), ideo exorate viscera misericordiæ ejus, quatenus suæ gratiosæ præsentiæ copiam concupitam mihi miseræ et infirmæ sine ampliori dilatione exhibere dignetur.
paras.en: If, then, [[5:8|you find|invenéritis]] [[5:8|my beloved|dilectum]] through the devotion you long for, [[5:8|that you tell him|ut annuntietis ei]], who does not hear me as I wish, that he may hear me through your prayer and have compassion on me: and though I do not deserve it, yet [[5:8|that I languish with love|quia amore langueo]], not for any mere creature or changeable and perishable thing, but for him alone (and he who is the master of all pure love knows full well how heavy and afflicting is the languor of love, how grievous to the lover is the absence of the friend he longs for); therefore entreat the bowels of his mercy, that he may deign to grant me, wretched and weak as I am, the longed-for fulness of his gracious presence without further delay.

paras.t: Denique huic tam fervidæ amatrici, sponsæ, animæ amorosæ, ei morem gerentes, respondent : Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum, id est, o anima valde pulchra inter sponsas sponsi cœlestis? Quæ mulier appellaris, non ratione femineæ fragilitatis, sed causa præclaræ fecunditatis : quia in te actibus sanctis abundas, fructibus quoque virtutum polles; etiam alios verbis et exemplis, meritis precibusque convertis (juxta quem modum et universalis Ecclesia dicitur mulier in libro isto) : sicut scriptum est, Mulierem fortem quis inveniet?
paras.en: Lastly, humouring this so fervent lover, the bride, the loving soul, they answer her: [[5:9|What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women|Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum]], that is, O soul exceedingly fair among the brides of the heavenly Bridegroom? Thou art called a woman not by reason of womanly frailty, but because of a glorious fruitfulness [*mulier*, a woman in the sense of a wife and mother]: for in thee thou aboundest in holy acts, and art strong in the fruits of the virtues; thou convertest others too by words and examples, by merits and prayers (in which manner the universal Church also is called a woman in this book): as it is written: [[Prov 31:10|Who shall find a valiant woman?|Mulierem fortem quis inveniet?]]

paras.t: Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus. Hæc omnia usque in finem capituli non mutantur in expositione. Hoc tamen adjici potest, quod Christus præter rationes præhabitas dicitur candidus, quoniam pius, dulcis et blandus est justis, præsertim in retributione; rubicundus vero, id est terribilis, asper atque iratus reprobis et iniquis : siquidem irati rubescunt in vultu, et exardescunt.
paras.en: [[5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus]]. All these words, to the end of the chapter, are not expounded otherwise [that is, here they keep the exposition given in the preceding article]. This, however, may be added: that Christ, besides the reasons given before, is called [[5:10|white|candidus]] because he is kind, sweet and gentle to the just, especially in the reward; but [[5:10|ruddy|rubicundus]], that is, terrible, harsh and angry to the reprobate and the wicked: for the angry grow red in the face, and blaze up.

5.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM CAPITULI QUINTI CANTICI CANTICORUM, DE CHRISTO ET SPONSA SINGULARI.
5.title_en: Explanation of the same fifth chapter of the Canticle of Canticles: of Christ and the singular Bride

paras.t: Sacratissima Virgo, ex lege et Prophetis, ex illuminatione divina et annuntiatione angelica, agnoscens Unigenitum Patris incarnandum, quum ore angelico didicisset illum ex se incarnandum, atque hoc ipsum humillime ac ferventissime cupiens, dicere potuit, æquivalenterque dixit : Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, id est, in uterum meum descendat, et ex purissimis meis sanguinibus corpus assumat humanum. Felicissimæ itaque Virginis venter hortus fuit pulcherrimus, omni castitate et sobrietate decoratissimus, virginea puritate redolentissimus, ex conceptione Verbi æterni ineffabiliter dignificatus, utpote thronus veri Salomonis, thalamus sponsi cœlestis, templum veri Dei effectus, supernaturali et superexcellentissima fecunditate ornatus : quippe qui eum concepit, qui a Patre æterno æternaliter genitus est et profluxit, ac verus Deus est, universorum reparator, salvator, judex, ac Dominus. Hic uterus locus est mundissimæ voluptatis, hortus paradisiacæ amœnitatis : ex quo nobis emanavit fluvius gloriosus universam irrigans terram, flos campi pulcherrimus; fructus quoque æternæ salutis, de quo locutus est unus Sanctorum non minimus : Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum, ecce hereditas Domini, filii merces fructus ventris. Ecce in utero isto conceptus est, atque ex eo vere est natus, qui ex corde Patris in æternitate est generatus, sicut Pater ipse testatur : Ex utero ante luciferum genui te. Hunc igitur uterum universitas electorum devotissime veneretur, quem nullus nisi mundo oculo contemplatur. O quam inæstimabiliter irrigatus, fecundatus, dulcificatus est beatissimæ Virginis uterus, ex tam diuturna habitatione in eo Fontis totius boni, a quo omnis processit fecunditas, qui in se ipso infinite essentialiterque suavis est!
paras.en: The most holy Virgin, knowing from the Law and the Prophets, from divine enlightenment and from the angel's message, that the Only-begotten of the Father was to become incarnate, when she had learned from the angel's mouth that he was to become incarnate of her[[Luke 1:26||]] [the margin gives Luke i, 26–38], and longing for this very thing most humbly and most fervently, could have said, and in effect did say: [[5:1|Let my beloved come into his garden|Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum]], that is, let him come down into my womb, and take a human body of my most pure blood. And so the womb of the most blessed Virgin was a most beautiful garden, most richly adorned with all chastity and sobriety, most fragrant with virginal purity, ennobled beyond words by the conception of the eternal Word: for it became the throne of the true Solomon, the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, the temple of the true God, adorned with a supernatural and supremely excellent fruitfulness; since it conceived him who was begotten of the eternal Father from eternity and came forth from him, and is true God[[John 1:1||]], the restorer of all things, the Saviour, the Judge and the Lord. This womb is a place of the purest delight, a garden of the loveliness of paradise: from it there flowed forth for us a glorious river watering the whole earth[[Gen 2:10||]], the most beautiful flower of the field; and the fruit of eternal salvation too, of which one of the Saints, and not the least, has spoken: [[Ps 126:2|When he shall give sleep to his beloved|Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum]], [[Ps 126:3|Behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb|ecce hereditas Domini, filii merces fructus ventris]]. Behold, in that womb he was conceived, and of it he was truly born, who was begotten from the heart of the Father in eternity, as the Father himself bears witness: [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]. Let the whole company of the elect, then, most devoutly venerate this womb, which none contemplates save with a pure eye. O how beyond all reckoning was the womb of the most blessed Virgin watered, made fruitful and made sweet by so long a dwelling in it of the Fount of all good, from whom all fruitfulness has proceeded, and who in himself is infinitely and essentially sweet!

paras.t: Veniat ergo dilectus meus in hortum suum per Incarnationis mysterium, ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Quemadmodum Filius Dei in utero Virginis est conceptus, ita in eodem nutriebatur, non plane sanguine menstruali, ut ceteri, sed utique puro, tanquam pomellis dulcissimis. At vero quoniam divinissima Virgo prius concepit Dei Filium corde quam corpore, et fide quam carne, ipsa optavit ut dilectus suus veniret in hortum, id est in cor suum cum mira eminentia gratiarum, quæ in conceptione Filii Dei in ea, auctæ sunt ultra omnem narrationem. Imo quo ceteris cunctis spiritualior fuit atque ferventior, eo gratiosissimum jugiterque recentem adventum Filii Dei Patris ac sui in mentem suam, incessabiliter ferventissime concupivit. Nec dubium quin ita obtinuit, sicut subjungitur ex sponsi persona :
paras.en: [[5:1|Let my beloved come into his garden|Veniat ergo dilectus meus in hortum suum]], then, through the mystery of the Incarnation, [[5:1|and eat the fruit of his apple trees|ut comedat fructum pomorum suorum]]. As the Son of God was conceived in the Virgin's womb, so he was nourished in it, not indeed with menstrual blood, as others are, but with pure blood, as with the sweetest of little apples. But since the most godlike Virgin conceived the Son of God in her heart before her body, and by faith before the flesh, she longed that her beloved should come into his garden, that is, into her heart, with a wondrous abundance of graces, which at the conception of the Son of God were increased in her beyond all telling. Nay, the more spiritual and fervent she was than all others, the more unceasingly and fervently she desired the most gracious and ever-new coming into her mind of the Son of God the Father and her own Son. Nor is there any doubt that she obtained it, as is added next in the person of the Bridegroom:

paras.t: Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa : id est, arcana ac opulentiam mentis meæ ingredere, in me Filio tuo per contemplationem obdormi : juxta quod scriptum est, In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam. Contemplare suaviter, quam infinita sit beatitudo mentis meæ increatæ, quam ineffabilis quoque exstiterit beatitudo, perfectio, gratia mentis meæ humanæ, quæ a primo suæ creationis instante, tam clare et plene vidit, ac fruitive gustavit Deitatis naturam ac suavitatem, quam pure et plene eam pura creatura videre potest ac fruitive gustare. Has benedicti ac adorandi Filii sui beatitudines, delicias, perfectiones, optima Virgo frequenter consideravit cum gaudio; sed quando eumdem tam amarissimam mortem pensavit passurum, mœror ingens mox supervenit : qui tamen ex consideratione copiosissimi fructus passionis illius mitigabatur. Veni quoque in hortum meum, in paradisum cœlestem deliciosissimum, contemplando gaudia civium supernorum, potissime mei, Filii tui, post ascensionem illico præsidentis, et secundum utramque naturam gloriosissime residentis. Insuper hortum meum, id est militantem Ecclesiam, frequenter ingredere, statum ejus considerando, et pro ea rogando, eamque tanquam potentissima advocata tuendo ac adjuvando in omnibus.
paras.en: [[5:1|I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse|Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa]] [Denis takes *Veni* as a command, "Come"]: that is, enter into the secrets and riches of my mind; fall asleep in me, thy Son, by contemplation, according to what is written: [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest|In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam]]. Contemplate sweetly how infinite is the beatitude of my uncreated mind, and how unspeakable too has been the beatitude, the perfection and the grace of my human mind, which from the first instant of its creation saw the nature of the Godhead and tasted its sweetness in fruition as clearly and fully as a mere creature can purely and fully see it and taste it in fruition. These beatitudes, delights and perfections of her blessed and adorable Son the excellent Virgin often considered with joy; but when she thought how that same Son was to suffer so very bitter a death, great grief at once came over her, which yet was softened by the thought of the most abundant fruit of his Passion. Come also into my garden, into the most delightful paradise of heaven, by contemplating the joys of the citizens on high, and above all mine, thy Son's, who straightway after the Ascension preside there and sit in the greatest glory according to both natures. Moreover, enter often into my garden, that is, the Church militant, by considering its state, and praying for it, and as a most powerful advocate defending it and helping it in all things.

paras.t: Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis : id est, pro amaritudinibus afflictionum et passionis meæ glorificatus sum corpore, et præmium accidentale sortitus sum, manifestatusque mundo et clarificatus, sicut Patrem rogavi dicendo : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum.
paras.en: [[5:1|I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices|Messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis]]: that is, for the bitterness of my afflictions and of my Passion I have been glorified in body, and have received an accidental reward [that is, a reward added to the essential reward of seeing God, here the glory of his body and of his name], and have been made known to the world and glorified, as I asked the Father, saying: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]].

paras.t: Comedi favum meum cum melle meo, id est, de propriæ deitatis et humanitatis meæ contemplatione reficior et exsulto. Bibi vinum meum, id est, evangelicam meam doctrinam personaliter degustavi, implevi, digessi : quoniam cœpi facere et docere; cum lacte meo, id est cum propria innocentia, de qua gloriabar in Deo Patre, iniquis dicendo : Quis ex vobis arguet me de peccato? Vinum quoque Christi, fuit doctrina consiliorum ipsius, et eminentior sua instructio; lac autem, traditio præceptorum, faciliorque doctrina sua moralis. Pro quibus omnibus accepit in patria præmium accidentale, et omnium electorum hominum conversionem ad ipsum, juxta illud quod scriptum est : Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum, et voluntas Domini in manu ejus dirigetur; et denuo, Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur; itemque, Tradidit in mortem animam suam, ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia.
paras.en: [[5:1|I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey|Comedi favum meum cum melle meo]], that is, I am refreshed and exult in the contemplation of my own Godhead and of my manhood. [[5:1|I have drunk my wine|Bibi vinum meum]], that is, I have tasted my gospel teaching in my own person, fulfilled it and digested it, since I [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpi facere et docere]]; [[5:1|with my milk|cum lacte meo]], that is, with my own innocence, in which I gloried in God the Father, saying to the wicked: [[John 8:46|Which of you shall convince me of sin?|Quis ex vobis arguet me de peccato?]] Christ's wine, again, was the teaching of his counsels and his loftier instruction; his milk, the handing on of the commandments and his easier moral teaching. For all these he received in the fatherland an accidental reward, and the turning of all the elect to himself, according to what is written: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed, and the will of the Lord shall be prosperous in his hand|Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum, et voluntas Domini in manu ejus dirigetur]]; and again: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]]; and also: [[Is 53:12|he hath delivered his soul unto death|Tradidit in mortem animam suam]], [[Is 53:12|Therefore will I distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong|ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia]].

paras.t: Hinc, Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi : id est, fructu ac merito conversationis ac passionis meæ in mundo, nunc gaudete et reficiamini mecum in cœlo, et de deitatis meæ plena ac contentativa fruitione inebriemini cum sobrietate interna, ac torrente voluptatis meæ potemini cum securitate jucunda, quemadmodum vobis promisi : Ego, inquiens, dispono vobis, sicut disposuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo; et rursus, Amen dico vobis, quod faciet illos discumbere, et transiens ministrabit eis.
paras.en: Hence: [[5:1|eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi]]: that is, by the fruit and merit of my life and Passion in the world, now rejoice and be refreshed with me in heaven, and be inebriated, with an inward sobriety, by the full and satisfying fruition of my Godhead, and drink of the torrent of my pleasure in joyful security, as I promised you, saying: [[Luke 22:29|I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom|dispono vobis, sicut disposuit mihi Pater meus regnum]], [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo]]; and again: [[Luke 12:37|Amen I say to you that|Amen dico vobis, quod]] he will [[Luke 12:37|make them sit down to meat and passing will minister unto them|faciet illos discumbere, et transiens ministrabit eis]].

paras.t: Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat. Hoc præclarissima sponsa Verbi æterni, sanctissima Virgo, præeminenter dicere potuit, quia contemplativissimam vitam duxit, et ab exteriori tumultu, omnique inordinato strepitu et cura superflua atque inquietudine culpæ penitus abstinens et sopita, vigilantissima mente Deo vacavit, pro Ecclesia exoravit, actibusque virtutum in termino excellentiæ perfectissimis jugiter fuit intenta. Denique in somno corporali cor ejus pervigil fuit, et ex assidua assuefactione perfecte insistendi divinis, ex ardentissima et exercitatissima caritate, ex splendidissima et exuberantissima sapientia sibi infusa, et contemplatione in vigiliis, pene aut prorsus continue, etiam tempore somni, vigili corde fuit Deo conjuncta, et pro commissa sibi Ecclesia vigilare non cessat.
paras.en: [[5:2|I sleep, and my heart watcheth|Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat]]. This the most glorious bride of the eternal Word, the most holy Virgin, could say above all others, because she led a life wholly given to contemplation, and, keeping utterly away from, and asleep to, outward tumult, all disordered noise, needless care and the disquiet of sin, she gave herself to God with a mind most wakeful, prayed for the Church, and was ever intent on acts of virtue most perfect, at the very summit of excellence. Even in bodily sleep her heart kept watch: from her constant habit of applying herself perfectly to divine things, from her most ardent and most practised charity, from the most splendid and overflowing wisdom infused into her, and from her contemplation in her waking hours, she was joined to God with a watchful heart almost or altogether without a break, even in the time of sleep; and she does not cease to watch over the Church entrusted to her.

paras.t: Vox dilecti mei pulsantis, atque dicentis : Aperi mihi, soror mea carissima, amica mea fidelissima ac familiarissima, columba mea pudicissima, simplicissima, immaculata mea, quæ nec minimæ culpæ unquam maculam incurristi. Quia caput meum plenum est rore, id est omni cœlesti benedictione, ac omni divino charismate. Ideo de universa plenitudine gratiæ ac gloriæ meæ paratissimus sum tibi præ omnibus liberalissime et affectuosissime communicare. Hoc modo sponsus cœlestis omni hora spiritualiter pulsavit ad januam purissimæ mentis suæ virgineæ præcordialissimæ Genitricis, eamdem ad indesinentem in omni sapientia et virtute profectum excitando, monendo et inflammando. Præsertim vero in hora annuntiationis dominicæ, in ipsa collocutione Virginis atque Archangeli, Unigenitus Patris eam admonuit intus ad consentiendum, ad aperiendum, ad suscipiendum in se talentum, thesaurum, ac pretium mundi : cui pulsationi obedientissima adolescentula libenter humiliterque consensit, dicendo : Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum. Deinde sua beatissima assumptione instante, his verbis Filius ejus invitavit eam ad cœlestis paradisi ingressum : ad quem cum incomparabili dilectione et gratulatione, reverentia, apparatu, occursu et gloria eam vocavit ac introduxit.
paras.en: [[5:2|the voice of my beloved knocking|Vox dilecti mei pulsantis]], and saying: [[5:2|Open to me, my sister|Aperi mihi, soror mea]] most dear, [[5:2|my love|amica mea]] most faithful and most intimate, [[5:2|my dove|columba mea]] most chaste, most simple, [[5:2|my undefiled|immaculata mea]], who hast never incurred the stain of even the least fault; [[5:2|for my head is full of dew|Quia caput meum plenum est rore]], that is, of every heavenly blessing and every divine gift of grace. Therefore I am most ready to share with thee, before all others, most generously and most lovingly, out of the whole fullness of my grace and glory. In this way the heavenly Bridegroom knocked spiritually at every hour at the door of the most pure, virginal mind of his most dearly loved Mother, rousing, urging and kindling her to unceasing progress in all wisdom and virtue. Above all, at the hour of the Annunciation of the Lord, in the very conversation of the Virgin and the Archangel, the Only-begotten of the Father urged her inwardly to consent, to open, and to receive into herself the talent, the treasure and the price of the world; and to this knocking the most obedient young maiden gladly and humbly consented, saying: [[Luke 1:38|Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it done to me according to thy word|Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum]]. Later, when her most blessed Assumption was at hand, her Son invited her with these words to enter the paradise of heaven, to which he called her and led her in with incomparable love and rejoicing, reverence, preparation, welcome and glory.

paras.t: Præterea, quum introducta fuisset illuc in anima, et cognovisset protinus se suo dignissimo corpori reuniendam, atque cum illo rursus clarissime introducendam, admirans præ gaudio ait : Exspoliavi me tunica mea, scilicet carne mortali, quomodo induar illa? id est, qualiter denuo illam assumam? quasi dicat : Non nisi supernaturaliter ac singulari privilegio fiet hoc. Lavi pedes meos. Quemadmodum, juxta divini Dionysii documenta, angeli sancti dicuntur purgari, nequaquam ab immunditia culpæ, sed a minoratione perfectionis cognitionisque suæ; sic excellentissima Domina lavit, id est purgavit, pedes suos, puta affectus inviolabiliter mundos, a minoratione perfectionis, quia in fervore sanctorum affectuum profecit assidue. In assumptione demum sua in cœlum, corpore sacro relicto, lavit pedes suos, ad summam divinæ dilectionis eminentiam pertingendo, et spiritualium ac corporalium pedum suorum puritatem innocentiamque monstrando, tam felicissime emigrando. Quomodo inquinabo illos? quasi dicat : Nequaquam decet me unquam peccare inobedientemve esse.
paras.en: Moreover, when she had been brought in there in her soul, and knew at once that she was to be reunited to her most worthy body and to be brought in again with it in the greatest splendour, wondering for joy she said: [[5:3|I have put off my garment|Exspoliavi me tunica mea]], namely mortal flesh: [[5:3|how shall I put it on?|quomodo induar illa?]] that is, how shall I take it up again? As if to say: only supernaturally and by a singular privilege will this come about. [[5:3|I have washed my feet|Lavi pedes meos]]. As, according to the teaching of the divine Dionysius, the holy angels are said to be cleansed, not at all from the uncleanness of sin, but from a lesser degree of their perfection and knowledge [that is, they are "purged" when raised from a lesser to a fuller knowledge, not from any fault]; so the most excellent Lady washed, that is, cleansed, her feet, namely her affections, which were inviolably clean, from a lesser degree of perfection, because she advanced unceasingly in the fervour of holy affections. Lastly, in her Assumption into heaven, leaving behind her sacred body, she washed her feet, reaching the highest summit of divine love, and showing the purity and innocence of her spiritual and bodily feet by so very happy a departure. [[5:3|how shall I defile them?|Quomodo inquinabo illos?]] As if to say: it is in no way fitting that I should ever sin or be disobedient.

paras.t: Insuper, quum benedictissima Virgo audisset a Gabriele, Ecce concipies et paries filium, dicere potuit æquivalenterque protulit : Exspoliavi me tunica mea, id est, ab omni copula carnali abstinere proposui, quomodo induar illa? id est, qualiter condecens esse valebit, ut viro commiscear? tanquam dicat : Non puto decere, præsertim si regem Messiam concipiam, de quo scio prædictum, Ecce virgo concipiet et pariet filium. Tamen de modo plenius edoceri peropto : quomodo igitur fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco? Nam quamvis sponsum acceperim, firmum tamen propositum habeo nunquam conveniendi cum eo.
paras.en: Again, when the most blessed Virgin had heard from Gabriel, [[Luke 1:31|Behold thou shalt conceive|Ecce concipies]] and [[Luke 1:31|shalt bring forth a son|paries filium]], she could have said, and in effect did say: [[5:3|I have put off my garment|Exspoliavi me tunica mea]], that is, I have resolved to abstain from all carnal union: [[5:3|how shall I put it on?|quomodo induar illa?]] that is, how will it be fitting that I should be joined to a man? As if to say: I do not think it fitting, above all if I am to conceive the King Messias, of whom I know it was foretold: [[Is 7:14|Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son|Ecce virgo concipiet et pariet filium]]. Yet I greatly wish to be taught more fully of the manner: how then [[Luke 1:34|shall this be done, because I know not man?|fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco?]] For though I have taken a spouse, I have a firm purpose never to come together with him.

paras.t: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen : quia non virili semine, sed mystico spiramine, virtute Altissimi obumbrante, illum concepi. Et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus, id est, ipsum Unigenitum Patris concepi cum gaudio cordis exuberantissimo redundante in corpus meum : concepi, inquam, ad tactum ejus, id est ex spirituali et causali contactu omnipotentiæ suæ.
paras.en: [[5:4|My beloved put his hand through the key hole|Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen]]: for it was not by the seed of man but by a mystical breathing [*spiramen*, "breath" or "inspiration", answering to *semen*, "seed"], [[Luke 1:35|the power of the Most High|virtute Altissimi]] overshadowing me, that I conceived him. [[5:4|and my bowels were moved at his touch|Et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus]], that is, I conceived the Only-begotten of the Father himself with a most overflowing joy of heart that spilled over into my body: I conceived, I say, [[5:4|at his touch|ad tactum ejus]], that is, by the spiritual and causal touch of his almighty power.

paras.t: Quo concepto, Surrexi, devotissime atque humillime regratiando pro beneficio tam immenso mihi exhibito, ut aperirem dilecto meo, id est, in thalamum mentis meæ introducerem eum per ardentiorem amplexum, per gratiæ totius ineffabile incrementum, ac de cetero semper paratior essem ad omnem obedientiam sanctam, et devotissimam servitutem ipsius : tanto amplius me ipsam in cunctis humilians, quanto major fui effecta. Surrexi quoque orando pro aliis, ut meis orationibus corda illorum aperirem fidei et gratiæ Filii mei, quatenus converterentur ad ipsum, et salvarentur per ipsum. Amplius, surgens abii in montana ad cognatam meam Elisabeth, ut mentem ejus et cor infantuli ejus nondum nati, aperirem Filio meo, ita ut cognosceretur ab eis.
paras.en: Having conceived him, [[5:5|I arose up|Surrexi]], giving thanks most devoutly and most humbly for so immense a benefit shown me, [[5:5|to open to my beloved|ut aperirem dilecto meo]], that is, to bring him into the bridal chamber of my mind by a more ardent embrace, by an unspeakable increase of all grace, and to be ever readier thenceforth for all holy obedience and most devoted service of him: humbling myself in all things the more, the greater I had been made. I arose also by praying for others, to open their hearts by my prayers to the faith and grace of my Son, so that they might be converted to him and saved by him. Further, rising up, I [[Luke 1:39|went into the hill country|abii in montana]] to my kinswoman Elisabeth, to open her mind, and the heart of her little child not yet born, to my Son, so that he might be known by them.

paras.t: Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham : id est, operatio mea et conversatio fuit deinceps totaliter spiritualis, et mortificativa ac aspernativa omnis delectationis carnalis magis quam ante. Et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima : quoniam amaritudinem passionis Filii mei indesinenter tuli in corde meo cum discretione et imitatione, dilectione et regratiatione eximia; sed et proprium corpus discretissime pertractavi in exercitiis virtuosis.
paras.en: [[5:5|my hands dropped with myrrh|Manus meæ distillaverunt myrrham]]: that is, my working and my way of life were thenceforth wholly spiritual, and more than before such as to mortify and spurn all carnal delight. [[5:5|and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh|Et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima]]: for I bore the bitterness of my Son's Passion unceasingly in my heart, with discernment and imitation, with love and surpassing thankfulness; and I also handled my own body with the greatest discretion in virtuous exercises.

paras.t: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo : quoniam, juxta expositiones inductas, non solum universas, etiam minimas, culpas prorsus vitavi, sed et actus Filio meo placentissimos, coram eo incessanter cum omni fervore exercui : ita quod cor meum fuit ei jugiter reseratum, nunquam clausum. At ille declinaverat atque transierat : quia etiam nonnunquam me suam carissimam matrem permisit dire affligi, et de sua passione tristari. Corporaliter quoque interdum recessit a me : sicut dum duodecim erat annorum, et passione instante, et quando ego et fratres ejus quæsivimus eum; nec inveni eum semper ad votum in tali requisitu.
paras.en: [[5:6|I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved|Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo]]: for, according to the expositions given above, not only did I wholly avoid all faults, even the least, but I also unceasingly performed before him, with all fervour, the acts most pleasing to my Son, so that my heart was always unbarred to him and never shut. [[5:6|but he had turned aside, and was gone|At ille declinaverat atque transierat]]: for at times he allowed me too, his dearest mother, to be cruelly afflicted and to grieve over his Passion. In body also he sometimes went away from me: as when he was twelve years old[[Luke 2:42||]] [the margin gives Luke ii, 42–45], and when his Passion was at hand, and when I and his brethren sought him[[Matt 12:47||]]; and I did not always find him as I wished in such a search.

paras.t: Anima mea liquefacta est, ut dilectus locutus est : quia cum summa aviditate, devotissima affectione et ardentissimæ caritatis liquefactione, prædicationes et cetera ejus verba audivi. Potissime autem liquefacta est anima mea, quando in cruce locutus est mihi : Mulier, ecce filius tuus; et discipulo quem dilexit : Ecce mater tua.
paras.en: [[5:6|My soul melted|Anima mea liquefacta est]], [[5:6|when he spoke|ut dilectus locutus est]] [Denis reads *ut dilectus locutus est*, "when my beloved spoke"]: for with the greatest eagerness, with most devout affection and the melting of most ardent charity, I heard his preaching and his other words. But above all my soul melted when on the Cross he said to me: [[John 19:26|Woman, behold thy son|Mulier, ecce filius tuus]]; and to the disciple whom he loved: [[John 19:27|Behold thy mother|Ecce mater tua]].

paras.t: Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem, id est prælati et majores Judæorum : qui mihi amantissimum meum crudeliter abstulerunt, verbis et factis suis me gravissime afflixerunt, ita quod gladius doloris pertransivit cor meum : et pallium consolationis, qua ex Filii mei præsentia et auditu operiri solebam, verterunt mihi in desolationem extremam.
paras.en: [[5:7|The keepers that go about the city found me|Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem]], that is, the prelates and elders of the Jews, who cruelly took my most loving Son away from me, and by their words and deeds afflicted me most grievously, so that the sword of sorrow pierced my heart[[Luke 2:35||]]; and the veil [*pallium*, "cloak" or "mantle"] of consolation, with which I used to be covered by the presence of my Son and by hearing him, they turned for me into utter desolation.

paras.t: Tuncque filiabus Jerusalem dicere poteram : Adjuro vos, si inveneritis dilectum meum, a Judæis captum, ligatum, abductum, ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo, quoniam enim videre et invenire non valeo.
paras.en: And then I could say to the daughters of Jerusalem: [[5:8|I adjure you|Adjuro vos]], [[5:8|if you find my beloved|si inveneritis dilectum meum]], taken by the Jews, bound and led away, [[5:8|that you tell him that I languish with love|ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo]], since I cannot see him or find him.

paras.t: Rursus, o filiæ Jerusalem, nondum credentes, si inveneritis dilectum meum, per fidem et caritatem credendo in ipsum; ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo : id est, coram ipso devote recolite qualiter ejus amore languida fui in mundo, præsertim in passione et post ascensionem ipsius.
paras.en: Again: [[5:8|O daughters of Jerusalem|o filiæ Jerusalem]] who do not yet believe, [[5:8|if you find my beloved|si inveneritis dilectum meum]] by believing in him with faith and charity, [[5:8|that you tell him that I languish with love|ut annuntietis ei quia amore langueo]]: that is, call to mind devoutly before him how I languished with love of him in the world, above all in his Passion and after his Ascension.
